# Pushbutton Ideas

Running log of pushbutton concepts for the AnonGee toolkit, one entry per idea, newest on top.

---

## 2026-10-11 15:41 UTC

**Idea name:** Lintel Beam Batch Placer — scans every Wall in the model (or a chosen scope) for hosted Door/Window `FamilyInstance`s that have no structural beam or slab edge already sitting over them, and drops a correctly-spanned, correctly-bearing RC lintel beam at each one in a single pass, closing the one opening-related structural member every RC-frame or load-bearing-infill project needs on nearly every wall and that nothing in this toolkit, or its own two already-logged opening-adjacent ideas, has ever placed.

**Potential:** Any load-bearing or RC-frame-with-infill-wall project has a lintel over almost every door and window — the short RC beam that picks up the wall load above an opening and carries it to the jambs either side — and today it is modelled the slow, error-prone way: pick the wall, eyeball the head height, draw a beam line by hand, pick a type, repeat for every opening on every wall on every floor, often fifty-plus times on an ordinary building. Nothing in this repo touches that chore. `cad2bim/wall_plan.py` already proves the toolkit has looked straight at door/window gaps in a wall's own geometry and chosen to paper over them rather than act on them: `_COLLINEAR_BRIDGE_MM` (`wall_plan.py:29,87-88,297-298`) deliberately bridges a wall face's collinear-merge *across* "the door openings," so a wall arrives whole — the openings are read, then thrown away by design, purely so the wall outline closes. The only other place this repo has looked at an opening at all is the still-unbuilt **Opening Recoverer** idea (this log, 2026-xx), which is scoped to *placing* the Door/Window `FamilyInstance`s `cad2bim`'s own pipeline never creates — it never once proposes a lintel, and a repo grep for `OST_Doors`/`OST_Windows` across every non-vendored `.py` file returns zero hits outside that one idea write-up and test fixtures, confirming no module anywhere in `anongee_toolkit` has ever read a door or window instance to act on it. The one proven primitive this needs — placing a real structural beam on demand, not by grid intersection but by two points and an elevation offset — already exists and is already production-proven: `structural/framing.py:126`'s `create(doc, start_mm, end_mm, symbol, level, offset_mm=0.0, cutback_mm=(0.0, 0.0), disallow_joins=True)` places exactly one beam per call, at the level's elevation plus a parameter-driven offset (never a line drawn high, per its own docstring at `:130-133`), and is already the call site every grid-driven beam in this toolkit goes through. Nothing has ever pointed it at an opening's own head height instead of a grid line. On the market, the closest match found (Autodesk App Store, `WallpostWPF`) inserts generic columns and beams at wall starts/ends and at window/door openings — but it is a paid/trial Marketplace add-in, is not described as RC-code-aware (no bearing-length rule, no merge of closely-spaced openings into one span, no handoff to a stirrup/rebar engine), and nothing free on the market does this at all.

**Description:**
`Lintel Beam Placer.pushbutton`, a new sibling to `Rotate Column.pushbutton` in `Essential.panel/Action.stack/`.
1. **Scope** — Whole Model / Active View / Selection, the same three-way picker `ConvertFloor.pushbutton` and others already ship.
2. **Find hosted openings** — for each scoped `Wall`, a plain `FilteredElementCollector` filtered to `FamilyInstance`s whose `Host.Id` equals the wall's id (the exact read the already-logged Wall Reinforcement Placer idea names, at its own `script.py`-shaped step 4, as "the one genuinely new geometry read this idea needs, since nothing in the repo currently looks for a wall's hosted openings" — needed now in two places, so this tool is the one that should actually build it first).
3. **Skip what's already covered** — a bounding-box overlap test of the opening's head-height band against `OST_StructuralFraming`/`OST_StructuralColumns` in the model (the same cheap reject-first shape `JoinPriority.pushbutton/script.py:275`'s `BoundingBoxIntersectsFilter` already runs in production); an opening already sitting under a real beam or a slab edge is left alone.
4. **Merge close openings, add bearing** — openings on the same wall within a configurable clear gap are combined into one lintel span rather than two overlapping ones, generalizing `wall_plan.py`'s own `_merge_collinear` bridge-across-gap arithmetic (`:290-298`) off DXF lines onto the wall's live centerline; each span is then extended by a configurable bearing length (default code-typical 150–230 mm) each side onto the solid wall, clipped so it never overruns the wall's own ends or a neighbouring opening.
5. **Place** — one call per span straight into `framing.create()`, with `offset_mm` computed from the opening's own `Head Height` instance parameter relative to the wall's base level (no cutback — a lintel bears onto wall, not a column face), typed and marked the same house-naming convention `rc_automation/naming_sheet.py`'s pattern engine already renders for every other structural member.
6. **Preview, then apply** — one row per proposed lintel (wall, opening(s) covered, span, level, offset) in a checklist dialog before a single `Transaction` places them all, the same shape every other batch-create tool in this repo already uses.

**Implementation:** New module `anongee_toolkit/structural/lintels.py`: `hosted_openings(wall)` (the `Host.Id` filter described above), `existing_beam_at(doc, wall, opening)` (the bounding-box pre-check), `lintel_span(wall, openings, bearing_mm, gap_mm)` (pure geometry — merge-across-gap plus bearing extension, unit-testable with stub wall/opening fixtures, no live Revit needed), and `place_lintel(doc, wall, span, symbol, level)` (a thin wrapper computing `offset_mm` and calling `framing.create()` directly). New `Essential.panel/Action.stack/Lintel Beam Placer.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (scope picker + bearing/gap config + preview grid), `bundle.yaml`, `icon.png`, `lintel_config.json` mirroring `ConvertFloor.pushbutton`'s own override-by-config shape for bearing length and merge-gap tolerance. Tests: `tests/test_lintels.py` — pure-Python checks on `lintel_span()` against a wall with one opening, two close openings that should merge, and two far-apart openings that should not, using the same stub-element fixture pattern `tests/fixtures/rc_automation/` already establishes.

**Future update:**
- Hand each placed lintel straight to the already-logged Beam Reinforcement Placer's own stirrup/main-bar engine once it ships, instead of this tool ever growing its own rebar logic.
- Once the already-logged Opening Recoverer ships and starts placing Door/Window instances on `cad2bim`-built walls, this tool becomes that pipeline's own lintel step for free — no change needed here, since it already reads openings generically off `Host.Id`, not off which tool created them.
- A resync pass: if a covered opening's width or head height changes after its lintel was placed, flag the now-mismatched lintel instead of leaving a stale span behind, the same stale-detection shape the already-logged Stair Waist & Landing Rebar Host Generator's `is_shadow_stale()` already establishes for a different shadow member.

## 2026-10-11 10:40 UTC

**Idea name:** Stair Waist & Landing Rebar Host Generator — builds a hidden, sloped "shadow" structural floor under every monolithic Revit `Stairs` run and landing this toolkit places, purely so the toolkit's own rebar engine has a legal host to hang main and distribution bars on, closing the one reinforcement category `stairs.sync`'s native-stairs decision quietly made impossible to automate the day it was made.

**Potential:** `structural/stairs.py:1-13` documents, in the module's own words, why this toolkit builds RC stairs as real Revit `Stairs` rather than a beam-and-slab waist: the project owner rejected the waist-slab version outright on 2026-08-27 because "building stairs with beam and slab is management nightmare and scheduling" — a framing-member waist pollutes every Structural Framing schedule forever. That call was correct for scheduling, but it carries a cost the docstring never mentions and no later idea in this log has caught: Revit's own rebar API only hosts reinforcement on a `Floor`, a `Wall`, or a structural `FamilyInstance` — the toolkit's own research file says so in as many words, `REVIT_API_RESEARCH.md:450`, "`RebarHostData.GetRebarHostData()`... works for floors, walls and family instances alike" — and `Architecture.Stairs` is none of the three. `rebar_hosts.py:38-48`'s `is_valid_host()` wraps exactly that same `RebarHostData.GetRebarHostData(element).IsValidHost()` check the whole reinforcement pipeline (`rebar_factory.py`, every `rc_automation` rebar command) gates on before placing a single bar, and a `Stairs` element fails it every time — there is no code path from a native stair to a hosted bar anywhere in this repo, and there cannot be one without working around the host type itself. The result: every monolithic flight and landing `stairs.sync` or `cad2bim` has ever placed is, and will keep being, invisible to this toolkit's entire rebar automation — the main bars that run up a waist slab's underside and the distribution mesh across it, textbook RC detailing on every staircase ever poured, still get drawn by hand in a 2D section view, the one reinforcement category this toolkit's otherwise end-to-end rebar pipeline (columns, beams, footings, walls, slabs — every other member already logged with its own rebar-placer idea) has never touched and structurally cannot touch without a workaround. On the market this is not a feature gap any add-in fills, because it is not a modelling-effort gap, it is the same Revit API ceiling: no Revit rebar add-in, free or paid (the AGACAD/BIM Link reinforcement suites included), places bars on a native `Stairs` element either, because none of them generate a legal host for it first — they simply do not support stairs as a reinforced member and say so in their own documentation.

**Description:**
`Stair Rebar Host.pushbutton`, a new sibling inside `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack/`, next to `ConvertFloor`/`DrawFloor`.
1. **Pick stairs** — current selection, or every `Stairs` on a chosen level, reusing `structural/stairs.py:placed(doc)`'s own `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(Stairs)` scan.
2. **Read each flight and landing's geometry** — `stairs.GetStairsRuns()` for each `StairsRun`'s `GetStairsPath()` walking line and `MinRunWidth`/`StructuralDepth` (the waist, read exactly as `stairs.py:43,48` already define `RUN_WIDTH`/`WAIST`), and `stairs.GetStairsLandings()` for each landing's sketch — the same two accessors `cad2bim/builders/stairs.py:303,388`'s `StairsLanding.CreateAutomaticLanding`/`CreateSketchedLanding` calls already prove this codebase knows how to read and drive.
3. **Build the shadow floor** — per run, offset the walking line by half the run width each side to get a waist-slab outline, and call the same sloped overload `ConvertFloor.pushbutton/script.py:1272-1283`'s `create_slab()` already uses in production — `Floor.Create(doc, loops, type_id, level_id, structural=True, slope_arrow_line, slope_angle)` — with the slope angle derived from the run's own rise/run instead of a sketch's slope arrow; per landing, a flat `Floor.Create` at the landing elevation using the landing's own sketch loop.
4. **Tag it as scaffolding, not structure** — stamp a dedicated `AnonGee_RebarHostOnly` shared parameter (Yes/No) on every shadow floor the tool creates, the same stamp-and-filter idiom `rebar_factory.py:306`'s `_stamp(rebar)` already uses to mark bars this toolkit placed, and hide it from the Structural Framing/Floor schedules by a view filter rule keyed on that parameter — reusing the Filter → View Filter Generator idea's own rule-to-`ParameterFilterElement` pipeline once it ships, or a hand-built filter today — so this tool does not reopen the exact schedule-pollution problem the owner rejected the waist-slab stair over in the first place.
5. **Place the bars** — once each shadow floor passes `rebar_hosts.is_valid_host()`, hand it straight to `rebar_factory.py:466`'s `place_layer()`/`:518`'s `place_set()` exactly as any other slab host, laying main bars parallel to the walking line at bottom cover and distribution bars perpendicular at top, plus a doubled top layer across each landing-to-flight junction for the negative moment every RC detailing guide calls for there.
6. **Resync** — re-reads each shadow floor's parent `Stairs` on demand and rebuilds the sketch if riser count, run width or waist thickness has changed since it was generated, so a later edit to the stair does not leave a stale, disconnected rebar host behind.

**Implementation:** New module `anongee_toolkit/structural/stair_rebar_host.py`: `shadow_outline(stairs_run)` (walking-line offset into a `CurveLoop`, pure geometry), `create_shadow_floor(doc, stairs, run_or_landing, floor_type_id)` (wrapping `ConvertFloor`'s `create_slab()` sloped overload), `is_shadow_stale(floor, stairs)` (comparing stored run-width/waist/riser-count snapshot, the same config-and-recheck idiom `JoinPriority.pushbutton`'s `cat_order` persistence already uses elsewhere in this repo). New `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack/Stair Rebar Host.pushbutton/` (`script.py`, `ui.xaml`, `bundle.yaml`, `icon.png`), wiring straight into the existing `rebar_hosts.py`/`rebar_factory.py` pipeline for the actual bar placement step rather than duplicating it. Tests: `tests/test_stair_rebar_host.py` — pure-Python checks on `shadow_outline()` against a known straight-run rectangle and a landing square, and on `is_shadow_stale()`'s comparison logic, no live Revit document needed.

**Future update:**
- Feed each shadow floor's outline into the already-logged Rebar Cover Auditor and Lap & Starter-Bar Continuity Auditor once they ship, so stair waist/landing bars get the same cover and continuity checks every other member already gets.
- Let the already-logged Stair Landing Completer run first and hand this tool a `Stairs` whose dog-leg already has its landing in place, instead of this tool having to treat an unlanded dog-leg as two independent flights.
- Offer a "convert to Floor on delete" fallback: if the parent `Stairs` is ever deleted but the shadow floor and its bars should survive as as-built record, detach the `AnonGee_RebarHostOnly` flag and re-type the floor as a normal structural slab instead of leaving an orphaned helper element behind.

## 2026-10-11 05:41 UTC

**Idea name:** Shoring Prop Layout & Striking (De-shuttering) Schedule Generator — computes a code-spaced temporary-prop grid under every slab and beam soffit straight from the floor's own existing sketch boundary, flags every point that clashes with a column, wall or opening, and pairs it with a per-member-type, per-concrete-grade striking-date schedule, closing the one site-execution step between "the model is detailed" and "formwork can actually come down" that this toolkit's two already-logged construction-sequencing ideas both stop short of.

**Potential:** A structural BIM team details slabs and beams to the millimetre and never once models how either one is actually held up while the concrete cures — the temporary shoring (vertical props under the soffit) and the striking (de-shuttering) date that says when it is safe to pull them. Today both are guessed on site: a site engineer eyeballs a prop spacing off a rule of thumb or an old drawing, and a striking date gets tracked on a whiteboard or a separate spreadsheet nobody ties back to the model's own concrete grade or pour date — get either one wrong (props too sparse, or stripped too early) and the result is at best a re-shore scramble, at worst a collapsed or permanently sagged slab. A repo-wide grep for `shoring`, `temporary works`, `\bprop\b` and `striking`/`de-shutter` across every `.py`/`.md` in `AnonGee.extension` — and across this idea log's own 118 prior entries — returns zero hits anywhere; the closest logged idea, **Formwork & Shuttering Takeoff** (2026-09-13), stops explicitly at a contact-area quantity report (shutter-needed vs not, per face) and never proposes a support layout or a removal date, and **Pour Break Manager** (sketch-driven pour zoning/sequence numbering) governs *when concrete goes in*, never when its formwork comes back out. The toolkit already has every raw building block this needs, each proven on a different problem: `ConvertFloor.pushbutton/script.py:384` reads a `Floor`'s own `SketchId`, and `read_profile(sketch)` (`script.py:437-463`) already turns that sketch's `Profile` into closed `CurveLoop`s purely to carry a boundary across a floor-to-slab rebuild — a real, native-Revit floor-boundary reader that has never been asked for anything but that one conversion. `anongee_toolkit/cad2bim/geom/shapes.py:1402`'s `_point_in_polygon(x, y, ring)` (ray-casting) and the grid-scan it already powers at `shapes.py:864-869` inside `decompose_to_rectangles()` — stepping a regular (x, y) grid across a ring and testing each cell centre for containment — is the exact "lay a spaced grid of points inside this closed shape" operation a prop layout needs, but it lives in the CAD-import pipeline, operates on plain coordinate tuples, not Revit curves, and is private (leading underscore) with its only caller being that one rectangle-decomposition routine. `structural/levels.py:19-28`'s `levels(doc)` already returns every level's elevation in millimetres, sorted low to high — exactly what a prop's height (soffit elevation minus the level below's elevation) needs and has never been read for that purpose. `JoinPriority.pushbutton/script.py:275`'s `BoundingBoxIntersectsFilter` pattern already proves the toolkit knows how to cheaply reject candidate points that land inside a column, wall or opening before anything gets placed. `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py:103,1021,1031` already reads `BuiltInParameter.STRUCTURAL_MATERIAL_PARAM` off a structural element, but only to copy a material assignment across symbols during import — never to key a curing-time lookup table the way a concrete grade (M20/M25/OPC/PPC) should. And `Export Schedule.pushbutton/script.py:91-120`'s `_ensure_bundled_openpyxl()` already proves out the "verify AnonGee's own bundled `openpyxl`, not a stray system copy, before writing a workbook" guard this would reuse verbatim for the striking-date export. On the market, prop/shoring layout calculators exist only as static load-table PDFs from scaffold/formwork manufacturers (PERI, Doka, MEVA) with no model tie-in at all, and striking-time tracking is sold, if at all, as a line item inside large paid construction-management platforms (Procore, Fieldwire) that track it as a manual checklist entry rather than deriving it from the model's own slab thickness, level elevations and structural material — nothing free or paid reads a Revit structural model's own geometry and grade to generate either one.

**Description:**
`Shoring Prop Layout.pushbutton`, a new sibling inside `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack/`, alongside `DrawFloor`/`ConvertFloor`.
1. **Pick the slab(s) and/or beams** — current selection, or every structural `Floor`/framing instance on a chosen level, the same scope-picker shape `Parameter Combine.pushbutton` already offers.
2. **Read the soffit boundary** — for a floor, `doc.GetElement(floor.SketchId)` + the same `read_profile()` logic `ConvertFloor.pushbutton/script.py:437-463` already runs, giving closed loops and the soffit's base Z; for a beam, its own bounding box footprint stands in for v1 rather than a true per-span sketch.
3. **Lay the prop grid** — step a configurable spacing (default 1.0-1.2 m c/c, office-overridable) across each loop's bounding rectangle and keep only grid points that pass a point-in-polygon test against the loop, generalizing `cad2bim/geom/shapes.py`'s private `_point_in_polygon()`/grid-scan pattern (`:1402`, `:864-869`) into a new, public, Revit-curve-aware helper rather than reusing the CAD-only tuple version as-is.
4. **Reject clashing points** — drop any grid point whose small test bounding box overlaps a column, wall, opening or another structural member, via the same `BoundingBoxIntersectsFilter` pattern `JoinPriority.pushbutton/script.py:275` already runs, so a prop is never proposed where it cannot physically stand.
5. **Compute height and report** — each surviving point's prop height = soffit elevation − the support level's elevation, both read via `structural/levels.py:19-28`'s `levels(doc)`; a results pane lists prop count, spacing achieved, and total props per slab/beam, with a running material estimate (props + base plates) for site procurement.
6. **Report-only / Place** toggle — Report-only (default) just exports the count/positions; Place additionally drops a generic "Shoring Prop" model instance (a simple adaptive or generic-model placeholder family shipped with the tool) at each surviving point on a dedicated `Temporary Works` workset, purely for visual/4D sign-off before mobilisation, never mixed into the permanent structural model's own worksets.
7. **Striking schedule** — a second tab: per selected member, read `BuiltInParameter.STRUCTURAL_MATERIAL_PARAM` (the same read `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py:1021` already performs) to classify concrete grade, look up a minimum curing period from a configurable table keyed by member type (slab soffit / beam soffit / beam sides / column) × grade, and combine it with a modeler-entered pour date to compute and colour-flag (red if still curing, green if safe) each member's striking date; **Export** writes the schedule to Excel through the same bundled-`openpyxl` guard `Export Schedule.pushbutton/script.py:91-120` already runs.

**Implementation:** New `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack/Shoring Prop Layout.pushbutton/` (`script.py`, `ui.xaml`, `bundle.yaml`, `icon.png`, `shoring_config.json` mirroring `ConvertFloor.pushbutton/slab_convert_config.json`'s override-by-config shape for spacing, clearance tolerance and the grade→curing-days table). New module `anongee_toolkit/structural/shoring.py`: `soffit_loops(doc, floor)` (wrapping `ConvertFloor`'s `read_profile()` logic, promoted out of that one pushbutton into a shared call), `prop_grid(loops, spacing_mm)` (a new, public, millimetre/Revit-curve-aware point-in-polygon grid generator, modelled on but not reusing `cad2bim/geom/shapes.py`'s private tuple-based version), `reject_clashes(doc, points, tol_mm)` (the `BoundingBoxIntersectsFilter` pattern generalized from `JoinPriority.pushbutton/script.py:275`), and `striking_date(member_type, grade, pour_date, config)` (pure function, unit-testable with no Revit import, following `rc_automation/standards.py`'s existing no-Revit-dependency convention for code-driven lookups). Tests: `tests/test_shoring.py` covering grid generation against a known rectangle and an L-shape, clash rejection against a stub bounding box, and striking-date arithmetic across the config table's grade/member combinations.

**Future update:**
- Read pour boundaries and pour dates straight from the already-logged Pour Break Manager's own output once it ships, instead of a modeler re-typing a pour date here, so the two tools share one pour record rather than two.
- Extend `prop_grid()` to follow a sloped soffit (ramps, sloped slabs) by sampling base Z per point instead of assuming one flat `base_z` per loop.
- Feed the already-logged Formwork & Shuttering Takeoff's own per-face contact-area numbers into this tool's procurement estimate, so shutter panels and props are quoted from the same run instead of two separate exports.

## 2026-10-11 00:39 UTC

**Idea name:** Orphan View & Sheet Hygiene Sweep — finds every View, Schedule and Legend sitting in the Project Browser that is not actually placed on any sheet, plus every sheet with zero placed views, in one scan, and batch-deletes whichever the modeler ticks — closing the one everyday "this project has 400 views and nobody knows which ones matter" cleanup this toolkit has never once automated, even though three sibling tools already automate the three view-hygiene questions on either side of it.

**Potential:** Every live Revit project accumulates orphaned views continuously and by nothing more than normal daily modelling — a "Duplicate View" taken to test a dimension string, a section cut to check a detail that never made it to a sheet, a schedule copied to try a different sort order, a plan view kept "just in case" after its sheet was deleted. None of this is a modeler mistake; it is unavoidable in a project that gets touched every day for months, and it has no native warning, no Revit dialog, and nothing in this repo that ever looks for it. `anongee_toolkit/revit/views.py:36-56` (`get_eligible_views`) already proves the toolkit can enumerate the project's views cheaply — `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(View).WhereElementIsNotElementType()` filtered to `not v.IsTemplate` — but it stops at exactly six `ViewType`s (`ALLOWED_VIEW_TYPES`, line 11-18: FloorPlan/CeilingPlan/EngineeringPlan/Section/Elevation/ThreeD) because its one and only consumer, "Use this to populate a 'Select View' ComboBox" (`API.md:485`), only ever needs a picker list — it has no reason to include Schedules, Legends, Drafting Views or Sheets, and, more importantly, it never once checks whether a returned view is actually placed anywhere. A repo-wide search for `Viewport` or `GetAllPlacedViews` — the two API surfaces that answer "is this view on a sheet" — returns zero hits outside CAD test fixtures; nothing in `anongee_toolkit` has ever asked that question. The toolkit already automates view hygiene on both sides of this exact gap and has simply never been pointed at the middle: `Bulk Delete.pulldown` (`Delete FillPatterns/LinePatterns/LineStyles.pushbutton`, sharing one `script.py` keyed by a `TARGET` constant per the per-button config comment at the top of the file) already proves the whole "collect unused named items → checklist dialog → confirm → batch `Transaction.Delete`" shape works and ships three times over; `Bulk Purge` (idea, 2026 log) already proposes growing that exact pulldown past styles into View Templates/Filters/Materials; and `Sheet Issue Kit` / `Sheet Set Builder` (both already logged) assume a clean, intentional sheet set already exists before they ever run. None of them ever asks the one question that actually determines whether that sheet set is clean: how many of the views in this project are dead weight nobody can see without opening every single one. On the market, this is a genuinely paid feature — Ideate Software's **Ideate Explorer** (seat-licensed, subscription-only) markets "Views Not Placed on Sheets" as one of its headline panels, and BIM Track/Revizto-class QA suites bundle an equivalent under much larger paid packages; Revit itself has never shipped it natively, and no free add-in on the market offers a standalone version of just this one check.

**Description:**
`Orphan View Sweep.pushbutton`, a new sibling inside `Essential.panel/Bulk Tool.stack/Bulk Delete.pulldown/`, reusing that pulldown's own proven checklist-and-delete shell rather than inventing a new one.
1. **Collect every real view** — not `get_eligible_views()`'s six-type picker subset, but every non-template `View` in the model: the same base `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(View).WhereElementIsNotElementType()` call, this time with `ViewSchedule`, `ViewDrafting` and Legends included and only `ViewType.Internal`/system browser organization views excluded.
2. **Cross-reference against sheets** — collect every `ViewSheet` via `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(ViewSheet)`, and for each call `sheet.GetAllPlacedViews()` (schedules and legends need `sheet.GetAllViewports()` → `Viewport.ViewId`, since schedule instances on a sheet are not returned by `GetAllPlacedViews()`) to build the set of every `ElementId` that is actually placed somewhere. Any collected view not in that set is orphaned; any `ViewSheet` whose own placed-view count is zero is flagged as an empty sheet.
3. **Checklist dialog** — one list, grouped by Orphan Views / Empty Sheets, each row showing name, `ViewType` label (via `get_view_label()`), and a "last modified" hint pulled the same way `Bulk Delete`'s own naming-collision check already reads element state before offering a delete — with a dependent-view guard so a primary view's dependents are shown nested under it rather than flattened into false "orphans" that would break on deletion order.
4. **Confirm → delete** — one `Transaction`, `doc.Delete(view.Id)` per ticked row, in dependent-before-primary order, reusing `Bulk Delete`'s own confirm-dialog and result-summary pattern verbatim.
5. **Safety default** — views referenced only by a `ScheduleSheetInstance` legend placed on another legend, or views that are themselves a sheet's title block's own internal view, are excluded from the candidate list rather than silently offered for deletion.

**Implementation:** New `Bulk Delete.pulldown/Orphan View Sweep.pushbutton/` (`script.py`, `ui.xaml`, `bundle.yaml`, `icon.png`), built as a fourth `TARGET` branch in the same `script.py` dispatch pattern `Delete FillPatterns/LinePatterns/LineStyles.pushbutton` already share (each file differs by exactly one `TARGET = "..."` line per the header comment), adding `TARGET = "orphanview"` with its own `_collect_orphanviews()`/`_collect_emptysheets()` pair in place of `_collect_fillpatterns()`/`_collect_linepatterns()`. New module `anongee_toolkit/revit/view_hygiene.py`: `all_real_views(doc)` (the widened collector described above), `placed_view_ids(doc)` (the `ViewSheet`/`GetAllPlacedViews`/`GetAllViewports` cross-reference), and `find_orphans(doc)` / `find_empty_sheets(doc)` returning the two flagged lists — exported from `anongee_toolkit/revit/__init__.py` alongside the existing `get_eligible_views`/`get_view_label` the same way every other `revit.*` helper already is. Tests: `tests/test_view_hygiene.py`, built the way `tests/test_views.py` (if present) or the repo's existing stub-`View` fixture pattern already mocks `ViewType`/`IsTemplate`, asserting a view placed via a stub `Viewport` is never flagged, a dependent view is nested under its primary, and a sheet with one placed legend is not flagged empty.

**Future update:**
- Fold straight into the already-logged Bulk Purge idea's single "model hygiene" pulldown once that ships, so View Templates, Filters, Materials and orphan Views are one consistent audit-and-purge surface instead of four separate pushbuttons.

## 2026-10-10 15:43 UTC

**Idea name:** Rebar Spacing Drift Auditor — catches the rebar sets whose Revit-recalculated spacing has silently drifted past the design-intent pitch after a host was resized, something the model never warns about on its own.

**Potential:** Every rebar in this repo is written once and never read back for spacing. `anongee_toolkit/structural/rebar_factory.py:390-409` (`apply_layout`) calls `GetShapeDrivenAccessor()` and does `SetLayoutAsNumberWithSpacing` / `SetLayoutAsMaximumSpacing` from a one-shot workbook value — it has no counterpart that re-reads the accessor later. `anongee_toolkit/rc_automation/models.py:288-309` (`_RebarRow.layout_rule`) is explicit that the design pitch exists only as the workbook's `Spacing` column (`tests/fixtures/rc_automation/COLUMN_REBAR.csv:1,4` — ties `@200`) and that "the workbook does not carry a LayoutRule column because a schedule never does" (`models.py:296-298`); nothing downstream ever compares that intended pitch to what Revit is actually showing today. `anongee_toolkit/structural/rebar_constraints.py:306-319` (`array_length_mm`) reads `accessor.ArrayLength` back from the model for exactly one purpose — confirming a *just-created* varying set's length — and stops; it never reads `.Spacing`/`.NumberOfBarPositions` or compares them to a design limit. `anongee_toolkit/structural/rebars.py:15` (`get_rebars`) is the only place the repo ever collects existing `OST_Rebar` elements for inspection, and it does nothing with what it finds beyond handing it to the visibility tools. So when a beam, slab or footing is later stretched, shortened or re-typed by hand (the ordinary daily editing a structural modeler does, independent of the RC Automation/BBS pipeline), a `FixedNumber` set keeps its bar count while Revit silently widens the spacing to fill the new length, and a `MaximumSpacing` set silently adds or drops bars — both change the actual reinforcement provided with no warning, no red flag, and no entry in any schedule, which still just says "N bars" or "@200" as typed. This is distinct from **Rebar Layout Rule Batch Editor**, which is a write tool for deliberately *changing* the assigned layout rule on many sets at once; this tool never changes a rule — it is a read-only detector that fires precisely when the rule was never touched but the geometry under it moved. It is also distinct from **Rebar Cover Auditor** (checks bar-to-face clear distance, not bar-to-bar pitch), **Design-Force Reinforcement Compliance Checker** (checks provided steel area against a structural analysis load case, an engineering-capacity question), and **Rebar Joint Clash & Congestion Checker** (checks 3D collision/congestion at intersections, not spacing drift along one run). Market check: Revit raises no warning for this at all — a `FixedNumber` set re-spacing itself is treated as expected, correct behaviour by the API. None of the usual paid add-ins (CTC BIM Logix, Naviate, Ideate, dedicated rebar-detailing extensions) ship a model-wide "has this rebar set drifted out of its design pitch since it was placed" check; they focus on bar creation, detailing and BBS export, not on auditing existing bars against the spacing the engineer originally specified for them.

**Description:**
1. Run with a selection to audit just those rebar sets, or with none to audit every `OST_Rebar` element in the model.
2. The tool collects each bar's `GetShapeDrivenAccessor()`, reads its current `ArrangeType`, actual `.Spacing`/`.NumberOfBarPositions`/`.ArrayLength`, and the host it belongs to.
3. For each set it looks up the design-intent spacing — first from a project/shared parameter on the bar or host if one is bound (e.g. a schedule-mark-matched `Spacing` value), falling back to the same `TypeMark → Spacing` lookup already used by the `COLUMN_REBAR`/`BEAM_REBAR`/`FOOTING_REBAR` sheets, matched by the host's Type Mark.
4. A results dialog lists every set whose live spacing now differs from its design value beyond a tolerance, grouped by host, with % drift, host length then vs. now (where recoverable), and a "select host" / "isolate in 3D" action per row.
5. For `MaximumSpacing` sets flagged over-limit, an optional one-click "re-apply design pitch" calls `SetLayoutAsMaximumSpacing` again with the stored design value so Revit adds the missing bars; `FixedNumber` sets are flagged only (changing their count is a design decision, not something to silently automate).
6. The audit list exports to TSV alongside the model, in the same findings-sheet shape RC Automation already produces, for the QA record.

**Implementation:** New pushbutton at `AnonGee.extension/AnonGee.tab/Essential.panel/Bulk Tool.stack/Rebar.pulldown/Spacing Drift Auditor.pushbutton` (third item beside the existing `Obscured Rebar.pushbutton` and `Copy Rebar Visibility.pushbutton` in that same pulldown). Reuses `anongee_toolkit/structural/rebars.py:15` `get_rebars()` for collection, the safe-call/accessor pattern from `anongee_toolkit/structural/rebar_constraints.py:70-93` (`_call`, `is_shape_driven`) to read `.Spacing`/`.NumberOfBarPositions` across API builds without crashing on free-form bars, `anongee_toolkit/ui/xaml.py` `load_xaml()`/`fill_combo()` and `anongee_toolkit/ui/forms.py` `alert()`/`confirm()` for the dialog shell, and the badge-list UI pattern already built in `Obscured Rebar.pushbutton/script.py`. New toolkit module `anongee_toolkit/structural/rebar_spacing_audit.py` with `actual_spacing_mm(rebar)`, `design_spacing_for(host, rebar_sheet_rows)`, and `apply_design_spacing(rebar, spacing_mm)` (thin wrapper over `rebar_factory.apply_layout`'s `SetLayoutAsMaximumSpacing` call). Tests: `tests/test_rebar_spacing_audit.py` built the way `tests/fixtures/rc_automation/COLUMN_REBAR.csv` already is — stub accessors exposing `.Spacing`/`.ArrangeType`/`.ArrayLength`, asserting drift is flagged only past tolerance and that `FixedNumber` sets are never auto-rewritten.

**Future update:**
- Extend the same drift check to slab/wall fabric-mesh sheet gaps and to tie/stirrup spacing along a full beam or column stack, not just one bar set at a time.
- Hook a `DocumentChanged` handler so a drift is flagged the moment an edit pushes a set out of spec, instead of waiting for a manual audit run.
- Feed the per-host drift log into `anongee_toolkit/rc_automation/reconcile.py`'s existing findings pipeline so an Excel-driven `beams.sync`/`columns.sync` run reports "drift since last sync" the same way it already reports created/matched/modified counts.

**Idea name:** Shared-Coordinate Setting-Out Schedule Exporter — extends `structural/coordinates.py`'s existing "two reference points, Z only" math (`survey_offset_mm()`) with the one axis it has always left untouched, X/Y plus the project's true-north rotation, and turns every placed column, pile/footing Mark and named grid intersection into a printable Easting/Northing/RL table a site surveyor can load straight into a total station — closing the one everyday handover this toolkit has solved exactly half of since the module's own docstring was written.

**Potential:**
Before any column, pile or footing can be poured, somebody on site has to know exactly where its centre is in real-world coordinates, not model coordinates — a surveyor keys an Easting/Northing/RL triplet into a total station or GPS rover and walks the layout out on raw ground. Today that number is produced by hand, every time a layout is set or revised: a modeler either exports a DWG and leaves the surveyor to dig coordinates out of CAD by eye, or reads dimensions off a plan sheet and retypes them against whatever offset the survey point happens to carry, repeating the same manual translation on every revision. The toolkit already carries every other half of this problem, proven and shipping, and has simply never been asked for the one multiplication that turns a model point into a number a surveyor can act on without opening Revit. `structural/coordinates.py`'s `survey_offset_mm(doc)` already reads `BasePoint.GetProjectBasePoint(doc)`/`BasePoint.GetSurveyPoint(doc)` and reports the project-base-to-survey-point offset — but only ever through its own `_elevation_mm()` helper, which touches `point.Position.Z` and nothing else; `.Position.X`/`.Position.Y` and the project's rotation to true north (`ProjectLocation.GetProjectPosition(XYZ).Angle`) are never read anywhere in this file, or anywhere else in the toolkit — `grep -rn "ProjectPosition\|GetProjectPosition"` across the whole `anongee_toolkit` package returns zero hits. `structural/grids.py`'s `intersection_mm(doc_grids, name_x, name_y)` already computes a named grid crossing as an `(x, y)` pair in millimetres, and `structural/columns.py`'s `placed(doc)` already walks every placed column `FamilyInstance` and returns its `(x_mm, y_mm)` location point — but both stay in internal, project-origin millimetres, never rotated or offset to the survey point the way `survey_offset_mm()` already does for elevation. The team already thinks in these exact terms on the input side — `rc_automation/excel_engine.py` lists `("Easting", "XCoord")`/`("Northing", "YCoord")` as accepted header aliases for the `x_mm`/`y_mm` columns an RC Automation workbook feeds in — but that is a placement *input* alias, never a surveyed, rotated *output* schedule. On the market, a true shared-coordinate stakeout export is something Autodesk's own Point Layout/total-station-integration add-ins and the seat-licensed Trimble/Leica Revit plug-ins charge for as part of a much larger paid field-layout package; nothing free turns a model's own already-placed Marks into a flat, printable setting-out table the way this would.

**Description:**
`Setting-Out Export.pushbutton`, a new sibling to `Export Schedule.pushbutton` in `Essential.panel/Action.stack/`.
1. **Scope & category pick** — a scope radio (Whole Model / Active View / Selection) exactly like `BBS Generator.pushbutton/core/rebar_reader.py`'s own `_collect_rebars(doc, uidoc, scope)` dispatch, plus a checklist of which point sources to include: Columns, Foundations/Piles, and named Grid intersections.
2. **Rotate-and-offset, not just offset** — a new `shared_xy_mm(doc, point_xyz)` sibling function in `structural/coordinates.py`, following `survey_offset_mm()`'s exact "read and report, never move anything" contract (its own docstring: *"that is a decision somebody makes on purpose"*): reads `doc.ActiveProjectLocation.GetProjectPosition(XYZ.Zero)` for `.Angle`/`.EastWest`/`.NorthSouth`/`.Elevation`, then rotates each point with the identical `cos_a, sin_a = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)` / `x*cos_a - y*sin_a, x*sin_a + y*cos_a` arithmetic `structural/footings.py`'s own `curve_loop(points_mm, origin_mm, rotation_deg)` already runs for footing outlines, before adding the survey offset — returning `(None, note)` on the same "cannot answer, say why" contract as `survey_offset_mm()` whenever the model has no project position set.
3. **Collect & key by Mark** — each matched column/footing/pile is read through its own existing locator (`structural/columns.py`'s `placed()` for columns, the same `Location.Point` read generalized for foundations/piles) and keyed by `BuiltInParameter.ALL_MODEL_MARK` — the same "Mark is the schedule key" convention `structural/rebar_hosts.py`'s `DEFAULT_KEY_PARAMETER = "Mark"`/`index_by_key()` already establishes — so a row reads the same Mark a site crew already has on the drawing, never a raw `ElementId`. Each named grid intersection is added the same way through `grids.intersection_mm()`.
4. **Export** — one sheet of `Mark | Easting (mm) | Northing (mm) | RL (mm) | Source` rows, written through the exact same `ExcelComWriter` (`io/excel.py`: `add_sheet()`, `write_array()`, `autofit_columns()`) Export Schedule and RC Automation's own outputs already use, landscape-formatted and print-ready for a direct site handover.
5. **Read-only** — no `Transaction` anywhere in the tool, the same safe-to-run-at-any-time class as Base Point & Survey Datum Auditor (2026-09-28), since every number it produces is derived, never written back.

**Implementation:**
- `structural/coordinates.py`: add `shared_xy_mm(doc, point_xyz)` alongside the existing `survey_offset_mm()`/`_elevation_mm()`, reusing `anongee_toolkit.revit.units.ft_to_mm` and the rotation arithmetic lifted from `structural/footings.py`'s `curve_loop()`.
- New `anongee_toolkit/structural/setting_out.py`: `collect_points(doc, scope, categories)` — dispatches scope exactly like `BBS Generator`'s `_collect_rebars()`, reads columns via `columns.placed()`, foundations/piles via the same `Location.Point` pattern, and grid intersections via `grids.intersection_mm()`, mapping every point through the new `shared_xy_mm()` and keying by Mark via `rebar_hosts.index_by_key()`'s convention.
- `Essential.panel/Action.stack/Setting-Out Export.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (scope radio + category checklist, reusing the toolkit's existing `ui.checklist.CheckList` control), `bundle.yaml`, `icon.png`, `README.md`.

**Future update:**
- A round-trip mode: read a surveyor's as-built total-station CSV back in and diff it against the exported design table, reusing `rc_automation/excel_engine.py`'s own header-matching/coercion conventions, to flag out-of-tolerance stakeout before a pour instead of discovering it after.
- Batch KML/DXF point-block export of the same table for GPS rovers or drone-survey cross-checks, alongside the Excel sheet.
- Cross-reference the already-logged Base Point & Survey Datum Auditor so a model whose survey point or rotation changes mid-project surfaces a "this export is now stale" flag instead of a silently outdated handover sheet.

The read half exists too: `structural/rebar_constraints.py`'s `is_shape_driven()`/`manager_for()` (`:80,86`) already separate shape-driven from free-form bars, and `array_length_mm()` (`:306-321`) already reads the accessor's current array length straight back out — proven, just never paired with a write loop. Revit's own Mark field has no sequencing behaviour at all: every copy a native duplicate command produces carries the *exact same* Mark as its source, so the modeler's very next move, every single time, is to click through each new copy by hand and retype `P-14`, `P-15`, `P-16`... into Properties — or skip it and let Revit's own duplicate-Mark warning pile up silently until a schedule or a rebar tag collides on it. `anongee_toolkit/structural/structure_run.py:157` already shows this repo's only existing Mark-handling logic anywhere — `if placement.mark in already:` — and it is a pure *read-only collision check* against a mark a human (or a workbook row) already decided; it has never been pointed at Revit's own duplicate-creation event, only at RC Automation's own Excel-driven placement pass. The one engine in the whole codebase that already does "claim the next number in sequence, cached per element, never collide" is `BBS Generator.pushbutton/core/bar_mark_manager.py`'s `AutoMarkGenerator.get_or_create()` (`:42-56`) — a `(prefix, diameter_mm)`-keyed counter that mints `f"{prefix}-T{diameter_mm}-{seq:02d}"` the moment a bar with no mark is first read — but a repo-wide grep shows it has exactly one caller, `rebar_reader.py:180`, and has never been generalized past rebar diameter groups to any other category's Mark/Pier No./Pile No. field. Hooking the live duplicate action itself, rather than auditing after it, needs a mechanism this repo has never once used: a repo-wide `grep -rniE "DocumentChanged|IUpdater|UpdaterRegistry" AnonGee.extension --include=*.py` (excluding vendored `lib/py2`/`lib/py3` trees) returns exactly one incidental hit — a string literal inside `cad2bim/tests/test_clr_registry.py:102`'s own interface-name list, there only to confirm the CLR interface name resolves, never implemented against a real document anywhere in the toolkit. Every one of the 108 ideas already logged here, and every pushbutton actually shipped, is a one-shot batch run a modeler has to remember to launch; none of them fire themselves off the back of a native command the way this one would. On the market, the closest shipped features — AGACAD's numbering tools, CTC's BIM Project Suite renumbering module, BIM One's Mark utilities — are all the same shape as this repo's own Grid Mark Assistant and Door & Window Mark Sequencer: a separate, paid, per-seat batch renumber run after the fact. None of them, free or paid, listen for Copy/Array/Mirror itself and fill the Mark in before the modeler's next click.

**Description:**
`Mark Incrementer.pushbutton`, a toggle-style sibling in `Essential.panel` next to Grid Mark Assistant and Door & Window Mark Sequencer, reusing the modeless-window architecture `Modeless.pushbutton` already documents as the toolkit's own reference pattern (design system §12.8 — WPF window off the main thread, every Revit write marshalled through `IExternalEventHandler`/`ExternalEvent.Raise()`):
1. **Arm, don't audit** — pressing the button opens a small modeless status panel and registers a project-scoped `IUpdater` (or a `DocumentChanged` subscriber, whichever proves stable under pyRevit's CPython3 engine across repeated presses) watching a modeler-picked category set; the panel stays open and interactive while Revit itself stays fully usable, so arming it is a once-per-session click, not a once-per-copy one.
2. **Catch the duplicate** — on every `DocumentChanged` firing, `GetAddedElementIds()` is diffed against the element(s) selected immediately before the native command ran; any added element that shares a Type with, and sits within copy/array/mirror range of, a source element already carrying a non-empty Mark (or Pier No./Pile No., per a configured parameter-per-category map) is queued as "needs a mark."

5. **Respect a hand-fixed mark** — the same lock convention Door & Window Mark Sequencer's own Implementation section already specifies (a mark that is non-empty and does not match this tool's own generated pattern is left alone) applies here too, so re-arming after a modeler manually retyped one mark never overwrites it.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/revit/live_mark_updater.py`: the `IUpdater`/`DocumentChanged` handler itself, plus a generalized `SequenceCounter` lifted from `AutoMarkGenerator`'s `(prefix, diameter_mm)` keying into `(prefix, group_key)`, so `BBS Generator` can eventually be pointed at the same counter class instead of keeping its own copy.

- Reuses `Modeless.pushbutton/script.py`'s existing `ModelessHandler`/`ExternalEvent`/session-state-in-`sys.modules` scaffold unmodified for the status panel, rather than writing a second modeless shell.
- Reuses `RoundElementDist.pushbutton/script.py:169-201`'s `build_direction_groups()` unmodified for the optional per-row restart mode.
- `Essential.panel/Mark Incrementer.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (category/parameter map + arm/disarm toggle + running log + undo-last-batch), `bundle.yaml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `icon.png`.

**Potential:**
A repo-wide `grep -rniE "MakeInstance|MakeType|FamilyParameter|FamilyManager" AnonGee.extension --include=*.py` (excluding `lib/py2`, `lib/py3/pythonwin`, `lib/py3/ezdxf`, `lib/py3/numpy`, `lib/py3/pandas`) returns **zero real hits anywhere in the toolkit** — the only two matches at all are `isinstance(...)` calls in unrelated geometry/type-checking code, confirmed by eye, not a single one a `FamilyParameter`. That is the same zero-hit result the already-logged Nested Parameter Associator (2026-10-08 00:40 UTC, immediately above) and Type Catalog Builder (2026-09-30 05:40 UTC) both already found and both used to justify themselves as this repo's first family-document-opening tools — this would be a third, sharing the same `Document.EditFamily()`/`Application.OpenDocumentFile()` access layer Nested Parameter Associator's own Implementation section already proposes as `anongee_toolkit/revit/family_documents.py`, pointed at a different `FamilyManager` call than either of those two ever touches. The everyday pain this leaves fully manual is one every modeler maintaining a real family library hits, usually mid-project rather than once at authoring time: a `Mark` or `Comments` field gets authored as a Type parameter early on, then a schedule or tag requirement shows up that needs a unique value per placed instance — or the reverse, an `Instance`-bound dimension that should have been standardized to a handful of catalog Types turns out to drift silently because every placed copy carries its own editable number. Revit's native fix is per-parameter, per-family, and entirely by hand: open the family, Family Types, scroll to the row, tick or clear the small checkbox under the "Instance" column, Apply, close, `LoadFamily` back into the project, confirm the overwrite prompt — once per family. A real structural/architectural range (a precast panel family with eight width variants, a door family with a dozen hardware-set types, a column family repeated across a dozen size catalogs) multiplies that into dozens of family-editor round trips for what is, underneath, one mechanical toggle repeated by name. `anongee_toolkit/revit/parameters.py`'s own `get_parameter()` (`:11-32`) already proves this toolkit is comfortable resolving a parameter purely by name across an unknown set of elements — "Checks the element instance first, then its ElementType" (`:17`) — but that function, and every caller of it, operates on a placed `Element` inside the *open* project document; nothing in the repo has ever resolved a parameter by name inside a *family* document's own `FamilyManager.Parameters` collection, the one place this flip actually has to happen. The one real constraint Revit enforces here, and the one piece of domain knowledge this idea needs to get right, is the same rule the stock Family Types dialog already encodes by greying the checkbox out: a `FamilyParameter` that carries a formula (`FamilyParameter.Formula` non-empty, or anything downstream of it in a formula chain) cannot be made an Instance parameter, because a formula is evaluated once per Type, never per placed copy — `FamilyManager.MakeInstance` throws rather than silently no-op'ing when asked to flip one. On the market, this specific batch operation shows up only as a handful of narrow, single-family Dynamo graphs circulating on forums (pick one open family document, one hardcoded parameter name, flip it) — no name-matching across a whole folder of `.rfa` files, no formula-safety check, no preview, and nothing that reports which families in a batch were skipped and why; nothing free, and no paid add-in found in public listings either, runs this across a library in one pass.

**Description:**
`Family Parameter Flipper.pushbutton`, new sibling to the already-logged Type Catalog Builder and Nested Parameter Associator in `Essential.panel` (the toolkit's three family-document-opening tools, all built on the same proposed access layer):
1. **Pick families** — every family loaded in the current project (listed by name, multi-select) or a browsed folder of `.rfa` files on disk, batched so a parameter name typed once is checked against every family in the set rather than family by family.
2. **Name the parameter(s)** — a modeler types (or picks from a union of every parameter name found across the already-selected families) one or more parameter names to target, e.g. `Mark`, `Width`; matched case-insensitively against each family's own `FamilyManager.Parameters`.
3. **Open and resolve, read-only first** — each family opened via the shared `family_documents.open_for_edit()` call (`Document.EditFamily()` for a loaded family, `Application.OpenDocumentFile()`, detached, for a browsed `.rfa`); for each name match, read `FamilyParameter.IsInstance` for its current state and `FamilyParameter.Formula`/the formula-chain check for whether a flip to Instance is even legal.
4. **Preview grid** — one row per family × matched parameter: family name, parameter name, current state (Type/Instance), requested target, and a flag of **blocked — driven by formula** for anything `MakeInstance` would reject outright, so a modeler sees the whole batch's outcome, including every family that will be skipped and why, before anything is written.
5. **Apply, per ticked row** — one `Transaction` scoped to each family document: `FamilyManager.MakeInstance(parameter)` or `FamilyManager.MakeType(parameter)` depending on the requested direction; a caught-and-reported failure (a parameter actually used in a nested-family array, or any other Revit-side refusal) leaves that one row failed rather than aborting the batch.
6. **Reload and report** — `fam_doc.LoadFamily(doc)` pushes each edited family back into the live project (overwrite-parameter-values prompt accepted automatically, since the flip itself never touches a value, only where it lives), then a result summary — families flipped / already-correct / blocked-by-formula / failed — in the same plain report convention every other sibling batch tool in this log already closes on.

**Implementation:**
- Reuses `anongee_toolkit/revit/family_documents.py`'s proposed `open_for_edit(app, family_or_path)` unmodified — this tool's own justification for that module shipping as shared code rather than being written twice, exactly as Nested Parameter Associator's own Implementation section already anticipates ("first family-document module... or second... either way shared rather than duplicated").
- New `anongee_toolkit/revit/family_param_flip.py`: `find_parameter_by_name(family_manager, name)` doing the case-insensitive resolve against `FamilyManager.Parameters` (the family-document-scoped sibling of `revit/parameters.get_parameter()`'s project-element resolve, `parameters.py:11-32`); `can_make_instance(parameter)` checking `Formula`/formula-chain membership before any write is attempted, so a blocked row is known at preview time, not discovered as a caught exception mid-batch; `flip(family_manager, parameter, to_instance)` wrapping `MakeInstance`/`MakeType` with the one try/except this API actually needs.
- Same preview-gated `CheckList`/`hostwnd`/`progressbar` modeless shell every other batch tool in the repo already runs on, reused rather than rebuilt.
- `Essential.panel/Family Parameter Flipper.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (family picker + parameter-name field + preview grid), `bundle.yaml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `icon.png`.

**Future update:**
- When flipping Type → Instance, carry each placed instance's *current displayed value* forward as its new per-instance default instead of letting it silently revert to whatever the family's own Type value was, since that is the one value-loss surprise a modeler doing this flip today would not expect.
- A saved rule list ("these parameter names are always Instance in our office standard") that this tool can re-run as an audit — flagging any family in a library that drifted from the rule — the same "office standard, auditable and batch-fixable" posture the already-logged Family Library Sync and Naming Convention Auditor entries both already take for their own, different family-health axes.
- Multi-parameter batches saved and replayed per family-type range (a precast panel family's whole width/height/mark convention flipped in one named preset), instead of typing the same parameter-name list in by hand on every run.
- Once Nested Parameter Associator ships its own name/`StorageType`/unit matcher, reuse it here too: a parameter flipped to Instance on a host family that already associates a nested instance's own parameter to it is exactly the case Nested Parameter Associator's own future-update list already flags as the one break worth detecting, not just the swap-driven one.

That entry's own scope is explicit and narrow, though: it opens a family document only to harvest/write an external type-catalog `.txt`, never to touch a nested instance or call `AssociateElementParameterToFamilyParameter` — so whichever of the two ships first, this idea is still the first (and, if Type Catalog Builder lands first, the second) real caller of family-document access for a genuinely different job: making a nested family's own parameter value visible and drivable at the host family's level. This repo already states the exact boundary that makes the gap real, in its own words: `structural/element_params.py`'s module docstring spells out, as one of the three reasons that module exists, "**A shared parameter is a document-level binding, not a value**... a family parameter cannot leave its family" — true today only because nothing in this codebase has ever called the one API built to let a family parameter's value reach *outward*, into a nested instance sitting inside the same family, or *inward*, surfacing a nested instance's own parameter up to the host. The pain this leaves fully manual is one every structural/precast modeler building parametric content hits constantly: a base-plate family with a nested anchor-bolt family inside it (the exact nesting the already-logged Embed Plate, Anchor Bolt & Lifting/Bracing Insert Placer idea assumes already exists as placed content, never as authored family structure), a precast panel family with a nested lifting-insert family, a door family with a nested hardware-set family — any time a modeler wants a host-level parameter (bolt diameter, insert count, hardware code) to actually show the nested instance's real value in a project schedule or tag, or wants one host parameter to drive several nested instances' matching dimensions at once, the only native path is: open Family Types, find the nested instance's exposed parameter in the list, click the small "=" associate glyph next to it, pick the host family parameter, confirm — once per nested instance, and the association is *per placed nested instance*, not per nested-family "slot," so swapping which family/type is nested in that slot (the exact operation the already-logged Family/Type Swap Wizard proposes doing in bulk at the project level) silently drops every association that instance held, with no warning beyond a value that quietly stops updating. A family with a dozen nested bolts/inserts, multiplied across the dozen types a real base-plate family carries, is a hundred-plus individual clicks repeated by hand, redone from scratch every time the nested content changes — and Revit's own UI gives no batch view of which associations exist, which are missing, or which just broke. On the market, this exact batch-wiring is not sold as a standalone feature at all: a handful of narrow, single-purpose Dynamo graphs circulate on forums for one specific family at a time (no name-matching, no preview, no re-run-after-swap detection), and the only place it is reliably done well is inside pre-built, paid "smart" parametric content libraries sold by specialist content-authoring firms, where the wiring is baked in once at content-creation time and billed for — never offered as a tool a modeler can run on their own family.

**Description:**
`Nested Parameter Associator.pushbutton`, new sibling to the already-logged Type Catalog Builder in `Essential.panel` (both the toolkit's only family-document-opening tools, sharing the same access layer):

1. **Collect** — `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(ImportInstance).WhereElementIsNotElementType().ToElements()`, the identical collector `cad_links.py:23` and `revit_ops.py:246` both already run, kept whole this time instead of filtered down to one half.

3. **Locate** — for each embedded instance, `instance.OwnerViewId` resolved to a view name (model-wide import vs. one specific drafting/detail view) and, where that view is placed, its sheet number — so a finding reads "Site-Plan-OLD.dwg, embedded in Drafting View 'CAD Trace (unused)', not on any sheet" instead of a bare element id.
4. **Size** — `instance.get_BoundingBox(None)` extents as a rough footprint estimate per finding, so the preview can be sorted by probable file-weight impact first, the same ranking Family Health Auditor's own future-update section already names wanting ("per-finding recovered-byte estimate") for its sibling family-level case.
5. **Preview grid** — one row per embedded import: source name, host view/sheet, extents, instance count if the same import type repeats; report-only until rows are ticked, nothing written on the scan pass itself.
6. **Act, per ticked row, one of two explicit choices** — **Purge** (`doc.Delete(instance.Id)`, for a trace nobody needs anymore); or **Convert to link** — since an embedded import carries no stored source path (that is exactly how step 2 told it apart from a real link), the tool prompts once per distinct embedded CAD type for the modeler to browse to the original DWG/DXF on disk, creates a true CAD link from that file at the same `OwnerViewId`/transform the embedded instance held, then deletes the embedded copy — turning an untracked, unmaintainable trace into a real, re-linkable reference instead of just removing it.
7. **Result** — a dated before/after count (instances purged, instances converted, bytes estimated recovered), exportable through the same `openpyxl` path `Export Schedule.pushbutton`/`BBS Generator.pushbutton` already use, so a cleanup pass becomes a handover artifact rather than a one-time silent fix.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/revit/cad_imports.py` (sibling to `revit/geometry.py`/`revit/parameters.py`): `collect_import_instances(doc)` running the shared collector once; `is_embedded(instance)` doing the `IsLinked` + `GetExternalFileReference()` agreement check from step 2; `locate(instance, doc)` resolving `OwnerViewId` → view name → sheet number (reusing whatever view/sheet lookup `Orphaned View Finder`'s own proposed engine settles on, once it ships, rather than a second implementation); kept outside `cad2bim/` on purpose, since `cad_links.py`'s own docstring is explicit that excluding the embedded half is deliberate for *that* tool's job — this is a new, narrower-purpose module, not an edit to cad2bim's.
- Convert-to-link reuses the browse-for-file prompt pattern `forms.pick_file`-style dialogs already use elsewhere in this repo, then calls Revit's own link-vs-import API pair (the same switch Insert ▸ Link CAD exposes over Insert ▸ Import CAD in the native ribbon) — the one CAD-placing call with no prior art anywhere in this toolkit, since every existing CAD reader here (`cad2bim`, `AutoLevel`) only ever reads a link a modeler already placed by hand, never creates one; wrapped so a failed re-link (missing file, wrong file picked, geometry mismatch) leaves the embedded original untouched rather than deleting first and failing second.
- Bounding-box sizing reuses the same `get_BoundingBox(None)` extents call `RoundElementDist.pushbutton`'s own `collect_solids()` neighbourhood already trusts for non-solid-based measurement, rather than attempting `get_solid_variable_m3()` against geometry that is frequently 2D line/hatch data with no solid to measure.
- Purge path reuses `operations/bulk_delete.py`'s `RevitTransaction`-wrapped per-item delete shape (the same pattern Family Health Auditor's own implementation plan already commits to reusing for its "fully unused families" row), so one import that turns out to still be needed by something the scan missed is skipped, not fatal to the batch.
- Same modeless window shell (`anongee_toolkit.ui.hostwnd`/`checklist`/`progressbar`/`theme`) every other multi-step tool in the repo already runs on.
- Sits in `Essential.panel/Bulk Tool.stack/`, own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`/`CHANGELOG.md`/`icon.png` per the root README's documented versioned-tool layout.

**Future update:**
- Once Family Health Auditor ships its `Document.EditFamily()` scan, point the same `is_embedded()`/sizing pair at geometry nested inside loadable families too, so one shared engine answers "where is every embedded DWG in this project, at either layer" instead of two separate tools each covering half the document model.
- Pre-fill the "browse to original file" prompt from a firm's own CAD-archive folder convention, matched against the embedded `CADLinkType`'s stored display name, cutting the one manual step convert-to-link still needs per distinct import.
- Cross-reference findings against the already-logged Orphaned View Finder's own "not on any sheet" flag, so an embedded import that only ever lived inside an already-dead drafting view is reported as a combined, higher-confidence single finding rather than two separate cleanup passes catching half of it each.
- Feed the purge/convert result into Sheet Issue Kit's own pre-issue checklist, so a consultant handover or client transmittal never silently carries along an embedded trace nobody meant to ship.

**Potential:**
`todo-list.md:1059` is unambiguous about where the roadmap's own "Shop drawing assembly" item actually stalls: "`Dimension.Create` needs stable geometric `Reference`s, and getting them for rebar and element faces is fragile and moves between Revit versions... Realistic first target: sheets, views, crops, schedules and most tags automatic; **dimensions by hand**." The already-logged Rebar Callout Tagger (2026-10-02 10:41 UTC) closes the *text* half of that same roadmap line — it writes `#12-16T@200`-style callouts via `MultiReferenceAnnotation`/`IndependentTag` — but its own write-up never once calls `Dimension.Create`, and a callout is a label, not a measurement: it tells a bar fixer the spec, not the as-drawn spacing a site engineer checks against a tape. The already-logged Rebar Cover Auditor (2026-09-19 UTC) is the closer miss — it already resolves a real, per-bar cover number via `anongee_toolkit/structural/rebar_constraints.py`'s `distance_to_cover_mm()` (`:118`) and `describe()` (`:149`) — but both only ever feed a report table; neither has ever been asked to draw that gap on a sheet. Every function in this repo that already sets `Options.ComputeReferences = True` (a repo-wide grep finds exactly four: `AutoDIM.pushbutton/script.py:90`, `RoundElementDist.pushbutton/script.py:205`, plus `FramewinToBIM`/`DrawFloor`/`anongee_toolkit/revit/geometry.py` which all set it `False`) walks a `Solid`'s `Faces` collection for a `PlanarFace.Reference` — `AutoDIM`'s own `planar_faces()` (`script.py:87-108`) and `RoundElementDist`'s `collect_solids()` (`script.py:211-`) do exactly this, and it is precisely why `dimension_element()` (`script.py:183-237`) can already build a `ReferenceArray` from `lo.Reference`/`hi.Reference` and call `doc.Create.NewDimension` for a column, beam or footing. A placed `Rebar` element's own geometry is not a face-bearing `Solid` the same way — it is a thin, curve-swept representation per bar — so `planar_faces()` run against a `Rebar` returns nothing usable, and the handful of public Revit API forum threads that answer "how do I dimension a rebar" (the question is common enough to have several, independently landing on the same answer) converge on a different, harder path: read `rebar.get_Geometry(Options)` with `ComputeReferences=True`, walk each `GeometryObject` down to its `Edge`, and call `Curve.GetEndPointReference()` on that edge's curve to get the one `Reference` type `Dimension.Create` will actually accept from a bar — `Edge`→`Curve`, never `Face`. Nothing in this repository has ever written that walk: a repo-wide grep for `GetCenterlineCurves`, `GetCenterlineReferences` and `GetEndPointReference` returns zero hits anywhere in `AnonGee.extension`, including inside `lib/py3` where every other rebar-geometry helper (`rebar_constraints.py`'s own `manager_for()`/`handles()`, `:80,96`) already lives. Day to day this is the one shop-drawing chore every RCC detailer still does entirely by hand, bar by bar, section by section: open a column/beam/wall section RC Automation or a modeler already built, try to pick a bar's edge (which does not highlight the way a wall face does, because Revit itself is working around the same Face-vs-Edge gap), place a spacing dimension between two bars, place a cover dimension off the nearest formwork face, and repeat for every bar group on every section a drawing set needs — with no batch path in Revit's own UI at all. On the market, bar-to-face and bar-to-bar dimensioning exists only as one line item bundled inside the same paid, seat-licensed rebar-detailing suites every other reinforcement idea in this log already checks against (AGACAD Rebar for Revit, Naviate Structure, BIM One); nothing free reads a model's own placed rebar geometry and drops a correct, reference-backed dimension string in one pass.

**Description:**
`Rebar Dimension Placer.pushbutton` lands beside the already-logged `Rebar Tag Sweep.pushbutton`'s own proposed home in `Essential.panel/Action.stack`, as its measurement-drawing sibling rather than a third independent tool:

1. **Scope** — active view only, restricted to the same section/detail/callout view-family short-list `AutoDIM.pushbutton`'s `_NO_DIM_VIEWS` guard (`script.py:34-40`) already enforces for the identical "Dimension.Create only works in a real 2D or locked-3D view" reason.
2. **Collect** — `FilteredElementCollector(doc, view.Id).OfCategory(BuiltInCategory.OST_Rebar)`, the same single-view-scoped collection Rebar Callout Tagger's own step 2 already specifies, paired with each bar's host element (`rebar.GetHostId()`) for the cover half of the job.
3. **Resolve bar references** — a new `bar_endpoint_references()` walk: `rebar.get_Geometry(Options(ComputeReferences=True))` → each `Edge` → `edge.AsCurve().GetEndPointReference(0/1)`, restricted to the handles `rebar_constraints.py`'s own `INTERESTING_HANDLES` tuple (`:59-60`, `StartOfBar`/`EndOfBar`/`RebarPlane`/`TopOfBar`/`BottomOfBar`) already names as meaningful, checked first against `manager_for()`/`handles()` (`rebar_constraints.py:80,96`) so a free-form bar with no shape-driven handles is reported "no stable reference available" rather than guessed at.
4. **Resolve host-face references** — unmodified `planar_faces()`/`extreme_faces()` (`AutoDIM script.py:87-129`) run against the bar's own host, so a cover dimension pairs a bar reference against the exact formwork face `rebar_constraints.distance_to_cover_mm()` (`:118`) already resolved as the one this bar's handle is constrained to — never the nearest face by distance alone.
5. **Preview** — one row per bar group: spacing-dimension count (adjacent-bar references along the set's layout axis), cover-dimension target face, and a "no reference" flag for anything that fell out of step 3; nothing written until rows are ticked, the same preview-before-apply posture every batch tool in this repo already runs on.
6. **Place and guard** — `doc.Create.NewDimension(view, line, referenceArray)` built the same way `dimension_element()` already assembles one (`script.py:228-233`), with a bar/face `Reference` pair instead of two face references; before placing, `FilteredElementCollector(doc, view.Id).OfClass(DB.Dimension)` is read and compared against the candidate reference set the same duplicate-run guard the already-logged Dimension Sweep idea already specifies (`pushbutton-idea.md:2166`), so a second pass after a revision only adds what changed instead of stacking a second dimension under the first.

- New `anongee_toolkit/structural/rebar_references.py`: `bar_endpoint_references(rebar, handle_names=rebar_constraints.INTERESTING_HANDLES)` doing the `Options(ComputeReferences=True)` → `Edge` → `Curve.GetEndPointReference()` walk, gated by `rebar_constraints.manager_for()`/`handles()` so an unconstrained/free-form bar is reported, not guessed at.
- Reuses `AutoDIM.pushbutton/script.py`'s `planar_faces()`, `extreme_faces()` and `build_dim_line()` unmodified for the host-face half of every dimension, exactly as Rebar Callout Tagger's own write-up already commits to reusing `element_frame()`/`bbox_center()` from the same file rather than a second implementation.
- Reuses `rebar_constraints.distance_to_cover_mm()`/`describe()` to pick which host face a cover dimension pairs against, rather than re-deriving a nearest-face search.
- `Essential.panel/Action.stack/Rebar Dimension Placer.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (view-scope note + preview grid), `bundle.yaml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `icon.png`, `rebar_dim_config.json` (minimum gap before a spacing dimension is skipped as redundant, cover-dimension offset) mirroring `slab_convert_config.json`'s existing override-by-config shape.
- Duplicate-run guard reads `Dimension.References` off `FilteredElementCollector(doc, view.Id).OfClass(DB.Dimension)`, the identical read the already-logged Dimension Sweep idea specifies for its own, non-rebar scope.
