## 2026-10-07 00:50 UTC

**Idea name:** Global Parameter Linker & Hardcode Consolidator — a batch front-end for Revit's native Global Parameters, auditing which type/instance parameters across the model are already driven by a Global Parameter versus silently hardcoded, then multi-selecting a set of types/parameters that share one value and associating all of them to a new or existing Global Parameter in a single transaction, instead of Revit's one-at-a-time "fx" icon

**Potential:**
Global Parameters are the one truly native "change it once, everything updates" mechanism Revit ships — a standard column width, a typical setback, a level-to-level height baked into dozens of type parameters — but the stock UI only lets a modeler associate one parameter at a time through a tiny fx icon buried in Type Properties or an instance's Properties palette, with zero project-wide visibility into which parameters are already global-driven versus hardcoded, and no warning when a later manual edit silently breaks an existing association. Retrofitting 40 column types onto one shared "Typical Column Width" driver today means 40+ manual fx-icon round trips, one type at a time, with no batch path and no audit of what's already linked. A repo-wide check of the existing 102-entry idea log (`grep -ci "global parameter" pushbutton-idea.md`) returns exactly one hit, inside **Standards Diff & Selective Transfer** (2026-09-20, `:1292`), and that entry only *flags* that a target's value "looks like it references a project-only Global Parameter" mid-diff — it never creates, associates, or audits one. The log's other parameter tools are mechanically different problems: **Parameter Migrator** and **Cross-Element Parameter Copier** move live *values* between ordinary parameters element-to-element, and the shipped `Parameter Combine.pushbutton` evaluates a formula into one target parameter per element — none of them touch Revit's `GlobalParametersManager`, `GlobalParameter.Create`, or `Parameter.AssociateToGlobalParameter` APIs, and a repo-wide grep for all three names (including every `lib/py3` package, not just `AnonGee.tab`) returns zero hits anywhere outside the one read-only reference below. The toolkit has in fact already built half of this and never finished it: `anongee_toolkit/structural/inventory.py:247-265`'s `_global_parameters(doc)` calls `GlobalParametersManager.GetAllGlobalParameters(doc)` and lists each Global Parameter's name and value-kind for `Extract Template.pushbutton`'s audit report — but it is strictly read-only (no caller anywhere resolves which *other* parameters consume each one, and nothing ever writes an association). `Parameter Combine.pushbutton/script.py`'s own `get_element_parameters_dict()` (`:96`) and its `ScopePickerApp`/`pick_elements_in_view()` scope picker (`:655`, `:804`) already solve the exact "let a modeler multi-select elements/types and see their parameter values side by side" UI problem this needs, just aimed at writing plain values rather than associating to a Global Parameter. On the market this is covered only by paid tooling (ModPlus's plugin bundle) or a hand-built Dynamo graph that demands visual-programming skill a modeler doing day-to-day type cleanup shouldn't need just to batch a native Revit feature; pyRevit stock and Autodesk's free BIM Interoperability Tools have nothing for it.

**Description:**
`Global Parameter Linker.pushbutton`, new sibling to `Parameter Combine.pushbutton` in `Advance.panel` (same panel, since both already read/write parameter values across a picked scope):
1. **Audit mode (read-only, runs first, always)** — walk every type (and, where applicable, instance) parameter across a picked scope, calling `Parameter.IsAssociatedWithGlobalParameters`/`GetAssociatedGlobalParameter` per parameter, and present a grid grouped by category/parameter name showing: linked (and to which Global Parameter), unlinked-but-matching-value (same raw value as an existing Global Parameter — a candidate to link), and unlinked-with-divergent-values (the drift case nobody currently catches, since a manual override breaks an association with no visible warning in the stock UI).
2. **Scope & candidate picking** — reuse `pick_elements_in_view()`/`ScopePickerApp` verbatim for element/type selection, and `get_element_parameters_dict()` to list each candidate's current parameter values so identical hardcoded values jump out before any write happens.
3. **Link (batch-associate)** — for a ticked set of (type, parameter) pairs confirmed to share one value, check `Parameter.CanBeAssociatedToGlobalParameters(doc)`, then call `param.AssociateToGlobalParameter(globalParamId)` per pair inside one `Transaction`; if no suitable Global Parameter exists yet, create one first via `GlobalParameter.Create(doc, name, definition.GetDataType())` seeded from the common value, the same "create the missing binding, then use it" sequencing the already-logged Parameter Pack Provisioner uses for shared parameters.
4. **Consolidate near-duplicates** — when the audit finds several Global Parameters already carrying the same value under slightly different names (a common drift after months of ad-hoc creation), offer to re-point every parameter associated with the duplicates onto one canonical Global Parameter and delete the rest, closing the cleanup half of the problem the stock `GlobalParametersManager` UI leaves entirely manual.
5. **Report** — a short text/Markdown summary (parameters linked, Global Parameters created, duplicates consolidated, remaining divergent values left for manual review) in the same "a text report as the tool's only witness" convention the rest of this log's Advance.panel tools already follow.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/global_params/` package: `audit.py` (wraps `_global_parameters()`'s `GlobalParametersManager.GetAllGlobalParameters` call, extended to resolve `GetAssociatedGlobalParameter` per candidate parameter rather than just listing Global Parameters in isolation); `link.py` (the `CanBeAssociatedToGlobalParameters`/`AssociateToGlobalParameter`/`GlobalParameter.Create` write path, isolated from the read-only audit module the same way `inventory.py`'s own docstring already insists a template-safe audit module must stay read-only).
- Reuse `Parameter Combine.pushbutton/script.py`'s `ScopePickerApp` (`:655`), `pick_elements_in_view()` (`:804`), and `get_element_parameters_dict()` (`:96`) directly for scope selection and value display, rather than re-building a picker UI from scratch.
- `Advance.panel/Global Parameter Linker.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (audit grid + link/consolidate actions), `bundle.yaml`, `README.md`, `icon.png` — the same per-button file set every sibling pushbutton already ships.

**Future update:**
- Feed newly-created Global Parameters back into `Extract Template.pushbutton`'s own `_global_parameters()` read path so a template export documents which project standards are now centrally driven, closing the loop between this tool's writes and that tool's existing read-only report.
- A "break association" safety check — before any ordinary bulk-edit tool in this toolkit (Bulk Rename, FilterParameter, Parameter Combine) overwrites a parameter's value, warn when that parameter is currently Global-Parameter-associated, since a plain `SetValueString` silently severs the link with no native Revit warning today.
- Formula support — associate a parameter to a Global Parameter *expression* (e.g. `Typical Bay Width / 2`) rather than only a direct 1:1 link, once a modeler's naming/formula conventions for derived Global Parameters are established.

That read/write pair has never been generalized past that single parameter: a repo-wide grep for `GetTemplateParameterIds` and `IsParameterControlledByTemplate` across every non-vendored `.py` file returns zero hits anywhere outside ToggleLinked's own narrower call — nothing in this codebase ever asks "is this view's current graphic override actually what its assigned template says it should be" for any of the dozens of other template-controllable settings (category overrides, filters, view range, phase, detail level). And the repo's one naming-pattern rule engine, `rc_automation/naming_sheet.py`'s `PATTERNS` dict and `render(patterns, key, **values)` (`naming_sheet.py:30-40`, `:173-189`), is explicitly scoped to Column/Beam/Footing/Slab/Stair type names and schedule marks and has no concept of a view or a template at all — the already-logged Naming Convention Auditor idea's own Future-update line names "Sheets, Views and Grids" as an unbuilt extension of that exact engine, confirming no view-naming-convention tool exists yet anywhere in this repo. On the market, enforcing view-template assignment by naming rule, and catching drift once a template is assigned, is sold only as a line item bundled inside large per-seat production suites (CTC's view-template tools, IMAGINiT Utilities) or left to a modeler checking View Properties one view at a time with no rule table and no batch report at all.

**Description:**
`View Template Audit.pushbutton`, new sibling to `ToggleLinked.pushbutton` in `Essential.panel/Modify.stack` (same panel, since both already read `view.ViewTemplateId`):
1. **Define rules** — a small rule table (name-pattern → expected template), e.g. `*Framing Plan*` → `STR - Framing Plan`, `*Foundation*` → `STR - Foundation Plan`, matched first-match-wins against each eligible view's `Name`, mirroring the already-logged Workset Assigner & Hygiene Auditor's own condition → target row shape, stored the same way in a `view_template_rules.json` beside `script.py`.
2. **Scope** — every eligible view via `get_eligible_views()` (its first real production caller), or Active View / Selection, matching every other batch tool's scope picker.
3. **Audit pass** — for each view: resolve the expected template from the rule table and compare it against `view.ViewTemplateId`; where a template is already assigned, read every `BuiltInParameter` that template actually controls (generalizing `template_controls_links` from one hardcoded `VIS_GRAPHICS_RVT_LINKS` check to the full set `GetNonControlledTemplateParameterIds()` omits) and compare the view's live value against the template's own — a disagreement is reported as drift, not touched yet.
4. **Preview grid** — one row per view: current template / expected template / status (correct, wrong template, no template assigned, N parameters drifted), rows that disagree pre-ticked.

6. **Report** — assigned / already-correct / drift-fixed / exception-kept / failed counts, the same badge pattern every sibling tool already renders.

- New `anongee_toolkit.revit.view_templates` module: `get_template_controlled_params(template)` wrapping `GetNonControlledTemplateParameterIds()` the way `ToggleLinked.pushbutton/script.py:16-24` already does but generalized across every readable `BuiltInParameter` rather than one hardcoded id; `diff_view_against_template(view, template)` comparing each controlled parameter's live value; `resolve_expected_template(view_name, rules)` running the rule table the same first-match-wins way the Workset Assigner idea's own description already specifies.
- Rule storage as `view_template_rules.json` beside `script.py`, the same override-by-config convention `slab_convert_config.json` and `tag_sweep_config.json` already use.
- Scope via `anongee_toolkit.revit.views.get_eligible_views()`/`ALLOWED_VIEW_TYPES` (`revit/views.py:11-18,36-56`) — its first real caller anywhere in the repo.
- Remediation reuses `forms.alert`'s `OPT_EDIT_TEMPLATE`/`OPT_REMOVE_TEMPLATE` pattern already proven in `ToggleLinked.pushbutton/script.py:44-60`, extended with a third "keep as exception" branch calling `SetNonControlledTemplateParameterIds` the same way `release_links_from_template` (`:27-33`) already does, generalized per parameter instead of one hardcoded id.
- `Essential.panel/Modify.stack/View Template Audit.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (rule editor + scope picker + preview grid), `bundle.yaml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `icon.png` — the same per-button file set every sibling pushbutton already ships.

**Future update:**
- Fold the rule table into `rc_automation/naming_sheet.py`'s own `PATTERNS`/`render()` engine instead of keeping a second, parallel one, closing the already-logged Naming Convention Auditor's own named gap ("Sheets, Views and Grids") rather than answering it twice.
- Feed a confirmed-compliant view set into the already-logged View Graphics Sync as its "already matches, nothing to copy" baseline, so the two tools agree on what "correct" means instead of each deciding it separately.
- A read-only, re-run-later drift-check mode with no write at all — the same deferred mode View Graphics Sync's own Future update names for its view-to-view copies, run here against a template assignment instead of a one-shot source/target push.
- Sheet-level titleblock-assignment auditing on the same pattern, once the already-logged Sheet Set Builder idea's own sheet-naming convention exists to check assignments against.

**Idea name:** Reference-Angle Rotator — replaces `Rotate Column.pushbutton`'s own "spin however many columns you selected through 360°÷N, regardless of anything in the model" placeholder math with a real angle-snap that reads each element's nearest wall or grid and rotates onto it, generalized off columns to any point-located `FamilyInstance` (framing, generic models, MEP equipment, furniture) in one batch, preview-gated pass

**Potential:**
This is not a hypothetical gap in an unbuilt tool — it is the actual, shipped behaviour of a pushbutton already on the ribbon. `Essential.panel/Action.stack/Rotate Column.pushbutton/script.py` is two files total (`script.py` + `icon.png` — confirmed by `find`), the only pushbutton in the entire 33-script repo shipped without even a `bundle.yaml`, `README.md` or `CHANGELOG.md`, and reading its actual math shows why that matters: `filter_columns` (`:24-38`) restricts the selection to `OST_Columns`/`OST_StructuralColumns` only; `sort_columns_spatially` (`:49-59`) orders the selection by `(Y, X)`; and `rotate_column` (`:61-80`) is driven by `step_angle = 360.0 / total_columns` (`:109`) and `current_target_angle = step_angle * (index + 1)` (`:118`) inside the `main()` loop (`:116-121`). The rotation every column ends up at has zero relationship to any wall, grid, or the column's own current orientation — it is purely "divide a full circle by however many elements happen to be selected." Select 2 columns and they land at 180°/360°; select 3 and they land at 120°/240°/360°; select the same 3 columns again in a different order and they land somewhere else, because the target depends only on `total_columns` and sort position, never on geometry. A `grep -rniE "snap.*rotat|rotat.*snap|align.*wall|nearest.*wall" --include=*.py .` across the whole repo returns nothing that rotates an element onto a wall or grid angle — the only "rotated column" references anywhere (`cad2bim/beam_cleanup.py`, `cad2bim/__init__.py:1336`) are about a beam *end* snapping to an already-rotated column's centre point, never about setting the rotation itself. Meanwhile the actual angle math this fix needs already exists two folders over, unused for this purpose: `StrucBIM.stack/RoundElementDist.pushbutton/script.py`'s `angle_of` (`:115`), `angle_delta` (`:123`), `axis_from_angle` (`:128`), `element_normals` (`:133-168`) and `build_direction_groups` (`:169-202`) already read any element's real-world facing angle and group walls and columns "measured along their own normal" per the module's own docstring (`:20-26`) — but that tool only ever uses the angle to *measure* a distance and report it in a checklist dialog; it never calls `ElementTransformUtils.RotateElement`. `Rotate Column.pushbutton` calls `RotateElement` (`:76`) but never computes a real target angle. Two pushbuttons in the same panel, between them, already contain a complete "read the true angle → rotate onto it" pipeline that nothing in the repo connects. The real-world pain this leaves unsolved is routine: an angled façade bay, a non-orthogonal site boundary, a rotated grid, or a wall a modeler nudges a few degrees mid-project — every column, piece of framing, duct/pipe-mounted equipment or furniture family along it now needs re-rotating to match, one at a time, by eye, because Revit's native Align tool only works on 2D sketch edges and never rotates a placed 3D `FamilyInstance`. Nothing on the market closes this as a batch, preview-gated operation either — the closest public examples are one-off Dynamo forum graphs that rotate a single picked family to a single picked face, and the "align to element" command bundled in a few paid BIM utility packs is still a pick-pick, one-at-a-time operation, never a whole-selection batch with a report of what it found and why.

**Description:**
`Align to Reference.pushbutton` replaces `Rotate Column.pushbutton` in place (same `Action.stack` slot), keeping its working parts and fixing its broken one:
1. **Selection** — drop the `OST_Columns`/`OST_StructuralColumns`-only allowlist in `filter_columns` and accept any `FamilyInstance` with a usable location point or curve (columns, structural framing, generic models, MEP equipment, furniture, planting), so the fix covers the everyday non-structural case — a light fixture or piece of casework that needs to face a rotated wall — the same way it covers the structural one.
2. **Reference detection** — for each selected element, reuse `RoundElementDist`'s `element_normals`/`angle_of` to read the element's current facing angle, then collect every `Wall` and `Grid` within a configurable pick radius (default e.g. 3 m) via a bounding-box-filtered `FilteredElementCollector`, compute each candidate's own angle with the same `angle_of` helper applied to its `LocationCurve`/`Curve`, and pick the nearest one by angle delta (`angle_delta`) with physical distance as the tie-break.
3. **Preview grid** — one row per element: category, Mark/Id, current angle, matched reference (wall/grid name), target angle, rotation delta; an element with nothing inside the pick radius is reported as "no reference found" and left untouched rather than guessed at.
4. **Rotate** — ticked rows only, one `Transaction`, reusing `rotate_column`'s own `ElementTransformUtils.RotateElement` call with the axis derived from each element's own location instead of a shared index-based angle.
5. **Legacy mode** — an explicit "even split" checkbox keeps the original 360°÷N behaviour available for whatever radial-array case it may originally have been written for, so nothing that already depends on today's behaviour breaks on upgrade.

**Implementation:**
- Rewrite `Rotate Column.pushbutton/script.py`: keep `get_selected_elements`, `get_element_location_point`, and the `RotateElement` call inside `rotate_column`; replace `filter_columns`'s category allowlist with a point-located-`FamilyInstance` filter; replace `sort_columns_spatially` plus the `step_angle`/`current_target_angle` math with new `find_nearest_reference(doc, element, radius_mm)` and `compute_target_angle(element_angle, reference_angle)` functions.
- Port `angle_of`, `angle_delta` and `axis_from_angle` from `RoundElementDist.pushbutton/script.py:115-132` rather than re-deriving the trig, matching the repo's existing per-pushbutton, self-contained convention.
- Add the `Wall`/`Grid` `FilteredElementCollector` + bounding-box radius pass, scored by angle delta first and centre-to-centre distance second.
- New `ui.xaml` preview grid, `bundle.yaml`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` — the file set every sibling pushbutton in `Action.stack` (e.g. `Export Schedule.pushbutton`) already ships and this one alone is missing.
- `align_config.json` beside `script.py`: default pick radius, legacy-mode default (off), angle-delta tie-break tolerance.

**Future update:**
- Reference Planes and Levels as additional candidate datums, and a linked model's own walls/grids read through the link's transform, reusing the already-logged Linked Model Parameter Sync's cross-document transform math.
- Feed every "no reference found" row into a running model-health report in the style of the already-logged Naming Convention Auditor / Warning Auditor, so orientation drift becomes a tracked metric instead of a one-off fix.
- Curved wall / curved grid references (tangent angle at the nearest point) once the already-logged Curved Pad & Free-Form Peripheral Tie Placer's arc-handling work lands — the same recurring arc gap several other logged ideas already defer to it.
- Rigid-cluster rotation for joined elements, reusing `RoundElementDist`'s own union-find join clustering (`build_clusters`, `:392`) instead of rotating physically joined elements independently and breaking their joins.

## 2026-10-05 15:48 UTC

**Idea name:** Stray Note Recoverer — salvages the one-off construction instructions cad2bim's own text classifier is built to throw away, instead of letting them vanish the moment the CAD underlay is unlinked

**Potential:** Every TEXT/MTEXT/ATTRIB entity in a linked DWG becomes a `TextRecord` the moment `readers/dxf_reader.py:275` runs — unconditionally, regardless of layer — and `model.py:81-120` shows exactly what survives on it: `.text` (the raw sentence), `.point_internal` (Revit-feet location, filled in once the transform is known), `.rotation_deg` (filled at extraction, so a beam-aligned note keeps its angle), plus `.mark`/`.b_mm`/`.h_mm` which are populated *later*, only if `marks.parse_mark` recognises the sentence as a structural label. What happens to that record next is a closed, six-way fork: `classify/layers.py:167-187`'s `classify_text_layer()` routes a TEXT layer to one of five narrow structural categories — column/beam/grid/slab/foundation text, or a schedule table — or to `CATEGORY_TEXT_IGNORE` (`:170` for an unnamed layer, `:187` as the universal fallback for everything else), and `build_default_text_mapping()` (`:190-192`) pre-fills that per-layer verdict into the override dialog at `ui_window.py:1013-1079`. There is no seventh category for "this is a sentence a human needs to read and act on, not a dimension label." A drawing's general-notes layer, detail-callout layer or a bare layer-`0` scribble carries both kinds of text mixed together — the labels the five categories exist for, and the one-off instructions ("provide extra stirrups here", "as per detail X", a camber note) that aren't labels at all — and the layer-level choice is binary, so a whole layer's ignored texts are discarded with the layer, content unseen. The one place this toolkit *does* read free-floating sentences for meaning is `legend.py`, and its own module comments plus a real, measured corpus sentence prove the boundary exactly: `*A- INDICATE 20mm CAMBER TO BE PROVIDED IN BEAM` (test9) is read by `_LEGEND_TEXT` (`legend.py:92`, the bare verb `INDICATES?`) as a candidate row, and is then correctly, deliberately refused by the `_REACH_MM` (`:125`) mutual-nearest swatch-pairing rule because it "describes a beam, has no swatch of its own" (`legend.py:46-50`). `cad2bim.pushbutton/todo-list.md:1029-1053` names the same sentence as the reason the verb-matching rule has to stay tight, and three assertions in `tests/test_legend.py` (`:177-207`, `:636`) exist purely to prove the pipeline's output for it is empty: `self.assertEqual([e for e in entries if "CAMBER" in e["meaning"]], [])`. So the architecture has, correctly, decided this sentence is not a hatch meaning and not a structural label — and then does nothing else with it: it is not geometry, so it never reaches a builder (`grep -rn "TextNote" AnonGee.extension/lib/py3/anongee_toolkit/cad2bim --include=*.py`, excluding tests, returns zero hits — no cad2bim builder has ever created one in Revit); it is not a legend row, so it never reaches `findings.md`'s report-only path that *does* exist for legend-paired unknowns (`findings.md:164-230` — AR-CONC, ANSI32, ANSI37, RC-PARDI and "FLOATING COLUMN" are all "kept verbatim and only reported" once paired to a swatch). The practical cost is the thing every one of this repo's manual-cleanup ideas (Tag Sweep, Note Text Sweep, Warning Auditor) is written to describe: once a model goes from a CAD import to a working Revit file, the original annotation layers get unlinked or suppressed, and from that point on a camber note, a special-curing instruction, a "do not pour until grid line X is cast" callout, or any other one-off sentence a drafter left on a general-notes or detail layer has no trace in the model at all — not a `TextNote`, not a `Comments` value, not a line in a report — and the only way to know it ever existed is to re-open the original DWG and re-read every sheet by eye. On the market this is provably unreachable for free: the Revit API has no supported way to read text out of a linked CAD import directly — the only native workarounds are exploding the linked import, which destroys the live CAD reference this toolkit's own conversion depends on, or parsing the DXF directly, which is exactly the private machinery `dxf_reader.py` already has and nothing else in the free pyRevit ecosystem ships as a packaged tool. Paid tools that touch Revit text at all (Ideate BIMLink's annotation/"General Notes" features) operate on `TextNote`s already *inside* a Revit project, round-tripping them to Excel for bulk editing — they have no DWG-side import step and nothing to say about a sentence still sitting unconverted in a linked CAD file. Nothing free or paid reads a structural CAD drawing's orphaned annotation layers during BIM conversion and hands a structural modeler a reviewable, located, placed record of every sentence the geometry pipeline correctly declined to turn into an element.

**Description:** `Note Recovery.pushbutton` (new, `Core.panel/BIM.stack`, sibling to `BIMGeneration.pushbutton` and `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton`, callable either as an extra pass inside a `cad2bim.pushbutton` run or standalone against an already-converted project's original DXF). One window, run after the main conversion (or on demand later):
1. Re-reads the same `TextRecord`s `dxf_reader.py` already extracted (or re-parses the source DXF if run standalone), and discards anything already spoken for: any text whose `.mark` was set by `marks.parse_mark` (already a column/beam/footing/grid label), any text consumed as a legend row by `legend.read()` (already a hatch meaning, report-only or acted-on), and any text sitting on a layer the user mapped to one of the five structural text categories.
2. On what's left — the `CATEGORY_TEXT_IGNORE` leftovers — runs a small, deliberately narrow instruction-sentence filter (mirroring `legend.py`'s own "the verb carries the weight, not the wording" posture): a short, extensible word list (`PROVIDE`, `CAMBER`, `NOTE:`, `AS PER`, `TYP\.?`, `UNLESS NOTED`, `DO NOT`, `ENSURE`) catches imperative/instructional sentences and screens out title-block boilerplate and drafting-standard decoration, which stay unreported by design.
3. Presents every surviving sentence in a `ui/checklist.py`-style approve list: original text, source layer, DXF coordinate, and — a best-effort nicety, not a requirement — the nearest already-placed structural element (reusing `revit/geometry.py`'s bounding-box distance helper) so a camber note can be visually cross-checked against "the beam it's probably about" before the modeler accepts or skips it.
4. On accept, places a real, located Revit `TextNote` at `point_internal`/`rotation_deg` on a dedicated "CAD Import — Review" text type (and, where the nearest-element guess is confident and the user keeps it, additionally stamps a `Comments`-style parameter on that element) — so every surviving sentence either becomes something schedulable/visible in the model or is explicitly, visibly dismissed, instead of silently vanishing with the CAD link.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/cad2bim/stray_notes.py` (Revit-free, same posture as `legend.py`/`fold_plan.py`) — `find_stray_notes(texts, regions, legend_entries, text_mapping, reach_mm=...)` returning `[{text, layer, point, point_internal, rotation_deg, nearest_hint}]`; reuses `classify.layers.CATEGORY_TEXT_IGNORE` and the same mutual-reach posture `legend.py:125` already tuned, so a sentence close enough to be a legend row is never double-surfaced here.
- New `anongee_toolkit/cad2bim/builders/notes.py` — `place_stray_notes(doc, entries, text_type_id)` wrapping `TextNote.Create`, modeled on `builders/beams.py`'s outcome-dict convention (`created`/`skipped`/`errors`).
- `run_builders.py` gains `_create_stray_notes(doc, texts, regions, legend_entries, selections)` alongside `_create_grids`/`_create_beams`, called from the main conversion sequence.
- `ui_window.py` gains the approve/skip checklist screen, built on `ui/checklist.CheckList` (the same component `RoundElementDist`'s approve-each-fix flow already proves out).
- New `Core.panel/BIM.stack/Note Recovery.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `bundle.yaml`, `icon.png`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — for the standalone re-run case (a project already converted before this ships, or a re-check after someone edits the layer mapping).
- `cad2bim/tests/test_stray_notes.py`: reuses `test_legend.py`'s own test9 fixture — the camber sentence must now appear in `find_stray_notes()`'s output, while genuine legend rows, parsed marks and schedule-table text must not double-appear; a `regression_dxf_sweep.py` leg addition counts stray notes recovered per corpus fixture the same way `findings.md` already counts recovered geometry.

**Future update:**
- Feed the nearest-element hint from step 3 into the already-logged Rebar Callout Tagger or Tag Sweep machinery once either lands, so an accepted note becomes a proper leader-tagged annotation on its target element rather than a floating `TextNote`.
- Once the already-logged CAD2BIM Round-Trip Fidelity Auditor exists, register "every stray note accepted or explicitly skipped" as one more fidelity metric it reports, the same way it would already report recovered geometry counts.
- A saved per-project instruction-word list (the imperative verbs a given office's drafters actually use), following the same saved-profile posture already proposed for Parameter Migrator, Universal Renamer and Linked Model Parameter Sync.

This toolkit has built an enormous amount of rebar machinery and has, on its own admission, never once computed a real development length. `RC Automation.pushbutton/todo-list.md`'s own `SCOPE-4` records "laps and starter bars" as "explicitly out of scope and reported as such per column, so nobody mistakes the output for a complete cage" — and `anongee_toolkit/rc_automation/rebar_spec.py:682-688`'s `plan_column_mains()` docstring gives the actual reason in its own words: "Laps and starter bars are deliberately absent -- the plan says so, the report says so per column, and a bar that stops at the top of the pour is honest about being incomplete in a way a **guessed** lap length would not be." The one place in the whole idea log that does attempt a lap number — the already-logged Lap & Starter-Bar Continuity Auditor (2026-09-14 15:39 UTC) — says the same thing from the audit side: its lap rule is "expressed as a bar-diameter multiplier per condition (tension/compression), defaulting to common IS 456 detailing practice but explicitly labelled a configurable sanity threshold rather than a certified code check." Nobody in this repo has refused to guess because a real number is hard to find; they have refused because nothing anywhere computes one. The raw material is already half-entered and sitting unused: `anongee_toolkit/rc_automation/models.py`'s `FootingType` (`:232-247`) and `ColumnType` (`:265-278`) both carry a `concrete` field ("M25", "M30", ...) today, but it is a free-text string kept only "because it is what the matching engine compares against when deciding CONFLICT" (`models.py:226-229`) — never parsed into a numeric `fck` anywhere a grep for `fck`/`concrete_grade`/`Fe415`/`Fe500` across every non-vendored module confirms. `anongee_toolkit/structural/rebar_types.py`'s `bar_types()`/`bar_diameter_mm()`/`match_bar_type()` already resolve a project's real `RebarBarType` elements by diameter and name for every single bar RC Automation places, but never once reads a yield strength or any Material property off them — so even the one module that already holds a live reference to the real Revit bar-type element never asks it the one question a development-length formula needs. The precedent for exactly this shape of swappable, per-code formula table already exists and is proven in daily production: `BBS Generator.pushbutton/standards/` (`IS_2502_2019.py`, `BS_8666_2020.py`, `ACI_315_2018.py`, loaded through `standards/__init__.py:17-22`'s `get_standard(key)`/`available_standards()`) already ships per-code bend-diameter and bend-deduction tables (`IS_2502_2019.py:20-35`) in exactly this swap-by-code-standard shape — it has simply never been extended past bar bending into bar anchorage. On the market, a bar-diameter/grade/condition development-length or lap-length calculator inside Revit does not exist as a free or standalone tool at all: it is either absent from Revit entirely, done on a calculator/spreadsheet by hand (the universal real-world practice), or bundled as one invisible step inside a full paid structural-design run (RCDC, ETABS/SAFE's own detailing output) or a paid, seat-licensed rebar-detailing suite (AGACAD, Naviate Structure) — nothing free computes the formula itself and hands it back wired to a Revit schedule's own grade fields.

**Description:**
A small calculation module first, a pushbutton second — `Development Length Calculator.pushbutton` (new, `Dev.panel/col1.stack`, beside `BBS Generator.pushbutton`, whose `standards/` package it reuses directly):

2. **Output** — straight development length `Ld` in mm; a separate **lap length**, since a lap is two bars sharing `Ld` scaled by IS 456 Cl. 26.2.5.1's 1.3×/2× factors depending on what fraction of bars are lapped at one section; a separate **anchorage credit** for a standard 90°/135° hook, computed by calling straight into BBS Generator's own bend-deduction table (`IS_2502_2019.py:30-35`) so a hooked anchorage is never double-counted against a straight `Ld` a second time.
3. **Batch preview grid** (the same checklist shell every QA tool in the repo already runs on) — one row per diameter/grade/condition combination a modeler is checking, not a single value typed and read once.

- `Dev.panel/col1.stack/Development Length Calculator.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (grade/diameter/condition inputs + preview grid), `bundle.yaml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `icon.png`.
- `tests/test_development_length.py`: hand-checked IS 456 `Ld` values for a spread of (diameter, M20/M25/M30, Fe415/Fe500, tension/compression) combinations against published reference tables, asserting the formula matches to the nearest mm.

**Future update:**

- Extend to beam top/bottom bar curtailment lengths (a bar terminated mid-span, not at a storey joint) once a beam-bar placer exists to check it against.
- Wire the new `parse_grade()` helper into the already-logged Design-Force Reinforcement Compliance Checker, so that tool's required-vs-provided comparison reads the same grade numbers this calculator does instead of two independently-typed sources for the same project fact.

**Idea name:** Section-Placement Normalizer (Y/Z Justification & Offset Auditor) — a batch, model-wide fix for the exact "ninety beams inherited the wrong offset" bug this toolkit has already hit in production and only ever patched going forward, in one narrow creation path, never for an element already in the model or placed by a modeler's own hand

**Potential:** `structural/framing.py:191-216`'s `_state_the_justification(instance, offset_mm)` exists purely because of a real, witnessed incident the module's own docstring quotes verbatim: "a real run arrived with `z Offset Value` of −1500 — the foundation level, from somewhere else entirely in the model, carried into ninety beams because nothing said otherwise" (`framing.py:195-197`). The root cause is a documented Revit API behaviour, not a one-off: `NewFamilyInstance` gives a new beam "whatever the family and the **last placement** left behind" (`framing.py:194`) — Y/Z Justification, Y/Z Offset Value are ambient state that leaks from whatever was placed immediately before, in-session, regardless of category or who placed it. `cad2bim/builders/beams.py:40-79`'s `_sink()` documents the same parameter from the opposite angle — the owner's own instruction, quoted verbatim, that "its sunk value should use Z Offset Value only for sunk or rise not the Start/End Level Offset" (`beams.py:43-44`), with a worked example of the exact failure this repo shipped once: "a beam that should have been 150 down had not moved at all" (`beams.py:47`) because the Start/End Level Offset fields looked right in the Properties palette while `Z_OFFSET_VALUE` silently carried the wrong number. Both fixes are **write-once, at creation, inside one pipeline** — `framing.create()` (the RC Automation/Bridge path) and `cad2bim/builders/beams.py` (the CAD-import path). A repo-wide grep for `JUSTIFICATION`/`OFFSET_VALUE` confirms the fix never reached further: it appears only in those two files. `structural/columns.py:252-276`'s `create()` sets `FAMILY_BASE_LEVEL_OFFSET_PARAM`/`FAMILY_TOP_LEVEL_OFFSET_PARAM` (the level offsets) but never once reads or writes any Justification or cross-section Y/Z Offset parameter — the identical ambient-inheritance bug framing.py went to the trouble of narrating is, for every structural column this toolkit places or a modeler places by hand, completely unaddressed. And neither fix helps the normal daily case at all: a modeler who draws a beam or stands a column with Revit's own native tool — which is most elements in most projects, this toolkit's cad2bim/RC-Automation pipelines notwithstanding — gets whatever justification/offset the last element left in Revit's placement memory, with no code anywhere checking it afterward. Today, noticing a beam or column sits oddly off its grid line in section/3D means opening Properties on that one element, finding Y Justification/Z Justification/Y Offset Value/Z Offset Value buried below the visible Level Offset fields, and resetting them by hand — repeated element by element, with no way to even see which of hundreds of elements disagree with the house convention. Native Revit has no batch view of these four parameters at all, and no commercial add-in (Ideate, CTC, Avail) surfaces cross-section Y/Z Justification/Offset as an auditable, batch-correctable set — only full-suite QA platforms touch anything adjacent, and only as a side effect of a clash report, never as a direct parameter check.

**Description:** `Section Placement Auditor.pushbutton` (Essential.panel/Bulk Tool.stack, beside `Copy Rebar Visibility`/`Obscured Rebar`) collects every `OST_StructuralFraming` and `OST_StructuralColumns` `FamilyInstance` in the model (or selection), reads its `YZ_JUSTIFICATION`/`Y_JUSTIFICATION`/`Z_JUSTIFICATION` and `Y_OFFSET_VALUE`/`Z_OFFSET_VALUE` parameters, and compares each against a configurable house convention — defaulting to exactly the five-value tuple `_state_the_justification` already encodes (Uniform/Origin/Top, Y-offset 0, Z-offset 0) — flagging any element that disagrees. A beam flagged with a non-zero `Z_OFFSET_VALUE` is cross-checked against `cad2bim/builders/beams.py`'s own sunk-beam convention (a deliberate drop, reported as "intentional — matches a sunk/stepped slab pattern" rather than a defect) before it is offered for correction, so the tool never "fixes" a legitimately sunk beam back to flush. Every other disagreement goes into a preview grid — element, category, mark, current vs. house-standard value per parameter — nothing written until rows are ticked, then one `Transaction` resets exactly the flagged parameters, leaving Level/Top-Level and their offsets (the member's actual position) untouched.

**Implementation:** `anongee_toolkit/structural/section_placement.py` (new): `read_placement(instance)` wrapping the same `BuiltInParameter` reads `_state_the_justification` already writes; `audit(doc, category_filter)` collecting via the same `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfCategory(...).OfClass(FamilyInstance)` pattern `framing.placed()`/`columns.placed()` already use (`framing.py:219-241`, `columns.py:279-300`); `is_intentional_sink(instance, tol_mm)` reusing `cad2bim/beam_cleanup`'s split/level data to recognize a deliberately sunk beam; `normalize(doc, instance, convention)` applying the correction inside the caller's transaction, mirroring `_state_the_justification`'s own five `_set()` calls (`framing.py:205-209`) but now callable against any existing element, not only one just created. `section_placement_config.json` beside `script.py` for the house convention values and the sink tolerance, matching the override-by-config shape `railing_config.json`/`drop_panel_config.json`-style sibling tools already use. New pushbutton `Essential.panel/Bulk Tool.stack/Section Placement Auditor.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `bundle.yaml`, `icon.png`, preview-grid UI matching `ConvertFloor`'s checklist-then-commit pattern. `tests/test_section_placement.py`: a synthetic beam carrying the exact `-1500` `Z_OFFSET_VALUE` from `todo-list.md`'s BUG-29 incident, and a synthetic sunk beam from `cad2bim`'s own fixture set, asserting the first is flagged and the second is reported "intentional" and left alone.

**Future update:**
- Extend the same read/normalize pair to `OST_Walls` once a wall-specific justification convention is agreed (walls carry their own `WALL_KEY_REF_PARAM`-style centerline justification, a different parameter set this v1 deliberately leaves out).
- A "freeze convention" mode that snapshots today's correct elements' values as the house standard automatically, for a project that never wrote one down.

This idea's action is auditing and normalizing those four section-placement parameters directly, independent of any level change, for both beams and columns — a different operation on an overlapping but distinct parameter set.

`Railing Placer.pushbutton` lands in `Essential.panel/Bulk Tool.stack`, beside `Copy Rebar Visibility.pushbutton` and `Obscured Rebar.pushbutton` — the stack this repo already uses for whole-model, run-once-per-discipline batch passes — and runs in three independent, checkbox-selectable source modes against one shared placement engine:

Four separate files, three subsystems (cad2bim's CAD reader, the structural placement layer, the RC Automation workbook model), all already know a footing can sit on a pile cap — and a repo-wide check shows that is the full extent of it: `grep -rniE "\bpile\b|PileCap|PileFoundation" AnonGee.extension --include=*.py`, excluding vendored `lib/py3/ezdxf`, `openpyxl`, `numpy`, `pandas`, `fontTools`, `tzdata` and `PIL`, returns exactly six hits — every one of them a comment or docstring using "pile cap" as context for a *footing's* outline, never a `BuiltInCategory`, a `FamilyInstance` creation call, a workbook sheet, or a schedule row for a pile. The placement primitive a pile needs already exists next door and unused for this: `structural/columns.py:252-275`'s `create(doc, point_mm, symbol, base_level, top_level=None, base_offset_mm, top_offset_mm)` is exactly "stand a vertical structural `FamilyInstance` at a point, constrained by two elevations" — a pile differs from a column only in which direction its "top" and "bottom" mean (cap soffit down to founding depth, not storey to storey), not in the Revit API call needed to place one.

The everyday cost this leaves open: a modeler on any piled-foundation job (basements, high column loads, soft soil — exactly the multi-storey RC buildings this toolkit already targets with `BIMGeneration.pushbutton` and RC Automation) gets every isolated pad, combined pad and pile-cap outline from the existing pipeline in one pass, and then has to work out the pile layout underneath each cap entirely by hand: read the pile diameter and safe working capacity off the structural note, divide the column's factored load by one pile's capacity to get a count, lay the piles out on a grid honouring the standard minimums (centre-to-centre spacing ≥ 3× pile diameter, edge distance ≥ 1.5× diameter from the cap edge), and place each one individually — repeated per cap, per level, across the whole foundation plan, with no schedule produced afterward and no idempotent re-run if the layout changes. Nothing in the repo does this, and nothing free on the market does either: RISAFoundation, Tekla Tedds and SAFE's pile-cap design modules compute a layout but are paid structural-calculation suites sold and licensed independently of Revit; the handful of Revit-native "deep foundation" add-ins on the Autodesk App Store place piles from a grid the user draws by hand, never compute spacing, count or capacity themselves, and are paid.

**Description:**
A new sibling pushbutton, `Pile Layout.pushbutton`, in `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack/` beside `ConvertFloor`/`DrawFloor`, backed by a new `PILE_TYPES`/`PILE_PLACEMENT` sheet pair RC Automation can read the same way it already reads `FOOTING_TYPES`/`FOOTING_PLACEMENT`:

1. **Input** — a picked pile-cap `Floor` (one `footings.py` already placed) or its outline read straight from a `FootingPlacement.outline` (`models.py:456`), plus a pile type's diameter, safe working capacity (kN) and founding depth from a small `PILE_TYPES` sheet shaped like `FOOTING_TYPES` already is.
2. **Layout** — pile count from the cap's column load ÷ one pile's capacity, rounded up (minimum 1 under an isolated cap, minimum 3 on a triangular grid under a corner/edge cap, per common code practice); piles placed on a square or triangular grid inside the cap outline honouring the 3×-diameter spacing and 1.5×-diameter edge-clearance minimums above, walking the outline's own vertices the same way `rc_automation/rebar_spec.py`'s `scan_segments()`/`region_breaks()` already walk a footing's polygon to keep a bar off a re-entrant corner — reused here to keep a pile off one instead of inventing a second polygon-edge engine.
3. **Place** — one `FamilyInstance` per pile via the exact pattern `columns.py:252-275` already runs (`NewFamilyInstance` + `StructuralType.Column`, or `.NonStructural` for a generic pile family), with `base_offset_mm`/`top_offset_mm` set to founding depth and cut-off level instead of storey height.
4. **Schedule** — one `PILE_PLACEMENT` row per pile (mark, parent cap mark, diameter, founding RL, cut-off RL) written back into the same workbook RC Automation already reads, matched and updated by mark on a re-run instead of duplicated, the same idempotency every `FOOTING_PLACEMENT` row already has.

**Implementation:**

- `anongee_toolkit/rc_automation/pile_layout.py` (new): `grid_layout(outline_points_mm, pile_diameter_mm, min_count)`, a triangular/square grid generator inside an arbitrary polygon built on the same point-in-polygon and edge helpers `cad2bim/slab_graph.py` already exports (`_point_in_ring`, `_signed_area`, both already imported into `foundation_plan.py:81-82`) rather than a third copy of that math.
- `rc_automation/models.py`: new `PileType`/`PilePlacement` dataclasses mirroring `FootingType`/`FootingPlacement` (`models.py:450-462`); `SHEET_PILE_TYPES`/`SHEET_PILE_PLACEMENT` constants beside `SHEET_FOOTING_*` (`models.py:58-63`); pulled into `MODE_CREATE_ALL`'s `_CORE_SHEETS` only for a project whose `FOOTING_TYPES` row is flagged piled (one added boolean column, not a new mode).
- `excel_engine.py`: grid parsing for the two new sheets, reusing `parse_outline()` (`excel_engine.py:135-147`) for the cap outline a layout computes against.
- New pushbutton `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack/Pile Layout.pushbutton`: the same modeless shell `ConvertFloor`/`DrawFloor` already use, with a pile-type picker and a preview grid before placement (the same preview-before-commit step `Parameter Combine` already runs).
- `tests/test_pile_layout.py`: a synthetic rectangular cap and a synthetic L-shaped cap outline, asserting the computed grid holds both the 3×-diameter spacing and 1.5×-diameter edge clearance, and that pile count matches a hand-checked load/capacity ratio.

**Future update:**
- Pile-cap bottom-mat reinforcement sized against the real pile reaction points (a point-load check) rather than the uniform-bearing check `rebar_spec.py` runs today, once piles exist in the model as real, positioned elements for it to read.

**Idea name:** INP/FRAMEWIN "Walls" Section Import — closes the one structural category both `.inp` importers already parse past but never create, so a lift-core or stair-core shear wall arrives with the rest of the frame on the same one-click import instead of being the one element type a modeler must still trace by hand off a printed PLANWIN/FRAMEWIN plan

**Potential:**
This repo has two independent, fully-built importers that turn a PLANWIN/FRAMEWIN `.inp` analysis export into a Revit RC frame — `BIM.stack/BIMGeneration.pushbutton` (`core.py` + `parser_service.py`, the actively-maintained one with its own UI) and the older standalone `BIM.stack/FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py` — and both already know the `.inp` file format has a fourth structural category beyond Columns/Beams/Slabs, because both reference `'Walls'` by name: `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py:217-219`'s three `_parse_section(lines, start_kw, stop_kws)` calls and `parser_service.py:129-131`'s three mirrored `isolate_structural_category(...)` calls both list `'Walls'` only as a **stop token** — the marker that tells the parser where the `Slabs` block ends — and neither ever calls either parsing function *with* `'Walls'` as the `start_kw`/`primary_heading` itself. A full-file grep confirms the gap is total, not partial: `grep -rniE "place_wall|_place_wall|wall_symbol|OST_Walls|NewWall|WallType" AnonGee.extension/AnonGee.tab/Core.panel/BIM.stack --include=*.py` returns zero hits across both pushbuttons — `core.py` has `get_structural_columns`, `get_structural_framings` and `get_floor_types` (`core.py:72-88`) and matching `_place_column`/`_place_beam`/`_place_slab` creators (`core.py:209-362`), but no `get_wall_types`/`_place_wall` pair exists anywhere, and `parser_service.py:extract_schematics` (`parser_service.py:125-165`) returns a dict with exactly `'columns'`/`'framings'`/`'slabs'` keys — never a `'walls'` key — so even if a wall block were parsed, nothing downstream would consume it. The daily cost is concrete and recurring: almost every multi-storey RC building this toolkit targets has at least a lift shaft or stair core modelled as shear walls in the structural engineer's PLANWIN/FRAMEWIN analysis run alongside its columns and beams, and today a modeler who runs either importer gets a complete, levelled, joined frame for everything *except* those walls — which must still be measured off the original printed/PDF structural plan and drawn one at a time with Revit's native wall tool, the one step in an otherwise one-click import that stays fully manual, and the one place a core wall's centreline or thickness can silently drift from what the engineer actually modelled. On the market, FRAMEWIN/PLANWIN's own Revit link (and the generic STAAD/ETABS-to-Revit links sold as paid CSI/Bentley interoperability add-ons) carries walls across because it owns both ends of the exchange; nothing free reads a plain FRAMEWIN `.inp` text export and places its walls the way this repo already does for columns, beams and slabs.

**Description:**
No new pushbutton, no new panel — both existing `.inp` importers gain the one category they already tokenize but never build, following the exact column/beam/slab pattern already proven in each file:

1. **Parse** — `isolate_structural_category(normalized_content_texts, 'Walls', [])` (and `FramewinToBIM`'s equivalent `_parse_section(lines, 'Walls', [])`) is called a fourth time, since the function's quad-point-block grammar (name → thickness-or-height value → up to 4 coordinate rows) is category-agnostic already — a `Walls` block in a FRAMEWIN `.inp` export uses the same shape, just with wall thickness where a column's `dimension` field carries storey height. `extract_schematics` gains a `WallEntityContext` dataclass (name, base/top elevation in metres, thickness, and the two base-face points a wall's `Location.Curve` needs) and a `'walls'` key in its returned dict, built the same way `ColumnEntityContext` is today (`parser_service.py:134-142`).
2. **Type resolution** — a new `get_wall_types(doc)` mirrors `get_structural_floor_types`/`get_structural_columns` (`core.py:72-88`) to list loaded structural `WallType`s in the picker UI, with the same "auto-pick the one whose name/material reads CONCRETE" scoring `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py:118-138`'s `auto_pick_symbol` already does for columns and beams — reused, not reinvented, since a wall's compound structure is resolved the same way `_resolve_or_duplicate_floor_type` (`core.py:147-187`) already resolves a floor's, just keyed on thickness instead of layer width.
3. **Placement** — a new `_place_wall(doc, wall_data, base_wall_type, level_cache)` mirrors `_place_beam`'s shape (`core.py:240-283`): resolve/duplicate a `WallType` by thickness via `WallType.Duplicate` + `CompoundStructure.SetLayers` (the same pattern `_resolve_or_duplicate_floor_type` already runs), then `Wall.Create(doc, Line.CreateBound(base_pt, top_pt_or_base_pt2), wall_type.Id, level.Id, height, 0, False, structural=True)` for a structural shear wall — called from `_run_generation` (`core.py:416-470`) in the same per-category loop already placing columns, beams and slabs, with the walls' own elevations folded into the existing `z_elevations` level-building pass (`core.py:427-434`) so no new level logic is needed.
4. **Joining** — walls join into the existing bounding-box-overlap join pass (`core.py:474-490` / `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py:916-932`) as a fourth element list alongside columns/beams/floors, reusing `_bounding_boxes_overlap`/`try_join_ordered` exactly as written today.

**Implementation:**
- `BIMGeneration.pushbutton/parser_service.py`: add `WallEntityContext` dataclass; call `isolate_structural_category(..., 'Walls', [])` inside `extract_schematics` and add the `'walls'` key to its returned dict.
- `BIMGeneration.pushbutton/core.py`: add `get_structural_wall_types(doc)` (mirrors `get_floor_types`, `core.py:80-88`), `_resolve_or_duplicate_wall_type(base_wall_type, thickness_mm, wall_type_cache)` (mirrors `_resolve_or_duplicate_floor_type`, `core.py:147-187`), and `_place_wall(doc, wall_data, base_wall_type, level_cache)` (mirrors `_place_beam`, `core.py:240-283`); wire the new per-wall loop and join pass into `_run_generation` (`core.py:416-490`); extend `execute_generation_protocol`'s signature with `wall_type` alongside `col_symbol`/`beam_symbol`/`floor_type`.
- `BIMGeneration.pushbutton/ui.xaml` + `script.py`: add a fourth type picker (Wall) beside the existing Column/Beam/Floor pickers, auto-selected the same concrete-detection way the other three already are.
- `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py`: same four changes inline (`_parse_section(lines, 'Walls', [])`, `auto_pick_symbol`-style wall-type scoring, a `get_wall_type`/wall-placement block mirroring `get_col_type`/column placement at `script.py:582-596` and `696-746`, folded into the existing TX3 join pass at `script.py:916-932`), keeping both importers at parity the way they already are for columns/beams/slabs.
- Regression case: a `.inp` fixture with a two-sided lift-core (4 wall segments forming a rectangle) at two storeys, asserting the resulting Revit walls are structural, land on the correct levels with the correct thickness, and join cleanly to the slabs above and below — plus a re-import pass asserting walls get the same create-or-update-by-name idempotency columns/beams/slabs already have, not duplicated on every run.

**Future update:**
- Door/opening cut-outs where a FRAMEWIN wall segment carries an opening sub-record, once a real `.inp` sample exposing that sub-format is available to parse against.
- Feed newly-created walls into the already-logged BOQ & Material Take-off Excel export (`FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py:946-1057`'s post-process block) as a fourth quantity sheet, so wall concrete volume and formwork area get costed the same pass columns/beams/slabs already do.
- Once wall geometry exists from this import, give the already-logged Rebar Joint Clash & Congestion Checker and Reinforcement Density Heatmap ideas a wall host to check and colour, the same way they already treat columns, beams and slabs as hosts today.

## 2026-10-02 15:42 UTC

**Idea name:** Parameter Combine — Reference Parameter Support (Level / Material / Phase / Design Option / Type) — fixes the one `StorageType` `Parameter Combine.pushbutton`'s own formula, find/replace, affix and sequence engine has always silently mishandled, so a modeler can finally batch-reassign a Base Level, a Structural Material, a Phase or a Family Type the same one-click way every text and number field already works today

**Potential:**
`Parameter Combine.pushbutton` is this repo's most powerful single-document batch parameter editor — four modes (Formula, Replace, Affix, Sequence), a live preview grid, per-row apply flags — but it hand-rolls every read/write function itself rather than importing `anongee_toolkit` at all (confirmed: `grep -n "^import\|^from" "AnonGee.tab/Advance.panel/Parameter Combine.pushbutton/script.py"` shows only `clr`/`os`/`re`/`math`/WPF imports, no `anongee_toolkit` line), and that hand-rolled code has a total, untested blind spot on `StorageType.ElementId`. `extract_parameter_value` (`script.py:106-125`) branches on `requires_number`, `is_yesno_parameter`, then `StorageType.Double`/`.Integer`, and falls through to `return parameter.AsString() or ""` for anything else — but `AsString()` on an ElementId-storage parameter (Base Level, Top Level, Phase Created/Demolished, Design Option, Structural Material, or any shared parameter typed Family Type) returns `None` on every Revit version, so today a `{Base Level}` or `{Structural Material}` token in a formula silently evaluates to an empty string instead of erroring — the preview grid shows a blank, not a warning, and a modeler has no way to know the source token they picked is simply unreadable by this tool. `setup_ui_data` (`script.py:266-286`) makes the problem worse before it starts: it offers *every* non-read-only parameter name as a valid `TargetParamCombo` entry, Level/Material/Phase/Type fields included, with no `StorageType` filter at all. The write path then fails outright: `on_apply_click`'s commit loop (`script.py:866-872`) branches only on `.Double` (unit-converts then `param.Set(float(...))`) and `.Integer` (`param.Set(int(float(preview_val)))`), and the final `else: param.Set(str(preview_val))` is reached for an ElementId-storage target — but `Parameter.Set` has no string overload for that `StorageType`, so Revit raises an `ArgumentException` the script's own `except Exception as e: print(...)` (`script.py:873-875`) swallows per-element, reporting only "some elements failed, check pyRevit console" with no indication the entire target category can never succeed. A repo-wide check confirms this is a real, already-named gap rather than an edge case nobody hits: the already-logged Multi Filter Parameter — ElementId Write Support (2026-09-27) and Cross-Element Parameter Copier (2026-09-23) both document the same `StorageType.ElementId` write gap in their own two sibling tools, but neither touches `Parameter Combine.pushbutton` itself, and Parameter Migrator (2026-09-13) routes around the problem entirely by going through `anongee_toolkit.revit.parameters.get_parameter_value`/`set_parameter_value` (`parameters.py:36-113`) instead — infrastructure that is already fully `StorageType.ElementId`-aware (`parameters.py:57-64` read, `:106-109` write) and sitting unused by the one tool that would benefit most from it, since it never imports the package. The everyday cost is concrete: after a level insertion-point revision, a material spec change, or a phasing correction, a modeler who has already built a Parameter Combine formula/sequence run for a batch of elements' text and number fields has to switch tools entirely — to One/Multi Filter Parameter's bracket-encoded dropdown, or a fully manual per-element edit — the moment the same batch also needs its Level, Material, Phase or Type reference touched, because the one tool built for exactly this kind of multi-row, previewed, formula-driven batch edit cannot see or write that one `StorageType` at all. On the market, Ideate BIMLink and CTC BIM Project Suite can batch-write a reference parameter, but only by round-tripping through an exported spreadsheet under a paid, seat-licensed add-in, and neither offers a live in-canvas formula/sequence preview the way this repo's own tool already does for every other `StorageType`; nothing free closes this specific gap.

**Description:**
No new pushbutton, no new UI chrome — `Parameter Combine.pushbutton`'s existing four-mode window gains the one `StorageType` branch it has always been missing, end to end:

1. **Read side** — `extract_parameter_value` (`script.py:106-125`) gains an `ElementId` branch ahead of its final string fallback: resolve `parameter.AsElementId()` to the referenced element and return its `Name` (falling back to `parameter.AsValueString()` for a built-in reference Revit names without a real element, e.g. a Phase), so a `{Base Level}`/`{Structural Material}` token in a formula finally reads the real current value instead of silently going blank.
2. **Target picker** — `setup_ui_data` (`script.py:266-286`) tags each candidate target name with its `StorageType` (a small side-dict, mirroring the pattern the already-logged Multi Filter Parameter idea proposes for its own value map) so the UI can show a reference icon/tooltip next to Level/Material/Phase/Type entries instead of offering them identically to a plain text field.
3. **Write side** — `on_apply_click`'s commit loop (`script.py:866-872`) gains an `elif param.StorageType == DB.StorageType.ElementId` branch *before* the catch-all `else`: resolve the computed `preview_val` string to a real `ElementId` by name-matching it against the target parameter's own valid candidate set (every `Level` in the document for Base/Top Level, every `Material` for a material reference, every `Phase` for Phase Created/Demolished, every `ElementDesignOptionSet` option for Design Option, every `FamilySymbol` in the element's own category for a Family-Type reference — each enumerated with the plain `FilteredElementCollector` calls `structural/levels.py`, `structural/columns.py` and sibling modules already run elsewhere in the repo), then `param.Set(resolved_id)`; an unmatched name is reported in the existing per-element error list instead of raising an uncaught `ArgumentException`.
4. **Ambiguity/validation** — a computed value that matches zero or more than one candidate is flagged in the preview grid exactly the way a numeric target already flags a non-numeric preview (`on_apply_click`, `script.py:639-644`), so a bad formula is caught before the transaction opens, not after it partially commits.

**Implementation:**
- `Parameter Combine.pushbutton/script.py`: add `resolve_reference_candidates(doc, target_param, category_id)` (one dispatch per reference category, reusing existing collector patterns rather than inventing a new one) and `resolve_name_to_elementid(name, candidates)`; wire both into `extract_parameter_value` (read) and the `on_apply_click` commit loop (write) as the two new branches described above.
- Prefer routing the actual get/set through `anongee_toolkit.revit.parameters.get_parameter_value(..., as_string=False)` / `set_parameter_value` (`parameters.py:36-113`) rather than re-deriving ElementId handling a third time in the repo — this would be the first of the three parameter-editing pushbuttons (`One`/`Multi Filter Parameter`, `Parameter Combine`) to actually import `anongee_toolkit`, closing the "never imports the package" gap the Potential section above confirms by grep.
- `TargetParamCombo`/`SourceParamCombo` items become a small `(name, storage_type)` tuple-backed list instead of plain strings, with a `StringFormat`/converter in `ui.xaml` so the combo still displays plain names.
- Regression case: a formula of `"{Type}"` targeting another element's `Structural Material` parameter across a mixed Column/Footing selection, asserting the resolved Material matches by name and that an unmatched name (a typo, or a material only present in one of the two categories) lands in the error list rather than throwing mid-transaction.

**Future update:**
- Promote `resolve_name_to_elementid` into `anongee_toolkit.revit.parameters` itself once proven here, so the already-logged Multi Filter Parameter — ElementId Write Support and Parameter Migrator ideas can both drop their own bracket-id/by-id matching in favour of one shared, by-name resolver.
- Feed a resolved-but-ambiguous Family-Type match into the already-logged Family/Type Swap Wizard (2026-09-29) as its one-element preview step, rather than that tool needing to build its own name-matching pass from scratch.
- Once Level references round-trip cleanly, give the already-logged Level Rehost (2026-09-24) and Phase Assignment Auditor (2026-09-25) ideas a working, previewed bulk-reassignment front end to land their own computed values through, instead of each needing its own write path.

The gap is not academic. Every new project a firm starts needs its office's 30-80 shared parameters rebound to whatever categories that job actually uses; every time the office's own shared-parameter file gains a field (a new COBie requirement, a new identity code, a new QA field), every *active* project needs the same rebinding again. Revit's native Shared Parameters / Project Parameters dialogs do this one definition, one category set, one click-through at a time — there is no native "import a parameter list" path at all. Doing this by hand, repeatedly, across many projects and many parameters, is exactly the kind of repetitive, easy-to-get-subtly-wrong setup task this repo has automated everywhere else it appears (grid setup, level setup, type creation) but never for the parameter-binding step itself. It is also the precise upstream cause of the failure mode the already-logged Shared Parameter GUID Doctor (2026-09-18) exists to *detect*: that entry's own Potential section explains that "a shared parameter is identified by its GUID, not its name," and that a project ends up with two different definitions reading the same name "from two different `.txt` shared parameter files: one from the office master, one baked into a vendor family... or last year's project template" — a mismatch created at exactly the moment someone manually recreates a parameter instead of reusing the office master file's existing definition. `element_params.py`'s own `_text_definition()` (lines 245-256) already guards against this for its own seven names by reusing a same-named definition already in the open shared-parameter file rather than creating a second one; nothing in the repo offers that same GUID-safe reuse behaviour to any *other* parameter a modeler needs bound, which is every parameter outside that one hardcoded set. On the market, bulk/templated shared-parameter provisioning exists only as one dialog deep inside paid, seat-licensed suites — CTC Software's BIM Project Suite ships a dedicated Shared Parameter tool, Ideate Software's BIMLink can push parameter setups as part of a much larger paid bundle — nothing free turns a plain parameter list into a batch-bound, GUID-safe set of project parameters the way this repo's own `element_params.py` already proves is possible for one hardcoded case.

**Description:**
`Parameter Pack Provisioner.pushbutton` (new tool, `Advance.panel`, sibling to `Parameter Combine.pushbutton` and — if it ships — `Shared Parameter GUID Doctor.pushbutton`, the panel that already owns document-level parameter operations rather than per-element geometry ones):

1. **Pack file** — a plain spec table (JSON or an `openpyxl`-read `.xlsx`, both libraries already bundled under `lib/py3/`) listing, per row: Name, Data Type (Text / Integer / Number / Length / Area / Volume / YesNo / URL / MultilineText...), Instance or Type, Parameter Group (defaulting to Identity Data), and Categories (a comma list of category names, or "All"). Ships with one starter pack that is byte-identical in content to today's hardcoded `ALL_PARAMETERS`/`CATEGORIES` pair — so the existing RC Automation behaviour becomes a documented, editable data file instead of a buried module constant — plus a blank template for a firm to author its own office-standard pack.
2. **Load & probe** — pick a pack, resolve its category names against `doc.Settings.Categories`, and show a live preview per row using the same present/missing split `bound_names()` already computes: Already bound (green), Will create (yellow), Category not in this project (greyed, skipped rather than failed).
3. **Mode** — reuses `MODE_FILL` / `MODE_CREATE` / `MODE_SKIP` verbatim (`element_params.py` lines 72-78); the decision a modeler needs to make is identical to the one RC Automation already asks, just over an arbitrary parameter list instead of a fixed one.
4. **Apply** — one `Transaction`; for every row not skipped, reuse (or create, GUID-safe) the external definition and bind it with the row's own type/instance-or-type/group/categories instead of the module's current hardcoded choices.
5. **Report & save-back** — created / already-bound / failed counts per row, and an option to write the pack back out (JSON/Excel) with anything resolved during the run, so a firm's parameter pack becomes a versioned file that travels with the project template rather than a one-off click-through only one person remembers doing.

**Implementation:**
- Generalize `structural/element_params.py` additively, not as a breaking refactor: extract `_text_definition()` into a `_definition(group, name, spec_type)` parameterized over any `SpecTypeId` instead of hardcoded `SpecTypeId.String.Text`; widen `ensure(doc, names, categories)` to accept `specs` (name + data type pairs), `categories`, `instance=True` and `group=GroupTypeId.IdentityData` as real parameters instead of the current module-level `ALL_PARAMETERS`/`CATEGORIES` constants — RC Automation's existing call site (`RC Automation.pushbutton/script.py:482`, `element_params.ensure(doc, missing)`) keeps working unchanged by calling the widened function with today's defaults.
- Move the generalized functions into `anongee_toolkit/revit/parameter_bindings.py`, alongside the existing `anongee_toolkit/revit/parameters.py`, so RC Automation and the new pushbutton share one implementation instead of RC Automation keeping a private copy — avoiding exactly the "one function, two silently-diverging implementations" pattern the already-logged Shared Parameter GUID Doctor entry documents elsewhere in this codebase (`bounding_boxes_overlap`, `_bracket_int`).
- New pushbutton reads its pack via the bundled `openpyxl`/`json`, builds its preview off the generalized `bound_names()`, applies via the generalized `ensure()`; same modeless `CheckList`/`hostwnd`/theme shell every other batch tool in the repo already runs on.
- Ship `packs/rc_automation_identity.json` (mirrors today's hardcoded set exactly) and `packs/template.json` (blank) inside the pushbutton folder; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`/icon, same version-bump-and-`CHANGELOG.md` convention every pushbutton here follows.

**Future update:**
- Pre-flight hook: any tool about to create a shared parameter (RC Automation, BBS Generator, a future rebar/wall tool) calls this module's GUID-safe `_definition()` first, the same inline-warn hook Shared Parameter GUID Doctor's own future-update list already proposes — now with an actual provisioning tool on the other end of it instead of only a repair tool.
- Cross-project batch mode: point the tool at a folder of project files and provision the same pack across every active job in one pass, so an office shared-parameter revision reaches the whole firm in one run instead of once per project opened by hand.
- Un-bind / retire mode — the mirror operation, removing a pack's bindings from categories that no longer need them, the one direction native Revit's own dialog already supports that this tool's create-first v1 would not.
- Read an office's existing shared-parameter `.txt` file directly (parsing its own `*GROUP`/`*PARAM` rows) as a pack source, so a firm's real shared-parameter file can drive this tool with no format conversion at all.
