**Potential:**
A repo-wide check makes the gap total rather than assumed: `grep -rn "PathReinforcement\b" AnonGee.extension --include=*.py` returns zero hits anywhere in the roughly 110 Python files under `anongee_toolkit` and every pushbutton script, and the only trace of the underlying Revit category is passive, not a placement path — `ConvertFloor.pushbutton/script.py:245-249` builds `CAT_REBAR` from `("OST_Rebar", "OST_AreaRein", "OST_PathRein", "OST_FabricAreas", "OST_FabricReinforcement")` purely so a slab conversion doesn't orphan reinforcement that's already there, and `script.py:1378-1379` calls `r.SetHostId(doc, new_el.Id)` on each dependent the same way for all five categories — nothing in the repository ever *creates* a `PathReinforcement`. This is a different gap from the one the already-logged Slab Fabric/Mesh Reinforcement Placer (2026-09-26) closes: that entry's own title and Potential section scope it explicitly to `FabricSheet`/`AreaReinforcement`, quoting `RC Automation.pushbutton/todo-list.md:330-332`'s SCOPE-5 verbatim — *"`FabricSheet` / `FabricArea` for slabs"* — and its own grep checks (`AreaReinforcement\b`, `FabricSheetType|NewAreaReinforcement|FabricArea(`) never touch `PathReinforcement` at all. SCOPE-5 is RC Automation's only named reinforcement gap for slabs, and even it doesn't mention this API — `PathReinforcement` is a gap the toolkit's own roadmap has never put into words, let alone scoped.

The absence matters because mesh/area reinforcement and support-line reinforcement answer two different structural questions. `AreaReinforcement` lays a uniform top/bottom mat across a whole panel; the extra top bars a continuous slab needs locally over every beam or wall it spans onto — to resist the negative (hogging) moment a uniform mat under-reinforces — are a second, independent layer, conventionally a handful of extra bars running a fraction of the span out from each support face. Every bar this toolkit has ever placed, across every category — footings, columns, beams, walls — funnels through exactly one Revit creation call: `rebar_factory.create_bar()` (`structural/rebar_factory.py:344-378`) wraps `Rebar.CreateFromCurves` (`:364`) and nothing else; `structural/rebar_run.py`'s `plan_footings()`/`place_footing()` (`:118,221`) and its column/beam/wall siblings all stage a `BarSpec` and hand it to that one function. `PathReinforcement.Create` is a structurally different API — it creates its own rebar-container element across a swept region rather than one shape-driven bar per call — and nothing in `rebar_factory.py`, `rebar_types.py` or `rebar_hosts.py` has ever been pointed at it. `structural/rebar_types.py` already proves the pattern this needs for a brand-new type class — `bar_types()`/`match_bar_type()`/`unresolved_bar_types()` (`:58,90,114`) resolve a `RebarBarType` by name hint and report what can't be matched rather than guessing — but has no `PathReinforcementType` equivalent. And the gap isn't bridge-specific the way Slab Fabric/Mesh Reinforcement Placer's is: `commands/slabs.py` already computes which beam sits on which panel edge, by name, inside `_beam_widths()` (`slabs.py:212-250`) — but only for a panel it just placed itself off a `BEAM_PLACEMENT` sheet, inside the walled garden of one RC Automation Excel run. A slab built by `cad2bim`, modelled by hand, or placed by any route other than that specific bridge pipeline gets no equivalent read at all — and there is no `structural/floors.py` or `structural/slabs.py` module in the package to give it one (`ls AnonGee.extension/lib/py3/anongee_toolkit/structural/` lists `columns.py`, `footings.py`, `framing.py`, `grids.py`, `levels.py`, `stairs.py` and the rebar modules — no floor-aware module of any kind).

The manual cost is routine and per-project: every continuous RC slab in a real building needs this layer, and today a modeler opens Revit's own native Path Reinforcement tool — pick one face, sketch one path, set a layout, repeat — once per supported edge, per panel, on every floor, cross-checking span and support width against the drawing by eye each time. On the market, the closest equivalents are the same paid whole-suite rebar add-ins the sibling entry already names (AGACAD's Rebar for Revit / RC Structural Detailer product line, ProStructures), whose additional/trimmer-bar tooling is still a manual, host-by-host sketch inside their own UI, not a batch pass driven off detected geometry; nothing free turns "this edge of this panel sits on that beam" into a placed `PathReinforcement` without a human doing it one edge at a time.

**Description:**
`Slab Support Bar Placer.pushbutton` (new tool in `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack`, sibling to `ConvertFloor.pushbutton` and `RoundElementDist.pushbutton` — the stack this repo already treats as home for geometry-driven, preview-gated batch edits to built structural elements, following the same posture Expansion/Seismic Joint Duplicator and Bay Fill already established there):

1. **Scope** — Selection / Active view / Whole document, picking `Floor` elements on Structural categories only (the same three-way picker `AutoLevel.pushbutton` already offers, reused rather than reinvented).
2. **Detect supports** — for each panel, walk its boundary edges and test each against every Structural Framing (`OST_StructuralFraming`) and Structural Wall in the model for footprint overlap within a configurable tolerance band, the same X/Y-overlap-then-measure shape the already-logged (but not yet built) Headroom & Soffit Clearance Auditor's proposed `nearest_soffit_above` would use for its own, differently-pointed question — here used to find what's *underneath* an edge rather than what's below a point. A beam/wall whose centreline runs parallel to and under the edge, within tolerance, is a detected support; whether it continues past the panel on both ends (true interior support, bars both faces) or stops at the panel (an end span) is read from the supporting element's own extent and reported, not guessed.
3. **Bar spec** — diameter, spacing, top cover and a projection length expressed as a fraction of the panel's own span perpendicular to that edge (default configurable, e.g. L/4), entered once per run or per edge-width bucket; a resolved `RebarBarType` and `PathReinforcementType` picked from what's already loaded in the project, same "resolve up front, stop rather than guess" discipline `unresolved_bar_types()`/`unresolved_cover_types()` (`rebar_types.py:114,220`) already enforce for every other bar category.
4. **Preview** — the same `CheckList` shell every other batch tool in this repo runs on: panel mark/name, supporting beam or wall, detected span, proposed bar diameter/spacing/projection each side, one tick per row; a row whose support type can't be resolved lists as unresolved, loudly, rather than silently skipped.
5. **Apply** — ticked rows placed via `PathReinforcement.Create` inside one `TransactionGroup`, one row at a time with per-row rollback on failure, the same posture `Convert Slab.pushbutton` already follows for its own pre-flight-report-then-commit runs.
6. **Report** — placed / unresolved / skipped counts, exported through the same `openpyxl` path `Export Schedule.pushbutton`/`BBS Generator.pushbutton` already use.

- New `structural.rebar_types.path_reinforcement_types(doc)` / `match_path_reinforcement_type(doc, name_hint)` / `unresolved_path_reinforcement_types(doc, rows)`, following `bar_types()`/`match_bar_type()`/`unresolved_bar_types()` (`rebar_types.py:58,90,114`) exactly, since `PathReinforcementType` resolution is a new type-class the toolkit has never looked up.

**Idea name:** Headroom & Soffit Clearance Auditor — cross-references the linked architectural model's doors, stair flights and corridor paths against the host structural model's beam and slab soffits through the link's own transform, flagging every spot where a structural member drops lower than the clear height a door head, stairwell or corridor actually needs, closing the one axis every structural-vs-architecture coordination pass in this toolkit still does by eyeballing a section cut: vertical clearance, checked across a document boundary, as a number instead of a look

**Potential:**
This toolkit already crosses two kinds of boundaries separately — category (`Convert Slab.pushbutton`, already-logged Convert Column ⇄ Wall) and document (the already-logged Linked Model Parameter Sync, 2026-09-23 15:42, which is still only *proposed*: it names the gap outright — "closing the one axis none of the repo's parameter tools has ever crossed: a value that lives in a *different* Revit document" — and its own research confirms the gap is total: a repo-wide grep for `RevitLinkInstance`/`GetLinkDocument` across every `script.py` and every `anongee_toolkit` module returns **zero hits anywhere in `AnonGee.extension`** (re-confirmed here), and `ToggleLinked.pushbutton` — the repo's only other link-adjacent tool, 69 lines total — never instantiates `RevitLinkInstance` at all, only flips `BuiltInCategory.OST_RvtLinks` view visibility via `SetCategoryHidden`. Neither axis has been combined with the one geometric question every RC structural team answers by hand on every project with an architectural link: does a beam or slab soffit drop below the clear height a door, a stair flight or a corridor actually needs? Today that's a modeler cutting a section through the link at every suspect corridor/stair/door, in both models at once, eyeballing whether the beam sits clear — a check that is only ever run where someone already suspects a problem, never exhaustively, because exhaustively means a section at every opening on every level. The two already-logged ideas that get closest both stop short of it by their own stated scope: Linked Model Parameter Sync only ever *copies a parameter value* across the link boundary, it never compares two documents' geometry against each other — its own run, by design, "is never written to" on the link side and never evaluates a spatial relationship stronger than "which element matches which"; and already-logged Sleeve & Opening Coordinator (2026-09-22 10:39) does read a second, MEP-side model's geometry and resolve a structural clash from it, but only for things physically *penetrating* a structural member (a pipe/duct crossing a beam, sized against a beam-depth ratio) — a door head sitting too close under a beam never intersects the beam's solid at all, so no boolean/bounding-box "crossing" test that tool runs would ever fire on this case; the finding here is purely a vertical-gap measurement between two things that don't, and shouldn't, touch. The one function already sitting in the toolkit that looks adjacent — `anongee_toolkit.revit.geometry.bounding_boxes_overlap()` (`geometry.py:40-59`, exported from both `anongee_toolkit/__init__.py:108` and `anongee_toolkit/revit/__init__.py:13`) — answers the wrong question for this: it is a 3-D any-overlap boolean, and the correct outcome for almost every door/beam pair in a well-designed building is that their bounding boxes do **not** overlap in Z at all; what this idea needs instead is the signed vertical gap between the top of an opening/headroom datum and the underside of whatever structural member sits above the same XY footprint, which no function in `revit/geometry.py` computes today. On the market, this exact check exists only as one output mode buried inside paid whole-discipline clash-detection platforms (Navisworks Clash Detective's own "clearance" test type, Solibri's Clearance ruleset) that run against an exported/aggregated federated model rather than live inside Revit against a project's own linked architectural file, and none of them are free; nothing free runs a live, in-Revit, link-aware headroom sweep and hands a structural modeler a plain list of which beam soffit to raise, or which door/stair layout to flag back to the architect, before a site RFI finds it first.

**Description:**
`Headroom Auditor.pushbutton` (new tool in `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack`, sibling to `Convert Slab.pushbutton` and `RoundElementDist.pushbutton` — the two tools whose pre-flight-report-before-you-touch-anything posture it borrows wholesale, with nothing here ever writing to the structural model it only reports on):

1. **Pick the link** — same dropdown-of-`FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(RevitLinkInstance)` picker Linked Model Parameter Sync's own proposal already specifies, labelled by the linked file name, an unloaded link greyed out with why.
2. **Pick what needs headroom** — tick categories to check on the link side (Doors by default via `OST_Doors`, Stairs via `OST_Stairs`, optionally Rooms/Spaces along a tagged "Corridor" department/name-pattern for a flat clear-height sweep rather than a per-opening one) and a required clear height per category (door: head height already implied by the door instance's own geometry, so this is really a *tolerance*; stair: a configurable code-minimum headroom, e.g. 2100 mm, checked along the flight's own going line, not just at top/bottom; corridor: one flat configurable minimum over the whole tagged area).
3. **Pick what might be in the way** — structural categories on the host side (Structural Framing, Floors, Structural Foundation for transfer slabs), pre-selection or whole-model.
4. **Match & measure** — for each link-side opening/flight/corridor-area element, transform its relevant top-of-clearance point(s) (a door's head-height points along its width, a stair flight's going line sampled every tread, a corridor area's boundary sampled on a grid) into host coordinates via the link's own `GetTotalTransform()` (the exact combine-a-link-transform-with-a-point step Linked Model Parameter Sync's own proposed `link_geometry` module already plans to build, reused here rather than re-invented), then for each point finds every host structural element whose bounding box overlaps that X/Y and whose `BoundingBoxXYZ.Min.Z` sits below it, and reports the smallest such gap to the point's own required clear height — positive (clear), zero-or-negative (clash), with a configurable warning band in between (e.g. within 25 mm of the minimum, so a fix made for one trade's tolerance doesn't silently re-fail another's).
5. **Preview report** (not a checklist with an Apply button — there is nothing in this model to change) — one row per flagged point/opening: which link element, which host structural element, the clear height required, the actual gap, severity (`Error` below zero, `Warning` inside the band), and a jump-to-element action that selects the host element and opens a 3-D view framed on both it and the link-side element so the two are seen together without either model needing to be opened separately.
6. **Export** — the same per-row report to Excel via the `openpyxl` path `Export Schedule.pushbutton`/`BBS Generator.pushbutton` already use, so the list can be sent back to the architect as-is.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit.revit.link_geometry` module shared with (and, if that idea lands first, simply reused from) the already-logged Linked Model Parameter Sync: `host_point_from_link(link_instance, link_point)` wrapping `RevitLinkInstance.GetTotalTransform().OfPoint()`, the repo's first real use of `RevitLinkInstance`/`GetLinkDocument()` for anything beyond this idea and that one.
- New `anongee_toolkit.structural.clearance` module: `door_head_samples(door_instance)` (width-wise sample points at head height, from the door's own `BoundingBoxXYZ.Max.Z` and location curve/width), `stair_going_samples(stairs_element, headroom_mm)` (points along each flight's walking line via `Stairs.GetStairsRuns()`/`StairsRun.GetStairsPath()` offset up by the configured headroom), `corridor_grid_samples(room_or_area, spacing_mm)`; and `nearest_soffit_above(doc, point_xy, z_above, categories)` — a new, narrower sibling to `bounding_boxes_overlap()` (`geometry.py:40-59`) that tests X/Y containment only and returns the lowest `Min.Z` among candidates, since that function's own any-axis boolean can't express "ignore Z, then measure the Z gap that's left."
- Reuses the same `CheckList`/`hostwnd`/`progressbar`/`theme` modeless shell and `openpyxl` export path every other batch/report tool in the repo already runs on; config (`headroom_config.json`: per-category clear-height defaults, warning band, corridor grid spacing) mirrors `slab_convert_config.json`'s override-by-config shape.
- Report-only by construction: no `Transaction` is ever opened against either document, so this is the one tool in the StrucBIM stack with no undo story to get right, because there is nothing to undo.

**Future update:**
- Pair with the already-logged Link Position Guard (2026-09-16 15:40): warn before a headroom sweep runs against a link transform flagged moved/stale since the baseline it last passed.
- Feed confirmed clashes into the already-logged View Range Manager/Section Batch Generator so a flagged point gets its own cropped section view auto-generated for the issued coordination set, instead of only the jump-to-element camera this run shows live.
- Extend `nearest_soffit_above` past Doors/Stairs/Corridors to Ceiling-datum sweeps (MEP's own clear-zone-above-ceiling question, mirroring how already-logged Sleeve & Opening Coordinator's penetration geometry could share a crossing-detector with a future MEP headroom mode).

On the market, automatic door/window recognition is a headline feature of paid CAD-to-BIM and scan-to-BIM suites, and it is built almost exclusively around vector door-swing-arc blocks in a clean architectural CAD standard — a shape this corpus doesn't reliably carry, which is exactly why `wall_plan.py` reaches for a gap-width histogram instead of block matching. Nothing free, and nothing else in this repo, turns a gap it already has to compute anyway into a placed opening.

**Description:**
1. **Recover the gap** — in `_merge_collinear`'s bridging branch (`wall_plan.py:343-348`), append the bridged interval to a new `axis["gaps"]` list (`(lo=hi, hi=r_lo, mid, z, layer)`, same internal-feet frame the rest of the module already uses) instead of only widening `hi`; thread that list through `_face()` so each finished face — and, downstream, each `_pair_faces()`/`_wall_segment()` result — carries its own recovered openings next to `start`/`end`/`width_ft`, the same shape `plan_walls` already returns segments in today.
2. **Classify** — convert each gap's length back to millimetres (`config`'s existing `ft`↔`mm` helpers) and bucket it: below the wall module's own noise floor, drafting noise; roughly 600–1050 mm, single-leaf door; roughly 1050–1800 mm, double-leaf door or a wide window; wider, and on an arch-category wall, a shaft/lift-access opening, matching `report.py`'s own observation that "an architectural door is wider than a lift-core access" (`:91-92`). Where a door/window mark ("D1"/"W1") sits in the DXF text near the gap, resolve it through the same text-to-geometry proximity pattern `stair_text.py` already uses for stair marks, so a classified type carries the drawing's own tag rather than a guess.
3. **Preview** — one row per recovered gap in the same checklist-and-confirm grid every other builder in this package dry-runs through: host wall, resolved width, proposed category, and a type pick-list seeded from whatever Door/Window families are already loaded in the project, falling back to duplicating a seed placeholder type sized to the recovered width — the exact "duplicate a seed type" move `ConvertFloor.pushbutton` and `BIMGeneration.pushbutton` both already make for sizes a project doesn't carry yet. A gap on a wall CRIT-2's thin-column stand-in still owns, or whose width straddles two buckets, lists as `skipped`, loudly, the same stated principle `builders/walls.py` already follows for widths a compound structure refuses.
4. **Place** — one `NewFamilyInstance(host_wall, level, family_symbol, structural_type)` per confirmed row, positioned at the gap's midpoint projected onto the wall's placed `LocationCurve`, inside the same `TransactionGroup` `_create_walls` already opens around `walls.place_walls`.

**Implementation:**
- `wall_plan.py`: extend the bridging branch as above; define the classification width bands beside `_COLLINEAR_BRIDGE_MM` so "what counts as a door" is set once — this is also the moment to fold `report.py`'s independent, currently-duplicated `_CORE_WALL_DOOR_MM` into the same constant instead of two numbers (1300 vs 700) doing the same job under different names.
- New `anongee_toolkit/cad2bim/builders/openings.py`, sibling to `builders/walls.py`, taking `place_walls`'s created wall ids paired with their planned segments' `openings` lists, and doing the classify/preview/place steps above.
- `run_builders.py`'s `_create_walls` gains one call to the new builder immediately after `walls.place_walls` returns, inside the same transaction group and behind the same `result["skipped"]`/`result["errors"]` reporting shape every other builder call already feeds into `report.py`.
- Regression cost is close to zero: the 17 fixture DXFs `WORK-9`'s 714-unit-test gate already exercises are the exact corpus the door-gap histograms in `wall_plan.py:76-92` were tuned against, so the same fixtures become the opening-recovery test set with no new drawings needed, following `test_wall_plan.py`'s existing structure.

**Future update:**
- Feed a recovered D1/W1 mark into `naming.py`'s existing template engine so a placed opening's Mark parameter carries the drawing's own tag instead of Revit's auto-numbered default.
- SCOPE-3 (P6 Annotation) and SCOPE-4 (P7 Rebar) both need door/window state to exist before tagging or lintel/sill reinforcement around an opening can be planned — this is what either would read first.
- Share a placement-and-report engine with the already-logged Sleeve & Opening Coordinator, so an architectural opening and an MEP-driven structural sleeve go through one preview grid instead of two.
- Check WORK-3's existing slab-opening handling before extending gap-recovery to `slab_outlines.py`/`foundation_plan.py` — that item already claims openings for slabs, so any follow-on here should scope strictly to the wall-hosted case this tool actually leaves unsolved.

**Idea name:** Type Catalog Builder — reads or writes a loadable family's external `.txt` type-catalog file directly from the `FamilyManager`, closing the exact limitation Type Matrix Generator's own entry (2026-09-11 10:45) names and explicitly declines to fix: "Revit's own answer, type catalogs, only works for loadable families... nothing turns [an Excel round-trip and a type-name matcher] into a general type factory" for that half of Revit's type system, and the one Revit document kind — the family document itself — this entire repo has never once opened

**Potential:**
Every tool this toolkit ships, and every tool already logged in this file, operates on a *project* document: `FilteredElementCollector(doc)`, `Element.Duplicate`, `ElementType.Duplicate`, all of it reading and writing types that already live inside an open `.rvt`. A repo-wide check makes the gap exact rather than assumed: `grep -rniE "FamilyManager|OpenDocumentFile|IFamilyLoadOptions|\.rfa\b|EditFamily" AnonGee.extension --include="*.py"` returns zero real hits — every match is vendored `pythonwin` noise (`lib/py3/pythonwin/pywin/framework/*`, a Win32 MFC demo library, not Revit code) — confirming that no script in this repo has ever called `Application.OpenDocumentFile` on an `.rfa`, read `Document.FamilyManager.Types`, or touched `Document.EditFamily()`. That absence matters because type catalogs are the one place Revit's own content system already solves the "18 types from a spreadsheet" problem Type Matrix Generator was written to fix for system families — but only if the family ships a correctly-formed external `<FamilyName>.txt` next to its `.rfa`, and nothing here, or in Revit's own UI, builds that file for you. A modeler who wants one today either hand-writes the tab-delimited text (the header row's `Parameter##UNIT` tagging, e.g. `Width##MILLIMETERS`, has to match the family parameter's own name, group and unit exactly or Revit silently drops the column on load) in Notepad or Excel-saved-as-tab-text, one row per type, with no validation until the family fails to load or loads with the wrong types — or gives up and keeps every size as a full in-family type, which is exactly the bloat this repo's own units module shows nobody here has tooled around yet: `anongee_toolkit/revit/units.py` (`:13-16`) is a hand-rolled `FT_TO_MM = 304.8` / `CF_TO_M3` constant table, not a wrapper over Revit's real `UnitUtils`/`ForgeTypeId` (2021+) or `DisplayUnitType` (pre-2021) API — it converts mm/ft/m for the toolkit's own structural math, but has no notion of a family parameter's actual `FamilyParameter.GetUnitTypeId()`/unit symbol, which is precisely what a catalog's `##UNIT` tag has to get right per parameter, per Revit version. A firm with a large parametric family — a footing type, a rebar coupler, a precast panel, a door/window family with 40 size variants — pays for that bloat every time the family is loaded: every type sits fully instantiated inside the `.rvt`, inflating file size and load time, when a catalog would keep one lean family definition and let Revit instantiate only the rows a project actually places. On the market this is a known, recurring content-management pain: a handful of free one-way Dynamo graphs circulate on forums (generate-only, no validation, no harvest, no re-import), and paid content-library suites (e.g. certain BIM content-management add-ins sold by CAD resellers) bundle catalog authoring as one line item inside a much larger, seat-licensed package; nothing free or otherwise documented in this repo's own market notes offers a validated, round-trip harvest → edit → regenerate cycle, let alone the "shrink the family back down once the catalog is proven" step below.

**Description:**
`Type Catalog Builder.pushbutton` sits in the same new `TypeTools.stack` (`Advance.panel`) Type Matrix Generator's own entry proposes, as its family-document-level sibling — one tool factories project types, this one factories the external file Revit's loadable-family half of the type system actually reads.

1. **Open the family document** — pick a loaded family already in the project (opened read/write via `Document.EditFamily()`, the exact API call this repo has never used) or browse to an `.rfa` on disk (`Application.OpenDocumentFile`, opened detached and not saved back unless the modeler chooses to). Either path lands on a `Document` where `doc.IsFamilyDocument` is true and `doc.FamilyManager` is live.
2. **Harvest** — enumerate `FamilyManager.Types` and, for each, every `FamilyManager.Parameters` value via `FamilyType.AsDouble()`/`AsString()`/`AsInteger()` keyed by `FamilyParameter.Definition.Name`, resolving each numeric parameter's real display unit through `FamilyParameter.GetUnitTypeId()` (2021+) or `DisplayUnitType` (pre-2021) rather than assuming feet — the exact per-parameter unit lookup `units.py` does not do today. Rows preview in the same `CheckList` grid shell (Element/Type name, one column per parameter, resolved unit) every other batch tool in this repo already runs on, tick which parameters and which types to export.
3. **Generate the catalog text** — write the tab-delimited `<FamilyName>.txt` next to the `.rfa`: header row `##<ParamName>##<UNIT_TOKEN>` per numeric column (unit token resolved in step 2), a bare header for text/yes-no columns, one row per type starting with the type name, values written in the catalog's declared unit — not Revit's internal feet — exactly as Revit's loader expects. A dry-run mode renders the exact bytes in a preview pane before anything touches disk.
4. **Generate from matrix (reverse)** — load a CSV/XLSX (the same `openpyxl` path `Export Schedule.pushbutton`/`BBS Generator.pushbutton` and Type Matrix Generator's own proposal already use) mapping rows to new family types; for each row, either **write directly into the catalog text** (fast path, family itself untouched) or **create the type inside the family first** via `FamilyManager.NewType()` + `FamilyManager.Set(param, value)` inside a `Transaction` on the family document, then harvest that type out to the catalog the same way step 3 does — giving a modeler a way to build the first few types visually in the Family Editor and let the tool take over once the pattern is proven.
5. **Slim the family** — once a catalog is generated and confirmed loadable (a real load-and-place smoke test against a scratch project, reported pass/fail per type), offer to delete the now-catalog-covered types back out of the `FamilyManager` and save the `.rfa`, shrinking a family that shipped 40 baked-in types down to the handful the office actually keeps as in-family defaults — the exact "fat family → lean family + catalog" migration this repo has never had the family-document access to attempt.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/revit/family_documents.py` (first family-document module anywhere in `lib/py3/anongee_toolkit/revit/`, sibling to `parameters.py`/`units.py`): `open_for_edit(app, family_or_path)` wrapping `Document.EditFamily()` / `Application.OpenDocumentFile()` behind one call; `harvest_types(fam_doc, param_names)` walking `FamilyManager.Types`/`Parameters`; `resolve_unit_token(param)` doing the real `GetUnitTypeId()`/`DisplayUnitType` → Revit catalog unit-string mapping `units.py` has never needed before; `write_catalog(path, header, rows)` / `read_catalog(path)` for the plain tab-delimited I/O (UTF-16 per Revit's own catalog encoding requirement, no external dependency).
- `FamilyManager.NewType()` + `Set()` path wrapped in a `Transaction` scoped to the *family* document, not the host project — the one transaction target nothing else in this repo has ever opened.
- Matrix ingestion reuses the `openpyxl` reader and the name-template tokenizer proposed for Universal Renamer / Type Matrix Generator, so a shared token formatter serves all three once any one of them lands.
- Load-and-place smoke test: load the regenerated family into a disposable, in-memory-only scratch document (`Application.NewProjectDocument`), place one instance per catalog row, report failures, then discard the scratch document without saving — proving the catalog is loadable before the "slim the family" step deletes the only copy of that data still living inside the `.rfa`.
- Same modeless `hostwnd`/`CheckList`/`progressbar`/`theme` shell, `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`/`CHANGELOG.md` convention every pushbutton in this repo already follows.

**Future update:**
- Two-way live diff: re-harvest an already-catalogued family's current `.txt` against its `FamilyManager` defaults and flag drift, the same "sheet vs model, report disagreement" posture already proposed for Naming Convention Auditor and Schedule Drift Reconciler.
- Firm-standard catalog library: save a matrix + base-family pairing once (mirroring Type Matrix Generator's own logged "cross-project type set" future update) so a catalog rebuild is a re-run, not a re-author, every time a size range changes.
- Feed harvested family-parameter tables into the already-logged BOQ & Cost Estimator so a catalog-driven family's cost rows stay keyed to the same parameter names a rate card references.
- Batch mode: point the tool at an entire office family library folder and regenerate every family's catalog in one pass, closing the loop with the already-logged Family Library Sync's own master-library folder scan.

**Idea name:** Note Text Sweep — model-wide find-and-replace across every `TextNote`'s actual paragraph content, with a formatting-safety flag, closing the one everyday annotation chore this toolkit has only ever read text for and never once edited: fixing a repeated general note, spec clause or typo everywhere it appears instead of sheet by sheet

**Potential:**
Every one of this repo's 29 existing tools that touches text does one of two things: it *renames* an element's own identity field (Bulk Rename's Fill Pattern/Line Pattern/Line Style names, or Universal Renamer's already-logged token-template rename across sheets/views/levels/grids/schedules), or it *reads* drawing text purely to extract data from it — `AutoLevel.pushbutton/anongee_autolevel/revit_ops.py:176-186` collects every `TextNote` in the active view or the whole document (`FilteredElementCollector(doc[, view.Id]).OfClass(TextNote).WhereElementIsNotElementType()`) and reads `element.Text` (`:201-205`) purely to parse a level mark like "FFL +3.500" out of it — the value is only ever consumed, never written back; nothing in that script, or anywhere else in the repo, ever calls a `TextNote`'s `Text` setter. A repo-wide check confirms this is a genuine, total gap: `grep -rli "textnote" AnonGee.extension/AnonGee.tab AnonGee.extension/lib/py3/anongee_toolkit` returns exactly two files — `AutoLevel`'s read-only scan above, and `Parameter Combine.pushbutton/script.py`, whose only `TextElement` hits (`ForegroundProperty`/`FontWeightProperty`) are the unrelated WPF UI text-styling class from `System.Windows.Documents`, not a Revit `TextNote` at all. There is no `anongee_toolkit/revit/text_notes.py`, no annotation module of any kind in `lib/py3/anongee_toolkit/revit/` (which today holds only `parameters.py`, `elements.py`, `filtering.py`, `selection.py`, `views.py`, `geometry.py`, `transactions.py`, `units.py`, `compatibility.py`, `application.py`) — every "batch edit text" tool this repo has logged or shipped edits an element's *name*, never a note's *sentence*. Yet the everyday failure mode this leaves open is one every structural office hits repeatedly: a general/typical note gets pasted onto 40, 80, sometimes 150 sheets across a set (a rebar-cover callout, a code-year reference like "as per IS 456:2000", a disclaimer, a revision instruction), and the day that clause changes — a code edition updates, a client's standard boilerplate wording changes, or a typo is spotted after issue — a modeler opens every sheet that carries it and edits the note by hand, one click, one retype, one sheet at a time, trusting memory (or a sheet-by-sheet grep of printed PDFs) to find every occurrence, with no report at the end proving none were missed. Revit itself has never closed this: there is no native model-wide Find/Replace for `TextNote` content (Find/Replace on the ribbon works inside schedules and a handful of other list views, never a document-wide sweep of annotation text), and `TextNote` cannot be scheduled the way a Type or a tagged parameter can, so an Ideate-BIMLink-style "edit in Excel" path is closed to it too. On the market, this exact feature exists only inside CTC Software's paid **BIM Project Suite** ("Find and Replace" module, subscription-gated, bundled with dozens of unrelated tools) and inside a handful of other paid whole-suite add-ins (Avail, some CAiCE/Naviate bundles); nothing free does a previewed, formatting-aware, model-wide text-note sweep, and writing one from scratch today means a bespoke Dynamo graph or pyRevit script most modelers don't have the Python/API background to build or trust.

**Description:**
`Note Text Sweep.pushbutton` lands in `Essential.panel/Bulk Tool.stack`, beside `Bulk Delete.pulldown`/`Bulk Rename.pulldown` — the stack this repo already treats as home for whole-model, ticked-preview batch edits, now covering annotation content instead of style/pattern names.

1. **Scope** — Selection / Active view / Whole document, the exact same three-way picker `AutoLevel.pushbutton` already offers (`revit_ops.py:169-187`) and the same collector call, reused verbatim rather than re-invented: `FilteredElementCollector(doc[, view.Id]).OfClass(TextNote).WhereElementIsNotElementType()`.
2. **Find** — a literal string or a regex pattern, with case-sensitive and whole-word toggles; every note whose `Text` contains a match is collected, capped at the same `MAX_TEXT_SCAN` ceiling AutoLevel's own module constant already sets for a document-wide sweep, so a huge model degrades to "truncated, refine your search" instead of hanging.
3. **Replace** — a literal replacement string (regex back-references deferred to a future update, kept out of v1 the same way this repo's other tools favour an honest, narrower first cut over a claimed capability that isn't proven yet).
4. **Preview, ticked rows only** — the same `CheckList` shell every other batch tool in this repo already runs on: Element Id, containing sheet/view name, current text (truncated), text after replace, one tick per row, every match ticked by default.
5. **Formatting-safety flag** — `TextNote.Text` is a plain-string view over a note whose bold/underline/colour runs are tracked by character range (`GetFormattedText()`/`FormattedText`); a replacement whose length differs from the matched span can silently shift or drop a formatting run downstream of the edit. Any row where `len(old) != len(new)` is marked **"formatting review recommended"** in the preview rather than silently applied and trusted — the same "never present an unverified result as safe" posture this log's own BVBS/BOQ entries already commit to for their own unresolved rows.
6. **Apply** — ticked rows written inside one `Transaction`, one undo step; a short report (replaced / skipped / formatting-flagged counts, plus the flagged rows' sheet names) exported through the same `openpyxl` path `Export Schedule.pushbutton`/`BBS Generator.pushbutton` already use, giving a BIM lead a sign-off log before a set is reissued.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/revit/text_notes.py` (first annotation-content module in the `revit/` package, sibling to `parameters.py`/`elements.py`): `collect(doc, scope, view=None)` (the AutoLevel scope/collector pattern, generalised out of that tool's own private script into a shared, importable helper); `find_matches(notes, pattern, regex, case_sensitive, whole_word)`; `apply_replacements(doc, rows)` (the `Transaction` + `TextNote.Text` setter loop, one flagged/skipped/replaced tri-state per row).
- Sheet/view lookup for the preview's "containing sheet" column reuses `revit/views.py`'s existing view-enumeration helpers rather than a new traversal.
- UI: the same modeless `CheckList`/`hostwnd`/`theme` shell every other batch tool here already runs on; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`/icon, same version-bump-and-`CHANGELOG.md` convention every pushbutton in this repo follows.

**Future update:**
- Extend the same find/replace engine to Tag text overrides, Revision "Description" fields (the already-logged Revision Cloud Sync's own domain) and Dimension/Spot Elevation text overrides, once the `TextNote`-only path is proven.
- Regex capture-group replacement, once literal-string mode has real mileage and a formatting-safety story that covers a variable-length substitution too.
- Saved find/replace "playbooks" — a small JSON list of an office's standard recurring text fixes (a code-year bump, a boilerplate disclaimer update) that can be re-run at project kickoff or whenever a template updates, the same saved-profile posture already proposed for Universal Renamer and Sheet Set Builder.
- Feed the flagged/replaced sheet list into the already-logged Sheet Issue Kit's "since-last-run diff", so a text sweep ahead of a reissue is itself part of that issue package's changed-sheet detection.

## 2026-09-29 15:39 UTC

**Idea name:** Expansion/Seismic Joint Duplicator — picks a grid line, offsets a parallel twin by a specified movement-joint gap, and duplicates every column, beam, footing and wall hosted along the original onto the twin at that offset, closing the one everyday RC layout task this toolkit's own grid-crossing math (`structural/grids.py`) has never been pointed at: mirroring a full structural bay across a building movement joint

**Potential:**
Every multi-block RC building this toolkit's own targets already imply — the hospitals, schools and industrial sheds `BIMGeneration.pushbutton`/`cad2bim.pushbutton` build from PLANWIN/FRAMEWIN INP and DXF imports — needs an expansion or seismic joint wherever the plan steps, changes height, or simply runs too long for one monolithic pour. Structurally that means a *doubled* line of columns, beams and footings straddling a small gap (commonly 20–40mm), each side later designed and reinforced independently but starting from an identical geometric twin of the other. Today a modeler either copies each element one at a time in Revit and nudges it by the gap by hand — easy to get one column or half a bay wrong across dozens of elements — or re-draws the second line from the DXF a second time from scratch. A repo-wide check confirms this is genuinely open ground: `grep -ni "expansion joint\|movement joint\|double column\|double grid\|offset copy" pushbutton-idea.md` returns zero hits anywhere in this 2,300+ line log of roughly seventy prior ideas, and `grep -rn "def " AnonGee.extension/lib/py3/anongee_toolkit/{structural,commands,operations}` shows no offset-and-duplicate command anywhere — every existing structural creator (`structural/columns.py:create`, `structural/footings.py:create`, `structural/framing.py:create`) is called exactly once per element by `structure_run.py`, never in a batch "same again, shifted" pass. `structural/grids.py:segment_mm()` already turns a `Grid.Curve` into the `((x1,y1),(x2,y2))` mm pair this needs as its starting point, and `rc_automation/datum.py` already knows how to write a new `Grid` from two such points — both proven, neither ever chained into an offset-copy. On the market, a generic "copy and offset" exists in a few paid Revit add-ins (BIM 360-adjacent toolkits, some AutoDesk App Store multitools) but is element-agnostic — it moves geometry, not a matched structural family/type/level/host set — so nothing free or paid does the structural-aware version this needs.

**Description:**
`Expansion Joint Duplicator.pushbutton` lands in `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack`, beside `ConvertFloor.pushbutton`, `DrawFloor.pushbutton` and `RoundElementDist.pushbutton` — the stack this repo already treats as home for grid/geometry-driven structural batch edits.

1. **Pick the source line** — an existing `Grid` (listed via `structural.grids.names()`), or two picked points for a joint that isn't itself a named grid.
2. **Enter the gap** (mm) and which side to offset toward; the tool computes the parallel line with the same vector math `grids.segment_mm()` already exposes, no new geometry engine needed.
3. **Optional twin grid** — create the offset `Grid` too, named by convention (`A` → `A'` or `A-J`), via the same `Grid.Create` call `rc_automation/datum.py` already uses for `grids.sync`.
4. **Collect** — every `Column` (`structural.columns.placed()`), framed `Beam` (`structural.framing.placed()`), `Footing` and structural `Wall` whose location curve/point lies on the source line within a tolerance, the identical "what's built against this grid" read `RC Automation.pushbutton` already performs through `rc_automation/identity.py`'s grid-crossing IDs.
5. **Preview, ticked rows only** — the same `CheckList` shell every other batch tool in this repo runs on: source element → its planned twin (type, level, offset position), one tick per row.
6. **Create** — ticked rows duplicated inside one `TransactionGroup`, each dispatched by category to the matching `create()` already in `columns.py`/`footings.py`/`framing.py`, called with the same type/level/parameters and only the location shifted by the offset vector — so material, structural usage and every parameter these creators already set come along for free. Rebar is deliberately **not** copied: a joint's two sides are a different design case, reinforced independently afterward through the normal `RC Automation.pushbutton` run.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/structural/joint_duplicator.py`: `offset_line(segment_mm, gap_mm, side)` (pure vector math, reusing `grids.segment_mm()`'s coordinate convention so it unit-tests the same way `rc_automation.naming`'s pure functions already do); `collect_on_line(doc, line_mm, tol_mm)` walking `columns.placed()` / `footings` / `framing.placed()` plus a wall pass keyed the same way `rebar_hosts.py` already enumerates host categories; `duplicate_element(doc, element, offset_vector)`, one dispatch branch per category calling straight into the existing `columns.create()` / `footings.create()` / `framing.create()` with the source element's own resolved type/level and a shifted point.
- Grid twin creation calls the same `Grid.Create` helper `rc_automation/datum.py` runs for `grids.sync`, just fed an offset pair instead of a sheet-driven one.
- UI: the same modeless `CheckList`/`hostwnd`/`theme` shell every other batch tool here already runs on; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`/icon, same version-bump-and-`CHANGELOG.md` convention every pushbutton in this repo follows.

**Future update:**
- Mirror mode — offset both sides of a chosen centerline at once, for a joint drawn down the middle of a shared gap rather than measured from one existing line.
- Gap-width auditor half of the same problem: scan the model for column/footing pairs already sitting close and parallel, and flag any whose gap disagrees with the code-minimum or the drawing's stated value.
- Feed twinned footings and columns straight into `RC Automation.pushbutton` for independent per-side reinforcement, and into `BBS Generator.pushbutton` so the BOQ counts both sides once real rebar exists on each.
- Multi-grid "block copy" — offset a whole run of parallel grids and everything hosted to all of them in one pass, for joints that run the full width of a plan rather than a single line.

The repo's two nearest neighbours both name this exact gap and stop at its edge rather than close it: **Standards Diff & Selective Transfer**'s own scope line (`pushbutton-idea.md:200`, its idea-name line at `:619`) lists "line styles, line patterns, fill patterns, materials, view filters and view templates" as what it diffs between two `.rvt` files and never once mentions a family; **Family Health Auditor** (2026-09-19 entry) is the repo's only family-focused check, but it runs single-document — in-place families, embedded CAD, duplicate-signature clusters inside the one open model — and never opens an external file to compare a family's current state against what it should be. On the market, batch library-sync-with-preview is sold only inside paid content-management platforms — BIM 360/ACC content libraries, CTC's Family Browser, Avail — each gated behind a subscription on top of Revit itself; nothing free diffs a project's already-loaded families against a master library before deciding what to reload.

**Description:**
`Family Library Sync.pushbutton` lands in `Advance.panel`, beside `Parameter Combine.pushbutton` and the eventual `Standards Diff.pushbutton` — the panel this repo already treats as home for two-document, checklist-gated comparison tools.

1. **Pick a source** — a folder of `.rfa` files, or a master `.rvt` opened read-only via `Application.OpenDocumentFile()` (the exact cross-document mechanism Standards Diff's own write-up proposes and never uses on families).
2. **Inventory both sides** — the active document's loaded families and the library's master families are both walked through `anongee_toolkit/structural/inventory.py`'s existing `_families(doc)` (confirmed at `inventory.py:117-150`), which already returns `[{category, family, types: [{name, mark, parameters}]}]` for loadable and system families alike — built today only for `Extract Template.pushbutton`'s read-only Markdown dump, reused here unchanged as the data source on both sides of the diff.
3. **Match and bucket** — families are matched by name; per match, the type list and each type's parameter values are compared using the same signature approach `ConvertFloor.pushbutton/script.py:704`'s `cs_signature(ftype)` already uses to tell "same shape, different values" apart (first lifted once already for the already-logged Type Consolidator idea). Each matched family sorts into **up to date**, **drifted** (same types, different parameter values), **missing new types** (library has types the project doesn't), or **not in library** (local-only, left alone).
4. **Preview, ticked rows only** — one table, same `CheckList` shell every other batch tool in this repo already runs on: family, bucket, what changed, a per-row tick.
5. **Apply** — ticked rows call `doc.LoadFamily(path, IFamilyLoadOptions, out family)` inside a single `Transaction`, with the overwrite choice made per row from the preview rather than Revit's native single blind global prompt.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/structural/library_sync.py`: `inventory_library(paths_or_doc)` (wraps `inventory._families()` for a folder of `.rfa` or an already-open library `Document`), `diff_families(project_families, library_families)` (name-match plus `cs_signature()`-style per-type comparison, returning the four buckets above), and `open_library(path)` (thin wrapper around `Application.OpenDocumentFile()`, closed again once inventoried) — all Revit-API-light enough to unit test the same way `rc_automation.naming`'s pure functions already are, aside from the two calls that must touch a live `Application`.
- `IFamilyLoadOptions` implementation reused verbatim from wherever the repo's own family-duplication code already answers Revit's "family already exists" prompt during a `NewFamilyInstance`/type-duplication pass (the same overwrite-decision shape `columns.py`/`framing.py` already resolve when writing a duplicated type) — the per-row apply is that same answer, driven by the preview tick instead of a hardcoded default.
- UI: the same modeless `CheckList`/`hostwnd`/`theme` shell every other batch tool here runs on; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`/icon in `Advance.panel`, same version-bump-and-`CHANGELOG.md` convention every other pushbutton follows.

**Future update:**
- Extend the same diff engine to system-family types (wall, floor, framing types with no `.rfa` at all) once `inventory._families()`'s `loadable=False` rows are proven out on the loadable side first.
- A "push" direction — flag families in the *project* that have drifted from or grown ahead of the library, so a modeler can promote a local fix back up to the master instead of only ever pulling down.
- Wire the already-logged Standards Diff & Selective Transfer's own comparison UI in as the shared shell once both exist, so "diff two documents" becomes one tool with a category picker instead of two siblings duplicating the same table/preview scaffolding.
- Schedule this as a recurring weekly check via the Bridge's own job-listener pattern (`Bridge Listener.pushbutton`), so drift is surfaced on a cadence instead of only when someone remembers to click the button.

**Idea name:** Structural Analysis Model Exporter — walks every grid, level, column and beam this toolkit already knows how to read back (`grids.py`, `levels.py`, `columns.placed()`, `framing.placed()`) and writes a STAAD.Pro `.std` input file with matched member sections and materials, closing the one direction `BIMGeneration.pushbutton`'s own FRAMEWIN/PLANWIN `.inp` importer has never run: Revit model **out** to an analysis package, never only an analysis package **into** Revit

**Potential:**
This toolkit builds structural Revit models *from* an analysis package's own export today, and has never once built the reverse file. `BIMGeneration.pushbutton/core.py:294,329` reads a FRAMEWIN/PLANWIN `.inp` file — grid, level, column, beam and slab data — to create the Revit model in the first place, and `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py:100-111`'s `_symbol_material()` reads `BuiltInParameter.STRUCTURAL_MATERIAL_PARAM` off a `FamilySymbol` purely to copy a material assignment across symbols *during that same import*. Neither script, nor anything else in the repo (`grep -rniE "staad|etabs|sap2000|\.std\b|e2k" AnonGee.extension --include=*.py`, vendored libraries excluded, returns zero hits), ever writes a structural-analysis input file back out. Yet every one of the read-side building blocks such an export needs already exists, built for a different purpose and never pointed the other way: `anongee_toolkit/structural/grids.py:39-52`'s `segment_mm(grid)` returns a grid's own two endpoints in mm and `intersection_mm()` (`grids.py:56-67`) already crosses two named grids into a point via `naming.cross_segments()` — exactly the joint-coordinate math a `.std` file's `JOINT COORDINATES` block needs, built today only to resolve where a footing goes from `GridX`/`GridY` schedule columns. `structural/levels.py:19-27`'s `levels(doc)` returns every level's name and elevation in mm, lowest first — a `.std` file's storey table, ready-made. `structural/columns.py:279-302`'s `placed(doc)` already returns `(ElementId, (x, y), level_name, type_name)` for every column in the model, and `structural/framing.py:219-239`'s `placed(doc)` returns the same shape for beams — both built so `BIMGeneration.pushbutton`'s reconciliation pass can tell "is this member already here" during a re-import, never to describe a member for export. The one real gap: `framing.placed()` deliberately returns only a beam's **midpoint** (`_midpoint()`, `framing.py:256-264` — "two beams sharing a midpoint on one level are the same beam," its own docstring says, which is all a duplicate check needs), so nothing in the repo currently reads a beam's own two end joints, which a `.std` `MEMBER INCIDENCES` line requires. Section sizing is likewise sitting half-built: `columns.py:91-108`'s `_dimensions(text)` already parses `"300 X 600"` out of a type name into an ordered `(width, depth)` tuple, and both `columns.py:113-115` and `framing.py:21-23` carry an identical `WIDTH_NAMES`/`DEPTH_NAMES` tuple used today only to *write* a duplicated type's `b`/`h` parameters — reading those same instance-type parameters back out for export is the same lookup run in reverse, not new logic. For a BIM team, the daily cost this closes is concrete: every RCC job hands its grid/column/beam layout to a structural engineer twice — once as the Revit model, once rebuilt by hand (or by the engineer, from a printed plan) inside STAAD.Pro or ETABS for the actual analysis — and every geometry revision repeats that manual re-entry a second time, in a second tool, with no guarantee the two ever describe the same building. On the market this exact handoff exists only as a paid, seat-licensed CSI/Bentley interoperability feature (ETABS's own Revit link, STAAD's ISM/CIS-2 exchange), each tied to owning that specific analysis package's current version; nothing free reads a plain Revit model's own grids, levels, columns and beams and writes a STAAD-readable text file a firm can open in whatever seat it already has.

**Description:**
`Analysis Exporter.pushbutton` lands in `Core.panel/BIM.stack`, beside `BIMGeneration.pushbutton` and `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton` — the one panel already reserved for structural-model-generation-from-an-external-file tools, now gaining the mirror-image direction.

1. **Scope** — whole model (an analysis run is never a partial building), read-only: no transaction opens, the same posture `structural/inventory.py`'s own module docstring already commits to for a whole-model walk ("Everything here is **read-only**").
2. **Joints** — every grid intersection actually used by a placed column or beam endpoint is numbered once and written as a `.std` `JOINT COORDINATES` line (`node_id  x  y  z`), reusing `grids.segment_mm()`/`intersection_mm()` for any joint still nameable off the grid, and a plain XY-plus-level match for anything else.
3. **Levels → Z** — `levels.levels(doc)` supplies the Z ordinate for every joint at that storey directly; no separate elevation lookup is written.
4. **Members** — one `.std` `MEMBER INCIDENCES` line per column (base joint → top joint, from the instance's base/top level and `placed()` location) and per beam span (start joint → end joint — the new part, a `_endpoints_mm()` sibling to `framing.py`'s existing `_midpoint()`, reading `Location.Curve.GetEndPoint(0)/(1)` the same way `_midpoint()` already reads the same curve).
5. **Sections and material** — one `.std` `MEMBER PROPERTY`/`CONSTANTS` block per distinct column/beam type, built from that type's own `WIDTH_NAMES`/`DEPTH_NAMES` parameter lookup (the same names `columns.py`/`framing.py` already use to *write* a duplicated type, run here as a read) and its `STRUCTURAL_MATERIAL_PARAM`-resolved material's `ConcreteCompressiveStrength`, falling back to `_dimensions()`'s name-text parse only when the instance parameters themselves are missing.
6. **Preview and write** — a per-member table (mark, joints, section, material, any row the exporter could not resolve) on the same `CheckList` shell every other batch tool here runs on, ticked rows only, then one `.std` file written to a chosen path — nothing is ever written back into the Revit model itself, so there is no transaction to roll back.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/structural/analysis_export.py`: `collect_joints(doc)` (grid-crossing + level-Z, built on `grids.intersection_mm()`/`levels.levels()`), `collect_members(doc)` (columns via `columns.placed()` plus base/top level read, beams via `framing.placed()`'s existing category/level fields plus the new `_endpoints_mm()`), `resolve_section(symbol)` (the `WIDTH_NAMES`/`DEPTH_NAMES` read-back, falling through to `_dimensions(type_name)`), and `write_std(path, joints, members, sections)` — a plain-text writer with no Revit API in it at all, unit-testable the same way `rc_automation.naming`'s pure functions already are.
- `framing.py` gains one small addition, `_endpoints_mm(instance, ft_to_mm)`, sitting next to `_midpoint()` and sharing its `Location.Curve` read — the one genuinely new geometry primitive this idea needs; `_midpoint()` itself is left untouched since `BIMGeneration.pushbutton`'s reconciliation still needs exactly the value it returns today.
- Material strength resolution reuses `FramewinToBIM.pushbutton/script.py:100-111`'s `_symbol_material()` lookup path (`STRUCTURAL_MATERIAL_PARAM` → `Material`), reading `Material.GetConcreteStrength()`/a project-standard grade table instead of just returning the `Material` object as that script does.
- UI: the same modeless `CheckList`/`hostwnd`/`theme` shell every other batch tool in this repo already runs on; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`/icon in `Core.panel/BIM.stack`, same version-bump-and-`CHANGELOG.md` convention every other pushbutton here follows.

**Future update:**
- Slab/floor panels as `.std` `ELEMENT INCIDENCES` plate elements, once a mesh-shaped export (rather than a line-member one) is proven — `BIMGeneration.pushbutton` already reads slab geometry from the same `.inp` files on the way in, so the plate-corner data this needs is the same shape in reverse.
- A second writer targeting ETABS's `.e2k` text format off the exact same `collect_joints()`/`collect_members()` data, so one internal model serves either analysis package without a second geometry pass.
- Load case scaffolding: once the already-logged BOQ & Cost Estimator's per-element self-weight numbers exist, seed a basic dead-load case in the `.std` output instead of leaving every run to start from an empty load table.
- Wire the already-logged Analytical-Physical Alignment Auditor's drift/orphan report in as a mandatory pre-export gate, so a `.std` file is never built from a model with unresolved analytical drift.

## 2026-09-28 05:40 UTC

**Idea name:** Rebar Machine Export (BVBS) — writes `BBS Generator`'s already-computed per-bar shape, dimension, diameter and bend data straight into the BVBS bar-processing exchange file every CNC rebar bending/cutting machine on the market (Schnell, MEP, EBS, Progress, Toptek and every "aSa"/"RebSteel"-family bending-shop software) reads natively, closing the one hop left between a finished BBS and a bent bar: a human retyping the schedule into the machine

**Potential:** `BBS Generator.pushbutton` already computes everything a bending machine needs to cut and bend a bar with nobody re-keying a number, and today all of it dead-ends in a human-readable Excel/PDF sheet. `core/bar_record.py:9-18`'s `BarRecord.__slots__` already carries `diameter_mm`, `shape_code`, `dimensions` (the A/B/C/D/E dict), `cutting_length_mm`, `bend_diameter_mm` and `no_of_bars` on every single bar the tool reads; `core/rebar_reader.py:236-237` computes `bend_dia_mm = standard_module.bend_diameter_mm(diameter_mm)` — the exact mandrel/bending-roller diameter a machine needs to select its bending pin — from the same `IS_2502_2019.py:20-27`/`BS_8666_2020.py`/`ACI_315_2018.py` clause-based formulas the BBS sheet already prints; and `_estimate_bend_deduction`'s own `_SHAPE_BENDS` table (`rebar_reader.py:276-292`) already holds, for every one of the 20-odd shape codes this repo supports, the exact ordered sequence of bend angles (`"21":[(90,2)]`, `"51":[(90,2),(135,2)]`, etc.) that a BVBS geometry block needs to describe a bar as a walked polyline of segment-length/angle pairs — the same adjacency data the already-logged Bar Shape Legend (2026-09-28 00:40) proposes drawing as a human picture, here consumed by a machine instead of an eye. None of it is ever written to a machine-readable format: `output/excel_writer.py` and `output/pdf_exporter.py` are this tool's only two writers, both human-facing documents (`grep -rniE "bvbs|bending machine|cnc" pushbutton-idea.md` and this repo's own tree both return nothing — no logged idea and no shipped code anywhere touches this). This is a real, separate step from what the toolkit already covers: the already-logged Bar Cutting Optimizer (2026-09-16) nests `total_length_mm` against stock bar lengths to minimise offcut waste — a *quantity* problem — and never touches a machine's own input format; the already-logged Bar Shape Legend draws the same shape geometry as a picture *for a person* to read off a printed sheet. Today, once a BBS leaves this toolkit, a rebar-shop operator (in-house or an outsourced bending yard) opens their machine's own control software — every major bending-machine vendor ships one, none of them read Excel — and manually types in, bar mark by bar mark, the diameter, the shape/type code in that specific machine's own numbering, and every A/B/C/D/E length, exactly reproducing numbers this repo has already computed once, with the exact same transcription-error risk BBS Generator's own revision-hash diffing (`_compute_hash`, `bar_record.py:47-58`) exists to protect the *schedule* from but cannot protect the *machine input* from, since nothing carries the schedule's own numbers there. One real gap surfaces doing this research and is worth naming honestly rather than glossing over: BVBS also carries a steel-grade code per bar (e.g. B500B/Fe500D), and this repo has never read one — `grep -rniE "fe500|b500b|steel grade"` across `BBS Generator.pushbutton` returns exactly one hit, a bare code comment ("Grade B500B", `BS_8666_2020.py:40`) documenting *why* a bend-radius constant has the value it has, never a parameter lookup; `bar_mark_manager.py:26-40`'s `read_bar_type_name()` — the only thing this repo calls "Bar Type" — reads a `"Bar Type"/"Comments"` parameter and, failing that, **falls back to `f"T{diameter_mm}"`**, a diameter label, not a metallurgical grade. On the market, a live Revit-model-to-BVBS pipeline exists only inside the same paid, seat-licensed rebar-detailing suites this repo's other rebar ideas already check against for their own narrower claims (AGACAD Rebar for Revit, RebarCAD, Naviate Structure's export module, Tekla's own reinforcement detailer) — each sold as a separate line item specifically because BVBS export is the one feature bending yards will pay extra for; nothing free reads a native `DB.Rebar` population and writes a bending yard's own machine format, and this repo's BBS Generator is the one tool in this toolkit that is one export function away from being able to.

**Description:**
1. **New sibling output, not a new reader.** `BBS Generator.pushbutton/output/bvbs_writer.py` (new) takes the exact same `list[BarRecord]` `write_bbs_workbook` already consumes (`excel_writer.py:135`) — no second pass over the model, no new Revit API call beyond the one grade lookup below — and writes a `.abs`/`.bvbs` text file alongside the `.xlsx`/`.pdf` this tool already produces.
2. **Per-bar record.** For each `BarRecord`: `diameter_mm` and `no_of_bars`/`cutting_length_mm` map directly onto BVBS's quantity/diameter/length fields; `shape_code` maps through a new small `BVBS_SHAPE_MAP` per standard (most codes are near-identical numbering already — a straight bar, an L, a U/stirrup — so this is a lookup table, not new geometry math) to the machine format's own shape-type number; the geometry block is built by walking `dimensions` (`{"A":.., "B":.., ...}`) in the order `standard_module.SHAPE_MAP[code]["dims"]` already lists (`IS_2502_2019.py`/`BS_8666_2020.py`/`ACI_315_2018.py`, the same ordered list Bar Shape Legend's `SHAPE_LAYOUT` idea already keys off) paired with the angle sequence `_estimate_bend_deduction`'s own `_SHAPE_BENDS[code]` table already carries — segment length, then turn angle, then next segment length, exactly the polyline BVBS's geometry section expects; `bend_diameter_mm` supplies the bending-roller/pin diameter field directly, already unit-correct in mm.
3. **Steel grade — asked once, not guessed.** A single project-level setting (persisted the same way `slab_convert_config.json` already persists a per-project override for `Convert Slab`, or as one more field on the existing BBS Generator settings surface `ui/main_window.py` already reads/writes via its established `cfg_get`/`cfg_set` pattern) lets the modeler pick or type the mill grade once per run (default `B500B`/`Fe500D` per the active standard module), applied to every bar in that export; a per-bar-type override list is offered for the rare mixed-grade job, but the honest default is "the whole run is one grade," which matches how a bending yard actually orders coil for a single work order.
4. **One more export button, same window.** `ui/main_window.py` gets one more checkbox/button beside the existing `chk_unit_weight`/`chk_calc_sheet` pair (`main_window.py:505,542,626`) — "Export BVBS for bending machine" — wired to call `bvbs_writer.write_bvbs_file(records, path, grade, standard_module)` after (or instead of) the Excel export, using the same save-path prompt the Excel writer already shows.
5. **What ships unresolved is reported, not guessed.** Any bar whose `shape_code` has no `BVBS_SHAPE_MAP` entry (a `"99xx"` custom shape, or a rare universal-fallback code with no machine-format equivalent) is excluded from the `.bvbs` file and listed by bar mark in a small on-screen summary ("14 of 312 bars need manual entry — custom shapes") rather than silently emitting a wrong shape number a machine would then bend incorrectly — the same "never fabricate an unverified value" posture Convert Slab's own type-resolution and BOQ Estimator's own `unpriced`-flag idea (2026-09-27 10:39) already commit to.

**Implementation:**
- New `BBS Generator.pushbutton/output/bvbs_writer.py`: `write_bvbs_file(records, path, grade, standard_module)`; `_bvbs_shape_code(shape_code, standard_module)` via a new small `BVBS_SHAPE_MAP` dict per standard module (sibling to the existing `SHAPE_MAP`, same file); `_geometry_block(dims, dim_order, bends)` walking dims/angles into the machine polyline; `_bar_line(record, bvbs_code, grade)` formatting one BVBS record.
- `standards/IS_2502_2019.py`, `BS_8666_2020.py`, `ACI_315_2018.py`: one new `BVBS_SHAPE_MAP` dict each, keyed identically to the existing `SHAPE_MAP` (mirrors exactly how Bar Shape Legend's proposed `SHAPE_LAYOUT` sits beside `SHAPE_MAP` in the same three files) — kept in the standard module because bend-angle conventions and shape numbering both already vary by standard in this codebase.
- `core/rebar_reader.py`: no change to the read path; `_SHAPE_BENDS` (`:276-292`) is imported/reused as-is by the new writer rather than duplicated, the same "one source of truth" instinct the rest of this file already follows.
- `ui/main_window.py`: one new persisted setting (`grade`, default per `standard_module`) and one new export action beside `chk_unit_weight`/`chk_calc_sheet` (`:505,542,626`), following that file's own `cfg_get`/`cfg_set` pattern.
- No new third-party dependency — BVBS is a plain fixed-width/delimited text format, written with the standard library the same way `output/pdf_exporter.py`'s fpdf2 fallback already keeps this tool dependency-light.
- Own `CHANGELOG.md` bump for `BBS Generator.pushbutton`, following the same version-and-changelog convention every other tool in this repo already follows.

**Future update:**
- Once the already-logged Bar Cutting Optimizer (2026-09-16) exists, hand its optimised, waste-minimised cut list to this same writer instead of the raw per-bar list, so the machine file a bending yard actually runs already reflects the least-waste stock allocation rather than a naive one-bar-per-line export.
- Feed per-bar-mark BVBS shape codes back into Bar Shape Legend's `SHAPE_LAYOUT` table validation (its own future-update line, 2026-09-28 00:40) once both exist, so a shape that fails to resolve for a machine is caught the same run a legend page would also have flagged it.
- A small round-trip reader for the handful of bending-machine tools that can *export* a produced/cut confirmation back to the same file format, so a re-run of BBS Generator after fabrication could mark bars as "cut" against the schedule — genuinely future scope, dependent on what a given machine vendor's own export actually looks like in practice.
- Per-bar-type grade overrides (mixed-grade work orders) once a real project surfaces the need, rather than building the more complex case before anyone has hit it.
