## 2026-09-28 00:40 UTC

**Idea name:** Bar Shape Legend — draws the standard bend pictogram BBS Generator has only ever described in numbers, straight into the workbook it already produces, using nothing but the cell grid openpyxl already gives it for free

**Potential:** Every field engineer and bar-bender site crew reads a bar-bending schedule the same way worldwide: shape code number first, then a quick glance at the printed code-book pictogram (BS 8666:2020 Table 2, IS 2502:2019 Table, ACI 315-2018's own catalogue) to see *which* segment is A and which is B before the numbers in those columns mean anything — a stirrup's "A" is a leg, a Z-bar's "A" is the first cranked run, and nobody who isn't a detailer memorises which is which for all 20-odd codes in daily use. `BBS Generator.pushbutton` already computes every one of those numbers with real engineering behind them — `core/shape_resolver.py:67`'s `resolve_shape()` docstring states outright "NEVER returns '??' — every shape gets a usable code" (`shape_resolver.py:77`), and `core/rebar_reader.py:231`'s `dims = extract_dimensions(shape_elem, rebar, FT_TO_MM)` feeds a real per-bar `{A, B, C, D, E}` dict into `BarRecord.dimensions` (`core/bar_record.py:11`) — but the sheet it ships to site does nothing with the *shape* of that data beyond a bare two-character code. `output/excel_writer.py:61-78`'s `BBS_COLUMNS` prints "Shape Code" (column 6) as plain text next to five numeric A–E columns (7–11), and `_build_bbs_row` (`excel_writer.py:282-337`) reads `r.dimensions.get("A", "")` through `.get("E", "")` (lines 316-320) into those same five cells with no geometric relationship drawn between them at all — a modeler or foreman gets five disconnected numbers and has to already know, from memory or a separate code-book PDF, that shape "21" means "A across, then down by B, then across by C" before those numbers mean a bendable bar. The three `standards/*.py` modules this repo already ships even carry the missing piece and never surface it: `BS_8666_2020.py:84-134`, `ACI_315_2018.py:90-122` and `IS_2502_2019.py:42-102` each key `SHAPE_MAP[code]["dims"]` to an **ordered list** of which letters that specific code actually uses and in what sequence (e.g. `"11": {"dims": ["A", "B"]}` for a one-bend L, `"21": {"dims": ["A", "B", "C"]}` for a two-bend Z/S, `"51": {"dims": ["A", "B"]}` for a closed stirrup) — the exact adjacency data a pictogram renderer needs and the exact data this repo has never once turned into a drawing. Confirmed by grep: there is no `pictogram`, `diagram`, `sketch`, `PIL`, or `Pillow` anywhere in this repo (`find AnonGee.extension/lib/py3 -iname "PIL*"` returns nothing), so today's only path to a shape picture is a human pasting one in from a code-book photocopy, or omitting it and trusting the site crew already knows the convention by heart — a trust that breaks exactly on the codes used least often, which is precisely when a wrong-shape bar gets bent and wasted. This is distinct from the already-logged Bar Cutting Optimizer (2026-09-16 10:39), which nests cutting lengths against stock bars and never touches shape geometry, and from Reinforcement Density Heatmap (2026-09-21 05:38), whose "band_for" bucketing is a colour lookup on a weight ratio, not a geometric drawing — no logged idea in this file proposes drawing anything. On the market, this exact pictogram exists only inside paid, seat-licensed rebar-detailing software (Tekla Structures' reinforcement detailing modules, RebarCAD's own shape library) that auto-generates it as a side effect of full BIM-linked detailing in a separate paid environment nothing in this repo talks to; the free BBS Excel templates that circulate among site engineers either carry one static clip-art shape image with no per-bar dimensions wired to it, or skip the picture entirely — nobody ships a free tool that draws the pictogram from the same live numbers already in the schedule.

**Description:**
1. **Legend, not per-row art.** A real BBS groups dozens of bar marks onto a handful of shape codes (every stirrup in a column is "51"; every main bar in a footing is "00" or "11") — a pictogram belongs once per *code actually present in this run*, not redrawn identically on every one of a hundred rows. `write_bbs_workbook` (`excel_writer.py:135`) gains one more worksheet, `_write_shape_legend_sheet(wb, records, standard_module)`, built the same way `_write_summary_sheet` (`excel_writer.py:394`) already is — a small loop over the run's data, not a per-bar operation.
2. **One block per code.** For each unique `shape_code` in `records` (deduplicated the same way `_write_summary_sheet`'s `dia_totals`/`dia_lengths` (`excel_writer.py:266-267`) already deduplicate by diameter), look up `standard_module.SHAPE_MAP[code]["dims"]` and `["formula"]`, and a small new per-standard `SHAPE_LAYOUT` table (one entry per code, e.g. `"11": [("right","A"), ("down","B")]`, `"21": [("right","A"), ("down","B"), ("right","C")]`, `"31": [("down","A"), ("right","B"), ("up","A")]`, `"51"/"56"`: a closed rectangle sized A×B) mapping that ordered dims list to a sequence of compass directions.
3. **Draw with cells, not pixels.** A new `core/shape_diagram.py` walks that direction sequence and paints a path of merged, thick-bordered cells across a small fixed grid (5 rows × 6 columns per block) using `BORDER_THICK`/`_thick` — already defined at `excel_writer.py:37`, `Side(style="medium", color="7F8C8D")` — on just the outer edge of each segment's cell run, with the dim letter (generic "A"/"B"/"C", not a bar's actual number — this is a legend, one per code, for looking the shape up) centered in a small merged label cell beside it via the exact `_fill`/`_font`/`_align` helpers (`excel_writer.py:41-43`) every other sheet in this file already calls. Curved codes (circular rings/spirals — `"60"`, `"61"`, `"77"`, `"80"`) get an octagon approximation built from diagonally-notched corner cells in v1, labelled "⌀D", rather than a claimed true curve — the same honest scope-out this repo's own Wall Reinforcement Placer (2026-09-27 15:41, diagonal corner-crack bars) and Curved Pad Tie Placer (2026-09-26 05:42) entries already model for a first cut.
4. **Wire it to the schedule.** The existing "Shape Code" cell in the main BBS sheet (`excel_writer.py:324`, column 6 of `_build_bbs_row`) gets `cell.hyperlink = f"#'Shape Legend'!A{legend_row_for[code]}"` and an underline font — a foreman clicks "51" on any row and lands on that one code's pictogram-plus-formula block instead of needing a separate code-book.
5. **PDF side.** `output/pdf_exporter.py`'s fpdf2 fallback path (`_export_via_fpdf2`, `pdf_exporter.py:90`) already runs when Excel COM isn't available (site laptops without Excel installed); it gets one more page rendered from the same `SHAPE_LAYOUT` table using fpdf2's own native `pdf.line()`/`pdf.rect()` vector primitives — no image library, no raster asset, so a PDF-only site issue still ships the legend page.
6. **User control.** One new checkbox, `chk_shape_legend`, added to `ui/main_window.py` next to the existing `chk_unit_weight`/`chk_calc_sheet` pair (`main_window.py:505,542,626` — same `cfg_get`/`cfg_set` persistence pattern, same `bool(...IsChecked)` wiring into `write_bbs_workbook`'s kwargs), so a project can turn the legend off for a quick internal re-export and on for anything actually issued to a site crew.

**Implementation:**
- `BBS Generator.pushbutton/core/shape_diagram.py` (new): `draw_shape_block(ws, top_row, top_col, code, dims, layout)` — the only genuinely new logic, a plain cell-border path renderer with a clamped per-segment cell span (1–4 cells) so a 150 mm hook and a 4000 mm main leg both render inside the same fixed block size, mirroring the same "clamp, don't scale unboundedly" instinct this repo's own `band_for()` (proposed for Reinforcement Density Heatmap, 2026-09-21 05:38) already applies to a different numeric range.
- `BBS Generator.pushbutton/standards/BS_8666_2020.py`, `ACI_315_2018.py`, `IS_2502_2019.py`: one new `SHAPE_LAYOUT` dict per module, keyed identically to each module's own existing `SHAPE_MAP` (`BS_8666_2020.py:84`, `ACI_315_2018.py:90`, `IS_2502_2019.py:42`) so a shape code and its drawing recipe always live beside each other, not in a fourth file that can drift out of sync.
- `output/excel_writer.py`: new `_write_shape_legend_sheet()` (sibling to `_write_summary_sheet`, `:394`) called from `write_bbs_workbook` (`:135`); one new line in `_build_bbs_row` (`:324`, the existing `r.shape_code,` row entry, `# 6 Shape Code`) adding the hyperlink once `legend_row_for` is known.
- `output/pdf_exporter.py`: extend `_export_via_fpdf2` (`:90`) with one more page, reusing `SHAPE_LAYOUT` directly — same data, two renderers (openpyxl cells, fpdf2 vectors), no third format to maintain.
- `ui/main_window.py`: `chk_shape_legend` beside `chk_unit_weight`/`chk_calc_sheet` (`:505,542,626`), default checked (this is a "make it usable on-site" feature, opt-out rather than opt-in).
- No new third-party dependency — confirmed no PIL/Pillow anywhere in `AnonGee.extension/lib/py3`, so the design deliberately stays inside openpyxl's own `Border`/`Side`/merged-cell primitives (already imported, `excel_writer.py:14`) and fpdf2's own vector calls, both already in this file's dependency chain today.

**Future update:**
- Once true curve rendering is worth the dependency cost, revisit the v1 octagon approximation for ring/spiral codes (60/61/77/80) with a proper arc — gated on this idea's own scope-out note, not assumed now.
- Feed a per-bar-mark actual-values variant (not just the generic legend) into whatever renders Bar Cutting Optimizer's (2026-09-16 10:39) site-floor cut sheet, so a bar-bender's physical cut list carries the real A/B/C numbers on the same pictogram a foreman already recognises from the legend page.
- Once Rebar Cage Copier (2026-09-17 05:40) exists, the same `SHAPE_LAYOUT` table is the natural place to validate that a copied cage's bar actually matches the shape family it claims, before it ever reaches BBS Generator's own read.

## 2026-09-27 00:42 UTC

**Idea name:** Multi Filter Parameter — ElementId Write Support, porting the exact `[id] Name` bracket-encode/decode trick `One Filter Parameter` already ships and already uses to batch-set Level, Material, Phase, Design Option and Family-Type-referencing parameters, into the one tool built specifically to replace it for real batch work and which hard-refuses every one of those same parameters today

**Potential:** `Advance.panel/FilterParameter.splitbutton` ships two pushbuttons with near-identical bundle tooltips, both promising the same five edit operations — `One Filter Parameter/bundle.yaml` and `Multi Filter Parameter/bundle.yaml` both read, verbatim, "change a parameter... (Set / Prefix / Suffix / Replace / Delete)" — and both built the same way: filter elements by category and parameter condition, then batch-edit a chosen writable parameter on every match inside one `Transaction`. Multi is the newer, more capable sibling — multiple AND/OR filter conditions and multiple edit rows applied in one pass, versus One's single condition and single edit — the tool a modeler reaches for on any real filtered set. But the two tools disagree on one entire `StorageType`, and only one of them tells the truth about it up front. `OneFilterParameter.pushbutton/script.py:68-79` defines `_bracket_int(s)`, a small parser for a leading `"[<int>]"` prefix ("Replaces `re.match` — the `re` module is unavailable in this CPython3 engine"), used because `_get_param_val_str` (`script.py:259-271`) deliberately formats every ElementId-storage parameter's display value as `"[{eid_val}] {name}"` — e.g. a Base Level parameter shows as `"[482913] Level 2"` — specifically so the numeric id survives a round trip through a plain-text WPF `ComboBox`. `_get_param_values` (`script.py:376-388`) feeds that bracketed string into every filter- and edit-value dropdown, and `_execute_edit`'s `Set` branch (`script.py:749-767`) closes the loop: for `StorageType.ElementId` it calls `_bracket_int(str(val1).strip())` to recover the id, wraps it back into a real `ElementId`, and calls `param.Set(new_id)` (`script.py:760-764`) — a genuinely working, shipped, one-click way to batch-reassign any element-reference parameter (Base/Top Level, Material, Phase Created/Demolished, Design Option, a shared parameter typed `Family Type`) across a filtered set, by picking a name off a dropdown instead of hand-editing one element at a time in Properties. `MultiFilterParameter.pushbutton/script.py` never adopted any of it: `_get_param_values` (`script.py:298-324`) only ever calls `param.AsValueString()` with String/Integer/Double fallbacks — no ElementId branch, no bracket, no id captured anywhere — and `_get_common_params` (`script.py:280-296`) filters candidate edit parameters purely on `p.IsReadOnly`, so a writable ElementId parameter is offered in the edit-row dropdown exactly like any other, with real, friendly values in its value list (Revit's own `AsValueString()` already resolves most ElementId BuiltInParameters to a name, just without the id Multi would need to write it back). A modeler picks "Base Level" as an edit parameter, sees "Level 3" as a selectable value, ticks it, hits **Execute Changes**, and `_apply_single_modification` (`script.py:382-420`) runs the request into a dead end it has always had: `if st == StorageType.ElementId: return False, "Set ElementId not supported"` (`script.py:415-416`) — surfacing only as one more line buried in the run's partial-`errors` list (`script.py:1022-1034`), after the transaction already committed whatever else the row touched. The same function's `Delete` branch, one line above, has no such gap — `elif st == StorageType.ElementId: param.Set(ElementId.InvalidElementId)` (`script.py:392`) already writes an ElementId — so Multi can already clear a Level/Material/Phase reference on a hundred elements in one pass, and cannot set one to anything, on the same parameter, in the same tool. This is exactly the everyday batch chore both tools were built for and only one delivers: re-basing every footing a level's insertion point shifted onto its correct new Base Level, swapping the Material on every column of a given type after a spec revision, or bulk-correcting a batch of elements someone modelled on the wrong Phase — today possible one row at a time in One (or one element at a time in native Properties), and silently refused the moment the same job needs more than one filter condition or more than one parameter changed together, which is the entire reason Multi exists. The tooling to close it is sitting half-built and mis-aimed. `lib/py3/anongee_toolkit/cad2bim/geom/compare.py:1-13` implements a generic, Revit-free, unit-tested `diff(revit_records, dxf_records, tol_ft)` (`compare.py:53`) and `format_console(comparison)` (`compare.py:120`) that midpoint-matches `CurveRecord`-shaped geometry (`model.py:12-19`, `.points`/`.layer_key`/`.length_ft`) between two sources and reports per-layer counts, "dxf_only" (dropped/merged), "revit_only" (import artifacts) and "clipped" (length-mismatched) members. But its only caller, `AnonGee.tab/Core.panel/cad2bim.pushbutton/script.py:695-698`, is explicitly labelled `# Diagnostic only: how much Revit's import dropped/clipped vs the raw DXF` and feeds it `revit_result.records` from `geometry_reader.read_link(doc, instance)` (`script.py:390`) — i.e. it diffs the *raw linked CAD import curves*, captured once at the start of the run, against the DXF text/geometry read, purely to decide whether Revit's own DWG import clipped a junction badly enough that the build should trust ezdxf instead. It never once looks at what the builders actually placed. Every builder hands back exactly the material needed to do that: `columns.py:86` initialises `result = {"created": [], "skipped": [], "errors": [], "notes": []}` and `columns.py:131` appends `instance.Id` for every placed `FamilyInstance`; beams, slabs, footings and walls follow the identical `"created": [ElementId, ...]` shape. Nothing in the repository ever re-reads `doc.GetElement(id).Location` / `get_BoundingBox(None)` for those IDs and re-runs them through `compare.diff()` against the DXF — the as-built check the roadmap asks for. `report.py:4-6` even documents the missing piece by name: the JSON export schema is "deliberately the intermediate format the future external CPython 3 + ezdxf validator will consume... the contract between the in-Revit reader and the out-of-Revit checker" — a contract written and never fulfilled. For a structural BIM team this is the exact failure mode that erodes trust in an automated CAD-to-BIM conversion: a column silently placed 40 mm off a drawn centreline by a snap-tolerance rounding, a beam whose builder-side split-at-columns logic (`beam_cleanup.split_beams_at_columns`, re-exported at `report.py:41-43`) leaves a segment short of the drawn length, or a slab edge that took a fallback profile (`slab_outlines.check_profile`, `slabs.py:297-330`) instead of the drawn ring — none of these are caught today because the only geometric check that exists runs before a single element is built. Ideate BIMLink and CTC BIM Project Suite QA tools check parameters and schedules, not "does the placed geometry match the source drawing"; Naviate has no CAD-import fidelity checker; a Dynamo graph doing this would have to reimplement the midpoint-matching and per-layer bucketing that `geom/compare.py` already has, tested, for free.

**Description:**
1. The modeler runs cad2bim as normal (or opens a model that was already converted from a DXF in an earlier session) and picks a new button, **Round-Trip Check**, from the same panel.
2. The tool asks for the linked/original DXF path (reusing the same picker `dxf_linker` already shows, `ui_window.py:35`) and the set of structural categories to audit (columns, beams, slabs, walls, foundations — whatever the naming/layer convention already classifies via `classify/layers.py`).
3. It collects the live elements in those categories (either the whole model or the current selection), and for each one extracts an as-built `CurveRecord`-compatible geometry proxy: a beam's `LocationCurve` becomes a two-point line record, a column's `BoundingBox` footprint becomes a closed rectangle record, a slab's boundary `CurveLoop` becomes a polyline record — all tagged with the same layer/category key the CAD-to-BIM naming convention already assigns.
4. It re-reads the source DXF with the existing `dxf_reader.read_dxf(path)` (`script.py:398`) and calls the existing `compare.diff(as_built_records, dxf_records, tol_ft)` unchanged, with `tol_ft` taken from the same `compare_tol_mm` tolerance already exposed on the Tolerances tab (`config.py:37`, `ui_window.py:779/839`).

## 2026-09-26 05:42 UTC

**Idea name:** Curved Pad & Free-Form Peripheral Tie Placer — gives the structural pipeline the one geometry primitive it has never once used, an `Arc`, closing SCOPE-6 (`RC Automation.pushbutton/todo-list.md:334-337`, "`RebarUpdateCurvesData` for pad shapes that shape-driven bars cannot follow... a different constraint API from the one this tool uses, which is why it is scope and not a feature") so a circular or segmental pile cap, silo ring beam or rounded raft corner can be drawn accurately and reinforced with bars that actually curve, instead of the faceted polygon every other tool here — and the market's paid rebar add-ins — settle for

**Potential:**
Every outline this toolkit draws or reinforces is built from exactly one primitive: a straight `Line`. `structural/footings.py:236-262` builds a pad's `CurveLoop` with `loop.Append(Line.CreateBound(start, end))` for each vertex pair, and nothing else in that function ever constructs an `Arc`. On the rebar side it is the same story one layer down: `rc_automation/rebar_spec.py`'s whole footing-layer engine — `outline_for()` (`:307-311`), `bounds()`, `region_breaks()` (`:413-428`, "between two consecutive vertices of a polygon the edges are straight"), and `scan_segments()` (`:89-118`, explicitly built to handle "an L-shaped or waisted pad" by returning multiple straight crossings) — takes a flat list of `(x, y)` vertices and reasons entirely in straight polygon edges; and the geometry it hands to Revit is built by `structural/rebar_geometry.py:line_curves()` (`:66-88`), which does `curves.Add(Line.CreateBound(start, end))` for every single segment of every bar, U-bar leg included. This is genuinely sophisticated for anything a straight edge can describe — five-sided pads, pits cut out of a combined footing, gable-shaped pads split at each vertex — but there is no code path anywhere from pad outline to placed bar that can represent a curve, and `RC Automation.pushbutton/todo-list.md` names that gap itself, by its exact API, as SCOPE-6: `RebarUpdateCurvesData`, "a different constraint API from the one this tool uses" (`Rebar.CreateFromCurves` + `GetShapeDrivenAccessor`, per `structural/rebar_factory.py:344-380` and `:398`). A shape-driven `Rebar` sweeps one fixed straight-segment shape along a normal (`apply_layout()`, `:390-416`); it cannot make a single bar whose own centreline bends continuously, which is exactly what a ring of ties around a circular pile cap, or a peripheral bar following a rounded raft corner, needs. Circular and segmental pile caps are an everyday structural detail — piled foundations for columns near a boundary, silo and tank rings, rounded corners on a basement raft — and every BIM modeler's current option in Revit is either drawing an n-gon dense enough to look round and then placing dozens of straight tie segments by hand, or stepping outside this toolkit (and outside Revit's native rebar tools) entirely; the handful of paid marketplace add-ins that place curved/ring ties charge a per-seat subscription for exactly this one capability, and none of them are wired into this toolkit's own schedule-driven pipeline the way every other reinforcement layer here already is.

**Description:**
A new pushbutton, **Curved Pad Placer**, that reads a small extension to the existing FOOTING_PLACEMENT/FOOTING_TYPES sheets `footings.py` already parses (`commands/footings.py:10-14`) — the same `Outline` column, but each point may now optionally carry a bulge/radius so a pair of points describes an arc instead of a straight edge, the same convention DXF and most CAD outline formats already use, so a modeler can trace a curved pad straight off a linked CAD file rather than typing coordinates:

1. **The pad itself.** Extend `structural/footings.py`'s `CurveLoop` builder (`:236-262`) to emit `Arc.Create(...)` wherever a segment carries a bulge, alongside the existing `Line.CreateBound` for straight ones — the pad is still one `Floor.Create` call (`:327-329`), just with a mixed-curve profile instead of an all-straight one.
2. **The bars that can stay straight.** Any radial tie or straight main bar whose scan line only ever crosses straight edges keeps running through the existing `rebar_spec.py`/`rebar_geometry.py` pipeline unchanged — a circular pad's main bars across the middle are still straight lines of varying length, exactly as `plan_footing_layer()` already computes for any other non-rectangular pad.
3. **The bars that cannot.** For a peripheral tie or a bar whose own centreline must follow the curved edge, place it first as a normal, roughly-shaped `Rebar` (any valid `CreateFromCurves` shape, since Revit requires one to create the element at all), then call `RebarUpdateCurvesData` on it to overwrite its actual centreline with the true arc-derived point set — one bar, one real curve, not a fan of short straight facets.
4. **One dialog, two shapes of geometry.** The pushbutton's own UI is the same picked-outline / schedule-row flow every other placement command here already uses (`_placement.run`, per `commands/footings.py:32-40`); the arc handling is invisible to the modeler except that the pad comes out round instead of many-sided.

## 2026-09-25 00:40 UTC

**Idea name:** Phase Assignment Auditor & Batch Re-Phaser — computes what each element's `Phase Created`/`Phase Demolished` *should* be from its level (and, where the mapping says so, from a demolished-without-a-modelled-replacement heuristic), flags every disagreement, and batch-corrects it, closing the one Revit-native staging mechanism this entire toolkit has only ever copied blindly, never read, decided, or checked

**Potential:**
A repo-wide grep for `PHASE_CREATED` and `PHASE_DEMOLISHED` across every `script.py` and every `anongee_toolkit` module returns exactly two hits, both on the same two lines: `ConvertFloor.pushbutton/script.py:895-897`, inside `copy_instance_params()`, where the two `BuiltInParameter`s are copied — alongside `ELEM_PARTITION_PARAM`, the workset — straight from a source element onto its recreated counterpart, with the comment `"# phase first: it can cascade onto other values"` (`script.py:894`). That is a preserve, not a decision: it never asks whether the source's phase was right to begin with, and every other command in the repo is silent on the subject entirely — `VIEW_PHASE`, `PhaseFilter`, `doc.Phases` and `ElementOnPhaseStatus` return **zero hits anywhere in `AnonGee.extension`**. RC Automation's own four placement commands confirm the gap from the creation side: `columns.py`, `beams.py`, `footings.py` and `slabs.py` all route through the shared `commands/_placement.py::run()` (`_placement.py:20-`), whose `apply` callback writes geometry, type, level and every schedule-mapped parameter onto a freshly created element — but never once touches `PHASE_CREATED`, so every element RC Automation places lands wherever `doc.Phases`'s currently active phase happens to be pointed at run time, regardless of which storey or which stage the sheet row actually describes. The sheet format itself already half-invites the word without ever meaning it: `rc_automation/placement.py:55` defines `_STOREY = ("storey", "story", "lift", "stage")` — a modeler who names a placement-sheet column `Stage`, meaning *construction phase*, gets it silently consumed as one more spelling of *floor level* instead, with no error and no way to tell the two apart from the sheet alone. The project's own roadmap wants the real thing and still doesn't have it: `todo-list.md:1019` (`FEAT-45`) records the owner's explicit ask for the rebar schedule to carry "**Phase or Procurement**, which must exist on **both** the concrete and the rebar parameters so a client can be told what a stage costs" — but that is a schedule *report* column; even once it ships, an element created by `columns.sync`/`footings.sync` for "Stage 2" and one created moments later for "Stage 1" in the same run would still land in whichever single Revit `Phase` was active for the whole session, so a phase-filtered plan or a Phase-split quantity schedule would show them identically and silently defeat the exact stage-cost split FEAT-45 exists to report. Outside this toolkit, mis-phasing is one of the most common and highest-consequence everyday mistakes on any renovation, addition or multi-stage RC project: an element pasted in from another model or another discipline's link defaults to whatever phase happens to be active in the *target* document, not the one it was drawn for; a wall that a later stage's demolition drawing shows removed is easy to forget to mark `Phase Demolished` on, so the demo plan still shows it standing; a modeler who forgets to switch the active phase before modelling silently mis-phases everything drawn that session with zero warning from Revit. Revit's own UI has no audit for any of this — Properties shows Phase Created/Demolished one element at a time, a Phase-filtered schedule can list the wrong ones but cannot compute what they *should* be, and there is no "does this element's phase agree with its level or its stage" check anywhere in the product. On the market, whole-suite paid add-ins (Ideate BIMLink, CTC BIM Project Suite) can bulk set Phase Created/Demolished via a schedule export/edit/reimport round trip, but that is a blind overwrite typed in by a human, exactly the workaround the already-logged Parameter Migrator and Workset Assigner ideas name for their own parameters — nothing free or paid derives the *expected* phase from an element's level or location and flags the disagreement.

**Description:**
1. **Mapping table** — a small, saved Level → Phase table (reusing whichever level-name vocabulary `AutoLevel.pushbutton` has already built for the project, rather than a second freeform level list), plus one toggle rule: an element whose `Phase Demolished` is earlier than the model's latest phase but has no later-phase element occupying the same location is flagged as a **likely missed replacement**, since a demolition with nothing modelled to replace it is usually an unfinished edit, not a real design intent.
2. **Scan** — every element in scope (selection / active view / whole model, category-filterable) read via `PHASE_CREATED`/`PHASE_DEMOLISHED` and its hosting `Level`; each is compared against the mapping table's expected phase for that level, and against the demolished-without-replacement heuristic.
3. **Checklist preview** — one row per disagreement: element id, category, level, current phase, proposed phase, reason — on the same `CheckList` shell (`anongee_toolkit/ui/checklist.py`) every other batch tool in the repo already runs on; level-derived mismatches pre-ticked, the demolished-without-replacement heuristic left unticked since it needs a human look rather than an automatic fix.
4. **Apply** — every ticked row's `Phase Created`/`Phase Demolished` is rewritten inside one `RevitTransaction` (`revit/transactions.py:71-`), one undo step for the whole batch.
5. **RC Automation hook** (later phase of this same idea) — a genuine `Phase` sheet column, resolved through the same mapping table and distinct from the existing `stage`-as-storey alias at `placement.py:55`, threaded into `_placement.py`'s shared `apply` callback so a newly created column, beam, footing or slab is phase-correct the moment it is placed instead of needing this auditor to catch it afterwards.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit.revit.phasing` module: `phase_by_name(doc)` (name → `Phase`, off `doc.Phases`), `expected_phase(level_name, mapping)`, `read_element_phase(elem)`/`set_element_phase(elem, phase, demolished=False)` — thin, `StorageType`-agnostic wrappers in the same style `revit/parameters.py::get_parameter_value`/`set_parameter_value` already establish for every other parameter write in the repo.
- New pushbutton bundle (`bundle.yaml`/`script.py`/`README.md`) in `Essential.panel/Modify.stack/`, alongside `JoinPriority.pushbutton`/`ToggleLinked.pushbutton`/`UnjoinByCategory.pushbutton` — the existing home for whole-model hygiene passes with no Excel bridge required.
- Level mapping loads from `AutoLevel.pushbutton`'s own already-built level table rather than duplicating a second level list the two tools could drift apart on.
- The RC Automation hook extends `commands/_placement.py::run()`'s `apply` signature with an optional phase resolver, and disambiguates `placement.py:55`'s `_STOREY` tuple so `"stage"` stops being consumed as a storey synonym once a sheet actually means construction phase by it.

**Future update:**
- Cross-check `Phase Created`/`Phase Demolished` against each sheet's own `View Phase` + `Phase Filter` pairing, so a demolition plan actually hides what it is supposed to hide instead of just carrying the right parameter values unseen.
- Extend the mapping to Rooms/Areas for an architectural handover, alongside the already-logged Room Finish Auto-Fill & Mismatch Auditor.
- Wire into the already-logged Design Option Scheme Comparator & Promoter, since a promoted option's elements often need re-phasing in the same transaction its Option Set is dissolved in.

## 2026-09-24 15:40 UTC

**Idea name:** Join Priority — Same-Category Tie-Break, closing the one join outcome `JoinPriority.pushbutton` names in its own docstring and then walks straight past: two elements of the *same* category meeting at a joint, where a category-rank list has nothing left to compare

**Potential:**
`JoinPriority.pushbutton` (`Essential.panel/Modify.stack/JoinPriority.pushbutton/script.py`) already solves cross-category join order well — a saved, reorderable category list, whole-model auto-join for touching-but-unjoined elements, and an edge-refresh pass for stale dashed linework — but it states its own ceiling in its top-level docstring in plain words: *"Same-category joins are left untouched in this version"* (`script.py:18`), and the code backs the claim exactly: every joined pair is classified once by `_cat_name(a) == _cat_name(b)`, and a same-category match is never added to `order_pairs` — it is only ever counted, both at scan time (`elif na == nb: same_cat += 1`, `script.py:359-360`) and again for newly auto-joined pairs (`else: same_cat += 1`, `script.py:428-431`) — then reported back to the modeler as a bare number, *"Same-category joins skipped: N"* (`script.py:472`), with no way to act on it. That is not a corner case on an RC structural model; it is the single most common join decision a modeler makes by hand every day: a primary (girder) beam framing into a column has to cut every secondary (joist) beam that lands on it so the secondary reads as *supported by* the primary rather than continuous through it, and today nobody but Revit's own arbitrary "last modified wins" join order decides which one actually gets cut — the modeler finds out only when a section view shows the wrong beam running through, or a concrete-volume schedule silently double-counts the overlap because the wrong element was left uncut. `IsCuttingElementInJoin`/`SwitchJoinOrder`, the exact two API calls that would fix it, are already imported and already working in this same file (`script.py:447,451`) — they are simply never invoked for a same-category pair because the tool has no second axis to rank by once category ties. Repo-wide, `BuiltInParameter.INSTANCE_STRUCT_USAGE_PARAM` (Revit's native "Structural Usage" field on Structural Framing — Girder / Joist / Purlin / Other / Automatic, exactly the primary/secondary distinction this needs) returns **zero hits anywhere in `AnonGee.extension`** or `anongee_toolkit` (confirmed by grep), so nothing in this toolkit has ever read the one built-in field Revit already ships for this. On the market, this exact "same-category join tie-break" is not sold as a feature at all — CTC's and IMAGINiT's join/geometry-cleanup add-ins expose category-priority join order (the half this tool already has) but stop at the same wall Revit's own priority system does; the primary-vs-secondary-beam convention is universally handled by a modeler eyeballing the join and switching it by hand, one beam at a time, via the tiny on-screen join-order arrows.

**Description:**
Extends `JoinPriority.pushbutton` in place — same dialog, same saved config, same one-pass apply — rather than shipping as a second tool, since the two problems (rank across categories, rank within one) are one workflow with two axes:

1. **Read the tie-break signal, per category** — for `Structural Framing`, read `INSTANCE_STRUCT_USAGE_PARAM` and rank `Girder` above `Joist`/`Purlin` above `Other`/`Automatic`; for every other category (columns, footings, walls, floors), fall back to a size comparison — the larger of the two by net solid volume cuts the smaller, on the ordinary structural convention that the bigger member is the one already fully formed when the smaller one lands on it (a stepped/combined footing cutting the isolated pad it absorbs, a thicker transfer wall cutting a thinner partition wall of the same category).
2. **Surface it in the same dialog** — the existing category `ListBox` (`PRIORITY_XAML`, `script.py:41-73`) gains a small per-category "tie-break" column next to each row: `Structural Usage` (only offered where that parameter exists on the category), `Larger volume cuts smaller`, or `Leave as-is` (today's behaviour, kept as the default so nothing changes for a modeler who ignores the new column).
3. **Extend the classification, not replace it** — `na == nb` no longer means "skip"; it means "read the chosen tie-break for that category, and only skip the pair if the tie-break itself can't distinguish them (same Structural Usage value, or a volume difference under a configurable percentage tolerance so two visually-identical beams aren't flipped on floating-point noise)." That residual, genuinely-unresolvable count is what still gets reported as "skipped," now meaning something real instead of covering every same-category pair unconditionally.
4. **Same apply path** — a resolved same-category pair is pushed into the existing `order_pairs` list (`script.py:437-456`) and goes through the exact same `IsCuttingElementInJoin`/`SwitchJoinOrder` block every cross-category pair already uses, inside the same `TransactionGroup` — one undo entry, whether the run touched only cross-category joins, only same-category ones, or both.
5. **Result dialog** — the existing summary line (`script.py:467-474`) splits into "cross-category: switched/correct" and "same-category: switched/correct/skipped (tie could not be broken)", so a modeler can see at a glance whether the beam framing on this floor actually got sorted or needs a manual look.

**Implementation:**
- New helper in the same `script.py`: `_tie_break_key(elem, rule)` returning a sortable value — the `INSTANCE_STRUCT_USAGE_PARAM` enum's own rank for the `"Structural Usage"` rule, `anongee_toolkit.revit.geometry.get_solid_volume_m3(elem)` (`geometry.py:10-37`, already public API, already zero-call-sites in `AnonGee.tab`) for the `"Larger volume cuts smaller"` rule — or `None` for `"Leave as-is"`, which short-circuits straight back to today's skip behaviour.
- `config.tie_break` persisted alongside the existing `config.cat_order`/`config.autojoin`/`config.refresh_edges` (`script.py:329-332`), one saved choice per category name, remembered the same way the category order already is.
- `PriorityDialog`'s XAML gains a `ComboBox` per list row (offered rules filtered to what that category actually supports — `Structural Usage` only where `INSTANCE_STRUCT_USAGE_PARAM` resolves on a sampled instance of that category in the current selection), wired the same way `autojoin_cb`/`refresh_cb` already feed `_apply()` (`script.py:155-164`).
- The `elif na == nb:` branch (`script.py:359-360`) becomes: look up `config.tie_break.get(na)`, compute both elements' tie-break keys, and either append to `order_pairs` (keys differ) or increment `same_cat` (rule is "Leave as-is", or the keys tie within tolerance) — the exact same shape the cross-category branch already has, just fed a same-category key instead of the category-rank dict.

**Future update:**
- A third tie-break rule, `"Higher top elevation cuts lower"`, for the vertical-join case (a taller wall segment cutting a shorter same-type infill) once the volume rule is proven in production.
- Per-pair manual override list (pick two specific same-category elements and force a direction) for the rare case a modeler disagrees with every automatic rule — the same "checklist beats blanket automation" posture every other batch tool in this repo already holds to.
- Extend `Structural Usage`-based ranking into the already-logged Analytical-Physical Alignment Auditor's read layer, since a beam whose `Structural Usage` disagrees with its analytical role (a `Joist` carrying what the analytical model treats as a primary load path) is a modelling error this tie-break would otherwise just quietly act on.

And the two building blocks this idea needs to combine are both already sitting in the toolkit, unused for this purpose: `anongee_toolkit.revit.geometry.bounding_boxes_overlap()` (`geometry.py:40-59`) is exported from both `anongee_toolkit/__init__.py:108` and `anongee_toolkit/revit/__init__.py:13`, and its only real caller anywhere is `BIMGeneration.pushbutton/core.py:369-373`'s own hand-rolled private duplicate — nothing has ever called it on two bounding boxes drawn from two different documents' coordinate spaces. `anongee_toolkit.revit.parameters.get_parameter_value`/`set_parameter_value` (`parameters.py:12-112`) are fully StorageType-generic and operate purely on whatever `element` object is handed in, so nothing about their own signature stops them working on an `Element` pulled from a linked `Document` — they have simply never been asked to. - Room-category refinement calls `Document.GetRoomAtPoint(XYZ)` on the *linked* document — new to the repo; `Room`/`SpatialElement` has so far only ever been proposed same-document by Room Finish Auto-Fill & Mismatch Auditor.
- Same modeless `CheckList`/`WpfDialogBase` window shell, `RevitTransaction` context manager, and `openpyxl` export path every other batch tool in the repo already runs on; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`.

**Future update:**

- Saved link + category + parameter-mapping profile, reusable on a re-run after the architectural model issues a new Room layout — the same saved-profile posture already proposed for Parameter Migrator and Universal Renamer.
- Multi-link mode: match against two or more loaded links in one pass (Architecture for Room data, a civil/site link for Zone) instead of one link per run.

Paid whole-suite add-ins bundle something adjacent (CTC BIM Project Suite's parameter tools; Ideate BIMLink's spreadsheet round-trip for bulk parameter edits) but only as one feature inside a licensed, seat-priced suite, and BIMLink's own shape still round-trips through Excel rather than reading a live value straight off a picked element in-canvas. **Description:**
`Parameter Copy.pushbutton`, sibling to `Parameter Combine.pushbutton` and `FilterParameter.splitbutton` in `Advance.panel/`, same audience and same toolbox already there:

1. **Pick source** — one element, via `revit.selection.get_selected_elements` (pre-pick) or an interactive `PickObject` prompt; the dialog lists every instance parameter (and, through `get_parameter`'s own instance-then-type fallback, type parameters too) with a checkbox and its current value read through `get_parameter_value`.

The already-logged Lap & Starter-Bar Continuity Auditor (2026-09-14) also reads real placed geometry, but only within *one continuous vertical run* of the same column's own main bars across a storey joint. Neither one, nor anything else in the repo, ever asks whether *two different elements'* cages occupy the same space where they meet — a footing's top mesh sitting exactly where a column's main-bar cage lands on it, a beam's bottom bars threading past a column's ties at the joint, two independently-run RC Automation passes whose footings share a corner. That gap is not hypothetical for this specific codebase: RC Automation places real footing reinforcement today (`rebar_run.py:118-258`, `_plan_one_footing`/`place_footing`), but per the already-logged Column Reinforcement Placer idea (2026-09-16), it places **zero column bars** — `CRIT-3` in `todo-list.md:98-110` says so outright — so every column cage in a model touched by this toolkit today is hand-modelled, landing on a footing mesh the tool placed automatically, by a different person, at a different time, with no check that the two ever agree on where they can both fit. The raw material for the check already exists, unused for this purpose: `anongee_toolkit.structural.rebar_geometry.line_curves()` (`rebar_geometry.py:66-88`) already turns every bar into an exact world-space centreline `Curve` list before it is placed, and `rebar_spec.BarSpec` already carries `diameter_mm` alongside `points` on every single bar (`rebar_spec.py:172-178`) — centreline plus diameter is exactly what a bar-to-bar proximity test needs, and nothing downstream of `line_curves()` ever asks a second bar's curves the same question. For bars already in the model regardless of who placed them, the real Revit API already used elsewhere in the repo for reading rebar back — `RebarHostData.GetRebarsInHost()` (`rebar_factory.py:552-570`, `existing_stamped_rebar`) — only returns bars hosted *by* one element, so it cannot see a neighbouring host's bars at all; the native per-bar geometry call this idea actually needs, `Rebar.GetCenterlineCurves(...)`, is never called anywhere in the repo (`grep -rn "GetCenterlineCurves" AnonGee.extension` returns nothing). And the broad-phase filter this idea needs to avoid an all-pairs bar-curve scan across a whole model already exists, shared, tested and almost entirely unused: `anongee_toolkit.revit.geometry.bounding_boxes_overlap(bb1, bb2, tol=0.08)` (`geometry.py:40`) is exported from both `anongee_toolkit/__init__.py:108` and `anongee_toolkit/revit/__init__.py:13`, exercised only by the toolkit's own self-test (`tools/verify_toolkit.py:672-677`) — and its one real production caller is not even this shared function: `BIMGeneration.pushbutton/core.py:369` hand-rolls its *own* private copy, `_bounding_boxes_overlap(box_a, box_b, tolerance=-0.05)`, at a different default tolerance than the shared one, to flag column/beam box overlap during CAD import (`core.py:490`) — the exact "one function, two silently-diverging implementations" pattern the already-logged Shared Parameter GUID Doctor (2026-09-18) documents for parameter matching now sitting in the geometry helpers too. On the market, generic clash tools (Navisworks Clash Detective, Solibri) are the wrong shape for this specific question: a column and the beam framing into it are *supposed* to overlap as solids, so whole-element clash rules flag every real joint in the building as a hard clash and need heavy manual rule-tuning before they're usable at all, and neither tool understands "bar," only "element" — a beam's bottom-bar cage physically fouling a column's tie set reads to them as the beam-vs-column clash everyone already suppressed. Paid, seat-licensed rebar-specific detailing suites (AGACAD Rebar for Revit, Naviate Structure) do include a bar-level clash pass, sold as one feature inside a much larger bundle; nothing free checks bar-to-bar congestion at a structural joint using the exact centreline-plus-diameter data this repo's own rebar pipeline already computes for every bar it plans.

**Description:**
`Rebar Clash Checker.pushbutton`, a new sibling to `Rebar Cover Auditor.pushbutton` and `Lap & Starter-Bar Continuity Auditor.pushbutton` — same audience, same modeless-checklist shell, one more question about the same reinforcement:

1. **Scope** — whole model, active view or pre-selection of hosts (`OST_StructuralColumns`, `OST_StructuralFraming`, `OST_StructuralFoundation`, `OST_Walls`); a joint-radius setting (mm) controls how far past each host's own bounding box the scan looks for a neighbour's bars.
2. **Broad phase** — collect every rebar-bearing host in scope, expand each host's `BoundingBoxXYZ` by the joint radius, and pair up hosts whose expanded boxes overlap via `anongee_toolkit.revit.geometry.bounding_boxes_overlap()` — the shared helper finally given a real caller instead of only `tools/verify_toolkit.py` and a hand-rolled duplicate in `BIMGeneration`. Same-host pairs are skipped outright: that is what Rebar Cover Auditor already checks.
3. **Narrow phase** — for each surviving host pair, pull every placed `Rebar`/`RebarInSystem` element on each host (`FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(Rebar).OwnedByHost(host_id)`-equivalent, alongside the toolkit's own `existing_stamped_rebar` pattern for tool-placed bars), read each bar's real centreline via `Rebar.GetCenterlineCurves(adjustForSelfIntersection=True, ...)` and its diameter via `RebarBarType.BarDiameter`, and test every bar from host A against every bar from host B with a 3D segment-to-segment closest-distance check; a pair closer than the sum of their radii (plus a configurable clear-gap tolerance) is a hit.
4. **Report** — one row per clashing bar pair: both host ids/names, both bar roles (main/tie/stirrup/mesh, from the same `ROLE_*` vocabulary `rebar_spec`/`rebar_factory` already use), the overlap depth, a jump-to-element action that selects both bars and zooms the joint into view; severity split the same `Error`/`Warning` way `validation.py` already uses — an outright physical overlap is `Error`, a clearance below a configurable minimum but not yet overlapping is `Warning`.
5. **Report only** — this tool never moves or deletes a bar; it is read-and-flag, matching Rebar Cover Auditor's own posture, since the fix (reroute, restagger, or re-run RC Automation with adjusted cover/spacing) is a modelling decision, not one this tool should make silently.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit.structural.rebar_clash` module: `host_pairs_in_scope(docs, hosts, joint_radius_mm)` (wraps `bounding_boxes_overlap`), `bars_on_host(doc, host)` (native `FilteredElementCollector` + `Rebar`/`RebarInSystem`, filtered to elements actually hosted on the given element), `segment_distance(curve_a, curve_b)` (3D closest-point-between-two-line-segments, run per curve-pair from each bar's `GetCenterlineCurves()` output), `find_clashes(pairs, clear_gap_mm)` returning one record per hit.
- Reuses `rebar_geometry.to_xyz`/`line_curves`'s existing unit-conversion posture (mm in, feet out to the API and back) rather than a second conversion path.
- Same modeless checklist window shell (`anongee_toolkit.ui.hostwnd`/`checklist`/`theme`) and jump-to-element selection every other batch auditor in the repo already runs on; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`.
- Fixes the tolerance duplication found while researching this idea as a small, separate first commit: repoint `BIMGeneration.pushbutton/core.py:369`'s `_bounding_boxes_overlap` at the shared `anongee_toolkit.revit.geometry.bounding_boxes_overlap`, or explicitly document why BIMGeneration's `-0.05` default differs from the shared module's `0.08` if it turns out to be deliberate — right now nothing says which.

**Future update:**
- "Since last run" diff mode — flag only a clash newly introduced since the last check (a bar added, a cover changed, a re-run of RC Automation), the same re-run/diff shape already logged as a future item for Type Matrix Generator, Sheet Issue Kit and the Sleeve Coordinator.
- Once the already-logged Column Reinforcement Placer ships and RC Automation starts placing column mains/ties itself, run this checker automatically as a post-placement step on the new cage against whatever footing/beam bars already sit at its base — catching a congested joint the moment automation creates it, not on a later manual audit pass.
- Extend the host-pair scope to the already-logged Sleeve & Opening Coordinator's MEP-vs-structure clash data, so one joint report can eventually show "steel-vs-steel" and "steel-vs-sleeve" congestion side by side instead of two separate tools looking at the same joint.
- A minimum-clear-gap config per bar-role pair (main-vs-main needs more clearance than tie-vs-mesh), read from the same per-project override posture `slab_convert_config.json`/`column_lap_config.json` already establish, rather than one flat tolerance for every kind of bar meeting.

## 2026-09-21 10:40 UTC

**Idea name:** Naming Convention Auditor — walk every Column, Beam, Footing, Slab and Stair type and schedule mark already in the model, recompute what the house convention's own pattern engine says each one should be called, and flag every disagreement, closing the one-directional gap in a rule engine this repo has so far only ever used to write, never to check

**Potential:**
The toolkit already has a full, project-editable house naming convention — `PATTERNS` in `anongee_toolkit/rc_automation/naming_sheet.py:30-40` (`"{b} X {h}"` for a column, `"{l} x {w} x {t}mm"` for a footing, `"{prefix}{n}"` for every schedule mark), overridable from a workbook's own `NAMING` sheet via `naming_sheet.parse()`, rendered deterministically through `naming_sheet.render(patterns, key, **values)` (`naming_sheet.py:173-189`). `grep -rn "naming_sheet.render" AnonGee.extension` finds exactly three call sites, and only two ever touch Revit: `commands/_sheets.py:63` (naming a **type about to be created**) and `commands/_marks.py:89` (naming a **mark about to be written**); the third, `commands/naming.py:95,125`, only regenerates the `NAMING` sheet's own documentation column and writes nothing to a model. There is no fourth call site anywhere that takes a type or instance **already in the model** and checks its current name against what `render()` would produce from that same element's own live dimensions — the engine has a write path and a describe-itself path, and no read-and-compare path at all. This is not a cosmetic gap: `typemaker.choose()` (`anongee_toolkit/structural/typemaker.py:70-109`) documents, in the project owner's own words from 2026-08-27, that *"the house name is the identity"* — when RC Automation looks for a type to reuse, a same-sized type under any other name is refused ("Deliberately no further passes... a type of the right size under another name is *not* this type", lines 106-109), and a **new** type is created instead. So a footing that drifted from the current convention (hand-renamed, imported via `cad2bim`, or left over from before a house-convention change) does not just look inconsistent in a schedule — every later RC Automation run silently manufactures a second, differently-named type of the identical size next to it, which is exactly the duplicate-type bloat the already-logged Type Consolidator (2026-09-13 00:39) has to clean up *after* the fact, on a schedule this repo's own naming engine could catch *before* it happens. On the market, no generic tool could ever check this: the convention is per-project and workbook-defined (`{b} X {h}` today, anything else tomorrow), so only code that already reads the same `NAMING` sheet — which exists nowhere outside this repo — can compute what "correct" even means here; paid whole-discipline QA suites (Naviate Structure, Ideate-class checkers) audit against fixed, generic naming templates, never a project's own live, Excel-editable pattern table.

**Description:**
`Naming Auditor.pushbutton`, sibling to `Bulk Rename.pulldown` in `Essential.panel/Bulk Tool.stack/`, since it is a batch check-then-fix tool for the same daily audience:

1. **Scope + convention source** — whole model, active view or pre-selection, restricted to the five `PATTERNS`-wired kinds `naming_sheet.WIRED` already names (`column`, `beam`, `footing`, `slab`, `stair`, plus the three `*_mark` keys); an optional workbook path re-uses `naming_sheet.parse()` so a project mid-transition to a new convention audits against its **current** rule, not a hardcoded default — same "optional workbook, defaults otherwise" posture `naming.py:20` already documents.
2. **Type pass** — for every `FamilySymbol` in a wired category, read its own governing dimensions the same way `typemaker.size()`/`_set_dimension()` (`typemaker.py:250-269`) already resolve them from a symbol's own parameters, feed those values into `naming_sheet.render(patterns, key, **values)`, and fold-compare (`naming_sheet._fold`, `naming.fold`) the result against the type's actual `Element.Name`.
3. **Mark pass** — for every placed instance, recompute the expected mark the same shape `_marks.py:89` already calls (`prefix` + running `n`), compare against the instance's current `ALL_MODEL_MARK`/`S_ScheduleMark` value.
4. **Report table** — one row per mismatch: category, element/type id, current name, expected name, a jump-to-element action; sortable, and grouped by type so ten drifted instances of one type show as one row to fix, not ten.
5. **Batch fix** — ticked rows only. A type rename goes through `typemaker.named_sibling`/`sanitise` (`typemaker.py:34-67`) rather than a raw `Element.Name =`, because this repo has already hit and solved "two types in one family can't share a name" once (`Duplicate` raising when the target name is taken, `named_sibling`'s whole reason for existing) and a second, independent solve is the risk worth skipping. A mark fix writes the parameter directly, the same read-only-checked `get_Parameter(...).Set(...)` shape `typemaker.set_type_mark` (`typemaker.py:272-286`) already uses.
6. **Export** — `openpyxl`, same path every other batch tool in the repo already writes its report through.

**Implementation:**
- New module `anongee_toolkit.rc_automation.naming_audit`: `expected_type_name(patterns, key, symbol)` (wraps `typemaker.size`'s own parameter-name tables plus `naming_sheet.render`) and `expected_mark(patterns, key, prefix, n)` (mirrors `_marks.py:89`'s call shape exactly, so "what a mark should be" is computed identically whether a job places it fresh or an audit checks it after the fact).
- Collector: one `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(FamilySymbol)` pass per category in `naming_sheet.WIRED`, paired with one instance pass per category for marks.
- Fix path reuses `typemaker.named_sibling`/`sanitise`/`set_type_mark` rather than re-implementing Revit's type-uniqueness handling a second time.
- Same modeless checklist window shell (`anongee_toolkit.ui.hostwnd`/`checklist`/`theme`) and `openpyxl` export every other batch tool already runs on; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md`.
- Optional workbook input reuses `rc_automation.excel_engine.read_grid` + `naming_sheet.parse()` exactly as `commands/naming.py` already does, so "read the project's convention" is not a second implementation of the first.

**Future update:**
- Wire as its own bridge command (`naming.audit`), registered in `commands/__init__.py:register_all()` beside the existing `naming.refresh`, so a pre-issue check can run headless through the same bridge `levels.sync`/`grids.sync` already use, per the already-logged Grid Sync (2026-09-19 05:41) posture for exposing a bridge-only capability as a pushbutton (and here, the reverse: exposing a pushbutton capability to the bridge).
- Run the audit automatically as a pre-flight step inside RC Automation itself, so a run reports "3 types will duplicate because their current name doesn't match the house convention" before it places anything, instead of the duplicate simply appearing.
- Extend `PATTERNS`/the audit to Sheets, Views and Grids (ISO 19650 / BEP-style rules) once column/beam/footing/slab/stair prove the audit-then-fix loop, giving the already-logged Universal Renamer (2026-09-11 14:30) a validation pass its own token-substitution engine has no way to check itself against.

**Idea name:** Reinforcement Density Heatmap — live kg/m³ steel-to-concrete ratio per column, beam, footing, slab and wall, painted straight onto the model as a graded colour overlay instead of buried in a schedule column, finally wiring the toolkit's own dead volume reader to its own dead weight data

**Potential:**
A modeler or a design lead has exactly one way today to sanity-check "is this column over-reinforced, or is that footing suspiciously light" — open the bar-bending schedule, find every bar tagged to that one host, add up the weight by hand, and divide by a volume nobody has actually computed, because Revit's own schedules report length and count, never a host's net concrete volume. On anything past a handful of elements this check simply never happens, so a transfer beam quietly detailed at 400 kg/m³ (visibly congested, unbuildable cover-to-cover) or a footing at 40 kg/m³ (undersized against its own design intent) ships to IFC drawings and only surfaces on-site when a bar-bender says the cage won't fit in the shutter. The two building blocks this needs already exist in this repo and have never been introduced to each other: `get_solid_volume_m3(element)` (`anongee_toolkit/revit/geometry.py:10-37`) walks any element's solids — including nested `GeometryInstance` geometry — to a net m³ figure, is re-exported as public API in `anongee_toolkit/__init__.py:17,107,222` and `anongee_toolkit/revit/__init__.py:13,37`, and has **zero call sites in any `AnonGee.tab/**/script.py`** (confirmed by `grep -rn "get_solid_volume_m3" AnonGee.extension`, whose only hits are the definition and its own two export declarations — the same dead-export finding the already-logged Design Option Comparator (2026-09-21 00:42) made about this exact function, for a different consumer). On the other side, `BBS Generator.pushbutton/core/bar_record.py:15,25,42-43` already computes `unit_weight_kg_per_m`/`total_weight_kg` per bar via `rebar_reader.py:246-247`'s `standard_module.UNIT_WEIGHTS` lookup, and `rebar_reader.py:68-83`'s `_host_member_type()` already resolves the actual host **element object** (`host = doc.GetElement(host_id)`, line 72) for every rebar it reads — but the `BarRecord` constructor at `rebar_reader.py:250-259` only keeps the host's derived `member_name`/`member_type` **strings**, discarding the host `ElementId` itself (the first element of `_host_member_type()`'s return tuple is thrown away with `_` at line 191, and `revit_element_id=rebar.Id.IntegerValue` at line 257 records the *rebar's* own ID, never the host's). So the schedule this repo already generates has a weight number sitting right next to a member name, and a volume function sitting one folder over that could turn that into a ratio — and nothing has ever connected the two, because the one field that would let them line up (the host's `ElementId`) is computed and then dropped on the floor. On the visualization side, the repo's only per-element graphic-override code, `anongee_toolkit/cad2bim/builders/view_filters.py`, colours whole *categories* one fixed tint each via `ParameterFilterElement`+`OverrideGraphicSettings` (`KINDS` tuple, `apply()`) — it has no notion of a computed, per-element, graduated value, and `grep -rn "SetElementOverrides" AnonGee.extension` returns **zero hits anywhere in the repo**, meaning `View.SetElementOverrides(ElementId, OverrideGraphicSettings)` — the one Revit API call that can paint two columns of the same category two different colours based on a number that isn't a stored parameter — has never been called once. RC Automation's own `rc_automation/validation.py` (`_validate_column_rebar`, `_validate_footing_rebar`, `_check_cage_fits`) checks bar counts, diameters, spacing and cage-fit *before* placement, against its own Excel-driven spec — a schema validator for what RC Automation is about to build, not a live geometric ratio read against whatever rebar (native, imported, or RC Automation's own) already sits in the model today. On the market, native Revit reports no density figure at all; paid whole-discipline QA suites (Naviate Structure, Ideate/Sidekick-class model checkers) audit modeling hygiene (naming, warnings, duplicates) but none of them compute or paint a steel-weight-to-concrete-volume ratio; standalone rebar-takeoff add-ins (the closest commercial category to BBS Generator itself) output a weight *table* and stop there — none turn it into a live, colour-coded model overlay.

**Description:**
`Reinforcement Density Heatmap.pushbutton`, sibling to `BBS Generator.pushbutton` in `Dev.panel/col1.stack/` (the stack that already owns the rebar-weight engine this reuses) or cross-referenced from `RC Automation.pushbutton`'s own panel, since both are its natural data sources:

1. **Scope** — pre-selection, active view, or whole model, same three-way picker `ConvertFloor.pushbutton`/`Design Option Comparator` already use, restricted to Column/Beam/Foundation/Floor/Wall — exactly the five categories `rebar_reader.py:27-30`'s `_HOST_CAT_MAP` already recognises as rebar hosts, so scoping never invents a new category list.
2. **Aggregate weight per host** — for each `Rebar`/`RebarInSystem` in scope, `GetHostId()` (the same call `_host_member_type()` already makes) groups bars by host `ElementId` instead of by the derived name string BBS Generator settles for today; per-bar weight reuses `rebar_reader.py`'s own `total_length_mm × standard_module.UNIT_WEIGHTS[diameter_mm] / 1000.0` formula rather than re-deriving a second one, so a density figure and a BBS Generator export always agree on what one bar weighs.
3. **Volume per host** — `get_solid_volume_m3(host)`, this function's first production call anywhere in the repo, one per host element (not per bar), cached per `ElementId` for the run.
4. **Ratio + band** — `density_kg_m3 = total_bar_weight_kg / (volume_m3 or float("inf"))` (zero-volume hosts report "no geometry" rather than a divide-by-zero), bucketed into a 5-stop band (configurable per member type, since a footing's sane range differs from a column's — e.g. Column: light <100, typical 100–200, heavy 200–300, congested >300 kg/m³) against a starting default table a project can override.

A legend panel shows the band-to-colour key. A second click clears every override this run applied (element IDs kept in memory for the session), leaving nothing behind the way a filter-based approach would.
7. **Export** — same `openpyxl` path `BBS Generator.pushbutton`/`Export Schedule.pushbutton` already use, one row per host with weight/volume/density/band, so a QA pass leaves a documented record alongside the visual one.

**Implementation:**

- Reuses `standard_module.UNIT_WEIGHTS` from whichever `BBS Generator.pushbutton/standards/*.py` module the project already has selected, imported rather than duplicated, so a unit-weight table only ever lives in one place.
- Same modeless window shell (`anongee_toolkit.ui.hostwnd`/`checklist`/`theme`) and `openpyxl` export path every other batch tool in the repo already runs on; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md` per the root README's versioned-tool layout.

**Future update:**
- Feed a confirmed-congested host straight into the already-logged Rebar Cover Auditor (2026-09-16 00:39) and Lap & Starter-Bar Continuity Auditor (2026-09-14 15:39) as a combined "why is this member flagged" QA package, one host, three checks, one report.

This is a distinct gap from the already-logged **Pour Break Manager** (2026-09-13 05:39), whose own volume read is scoped to a modeler-drawn pour boundary *within* one option and whose write-up says no volume helper exists "anywhere in `anongee_toolkit/structural/`" — true for that folder, but `revit/geometry.py` sits one level up and is the function this idea would make the first real caller of. On the market, native Revit shows no quantity delta between Design Options at all; Ideate Explorer/Sidekick and Naviate/Symetri's Model Checker audit *existing* model health but never compare or promote Design Options, and a genuine option-comparison workflow otherwise lives only inside full paid 5D/cost-estimating suites (Assemble, CostX) that require a separate license and a model export — nothing free does a same-session, Revit-native compare-then-commit on Option Sets.

**Description:**
`Design Option Comparator.pushbutton` (new tool, `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack`, sibling to `ConvertFloor.pushbutton`/`DrawFloor.pushbutton` — the one existing precedent for this API surface, and the stack that already owns "read live structural geometry, act in batch" tools) runs in one window:

1. **List Option Sets** — `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(DB.DesignOptionSet).ToElements()`, one row per set, expandable to its member options (`DesignOptionSet.Options`, each a `DesignOption` with `.Name`/`.IsPrimary`), the repo's first-ever enumeration of this API surface rather than the single activation-guard read `ConvertFloor.pushbutton` already does.
2. **Scope the compare** — pick categories to include (Structural Columns, Framing, Foundations, Floors/Slabs, Walls by default — the same categories the rest of this toolkit already treats as structural), same three-way whole-model/active-view/selection picker `ConvertFloor.pushbutton` already offers, here constrained to elements whose `DesignOption` falls inside the picked set.
3. **Compute per-option quantities** — for every option in the set, `FilteredElementCollector(doc)` filtered to that option's elements in the picked categories, summing `get_solid_volume_m3()` per category (concrete volume being the number a structural reviewer actually wants) alongside a plain element count per category — the first production call this shared function has ever had.
4. **Preview checklist** (`anongee_toolkit.ui.checklist.CheckList`, `anongee_toolkit.ui.hostwnd`/`theme`, the same shell every other multi-step tool in the repo runs on) — a side-by-side table, one column per option: total volume, per-category breakdown, element count, and which option is currently `IsPrimary`; a single radio-style pick selects the option to **promote**, defaulting to none selected so nothing is deletable by accident.
5. **Promote** — one `TransactionGroup` (the same rollback-safe wrapper `ConvertFloor.pushbutton`/`JoinPriority.pushbutton`/RC Automation's own placement pipeline already use): delete every element belonging to every option in the set *other than* the picked one, then dissolve the Option Set itself, folding the surviving option's elements back into the main model the way Revit's own "make primary and delete others" behavior works when done by hand — except reviewed and committed in one step instead of a manual multi-dialog slog.
6. **Report** — per-option volume/count table plus the promote outcome (elements deleted, Option Set dissolved), exportable via the same `openpyxl` path `Export Schedule.pushbutton`/`BBS Generator.pushbutton` already use, so a design-review decision leaves a documented before/after record instead of just a changed model.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit.revit.design_options` module: `list_option_sets(doc)` wrapping `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(DB.DesignOptionSet)`, `elements_in_option(doc, option, categories)` filtering a category-scoped collector by each element's `DesignOption.Id` matching the target option's `Id` (the exact property `ConvertFloor.pushbutton/script.py:1183` already reads one element at a time, generalized to a whole-option collection pass).
- Volume/count aggregation calls `anongee_toolkit.revit.geometry.get_solid_volume_m3()` per element, summed per category per option — this module's first real caller, promoting it from a documented-but-dead export to production code; failures already return `0.0` rather than raising, so one bad solid never blanks an option's whole total.
- Promote step wraps `Document.Delete(ElementId)` per losing-option element inside the same `TransactionGroup` shape `ConvertFloor.pushbutton` already commits its multi-step conversions through, followed by the API's own Option Set removal call so the set itself doesn't linger empty after its losing members are gone.
- Same modeless window shell (`anongee_toolkit.ui.hostwnd`/`checklist`/`theme`) and `openpyxl` report path every other batch tool in the repo already runs on; own `bundle.yaml`/`README.md` per the root README's versioned-tool layout.
- Reuses `ConvertFloor.pushbutton`'s own `el_name()`/`eid_val()` helpers for consistent element-naming and `ElementId` comparison rather than a second implementation of either.

**Future update:**
- Extend the per-option comparison beyond volume/count to cost, once a project's own material cost-per-m³ table is known (feeding the same `openpyxl` report row), turning "which scheme is smaller" into "which scheme is cheaper."
- A non-destructive "export comparison only" mode that produces the side-by-side report without ever promoting, for design-review packages where the decision isn't final yet.
- Nested Option Set support — a set containing an option that itself hosts a secondary Option Set (a scheme choice within a scheme choice) — once a project actually needs one, rather than assuming every set is flat.
- Feed a confirmed promote straight into **Sheet Issue Kit**'s (2026-09-15 15:40) since-last-run diff, so a design-option decision shows up as "what changed since the last issue" the same way a standards sync or a sheet re-export already would.
