## 2026-10-04 00:40 UTC

**Idea name:** PDF Markup → Revision Cloud Importer — reads a reviewer's marked-up sheet-set PDF (Bluebeam Revu or Acrobat clouds + comments) and batch-creates matching native Revit `RevisionCloud` elements with the comment text attached, closing the one external-review round trip this toolkit has never built despite already having a working "read an external file, classify its marks, place native geometry" pipeline in `cad2bim`

**Potential:**
Every reviewed set comes back the same way: a consultant, client or checker marks up a printed/exported PDF in Bluebeam or Acrobat — a cloud around a clash, a typed comment beside it — and a modeler has to open that PDF, eyeball where each cloud sits on the matching Revit sheet, and redraw it by hand with the native Revision Cloud sketch tool, then retype the comment into the cloud's Comments field. On a 40-sheet issue with a hundred markups, that is a full day of visual estimation and retyping, and every redrawn cloud is a guess at the original's exact location rather than a copy of it. A repo-wide `grep -rn "RevisionCloud" --include=*.py .` returns zero hits — nothing in this codebase has ever created one — and there is no PDF-*parsing* dependency anywhere either: the only PDF-adjacent code is `BBS Generator.pushbutton/output/pdf_exporter.py`, which only *writes* PDFs via `fpdf`, and `lib/py3/ezdxf/addons/drawing/pymupdf.py`, which only wraps PyMuPDF as an optional DXF-to-PDF *export* renderer inside the vendored `ezdxf` package — neither ever reads an annotation out of an existing PDF. Nothing on the market closes this loop either: Bluebeam Studio Sessions and Autodesk Construction Cloud's markup/issue tools both keep a cloud inside their own viewer and hand back only a flattened PDF or a generic issue record, never a native Revit `RevisionCloud` tied back to the sheet it was marked on — so even paid review platforms stop one step short of the thing a modeler actually has to do next.

**Description:**
`PDF Markup Import.pushbutton`, a new button in `Essential.panel` alongside the other batch, preview-gated builders:
1. **Pick inputs** — one or more markup PDFs plus the current project's sheet set.
2. **Match pages to sheets** — auto-match each PDF page to a `ViewSheet` by the sheet number read from the page's own title-block text (the same text layer Revit's PDF export always burns in), falling back to a manual pairing grid when a match is ambiguous.
3. **Read markups** — for each matched page, read every `Square`/`Polygon`("Cloud")/`FreeText` annotation from the PDF's own `/Annots` array, pulling its rectangle or vertex list plus its comment text and author.
4. **Map coordinates** — convert each annotation's PDF-page position to sheet space using the page size vs. the sheet's printable outline and print scale, then to the sheet's model-space point.
5. **Preview grid** — one row per detected markup: sheet, comment text, author, a mapping-confidence flag (anything near a page edge or a rotated/skewed export gets flagged for manual confirmation rather than guessed).
6. **Create** — nothing is drawn until rows are ticked; one `Transaction` then creates a native `RevisionCloud` per ticked row against the chosen Revision, with the markup's comment written to its Comments parameter and author to a shared parameter — turning an external redline into a trackable, schedulable, filterable native element instead of a flattened picture redrawn by eye.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/markup/pdf_reader.py`: `parse_annotations(pdf_path)` → per-page list of `(subtype, rect_or_vertices, contents, author)`, using PyMuPDF (`fitz`) for the actual `/Annots` read — the same library already vendored (if AGPL-licensing is acceptable) inside `ezdxf`'s own optional PDF renderer, run through the repo's existing `CPython3 engine.pushbutton`-proven CPython3 pattern since IronPython can't load it directly.
- `anongee_toolkit/markup/coordinate_map.py`: `pdf_point_to_sheet(page_size, pdf_xy, sheet_outline, print_scale)` and `sheet_to_model(sheet, point)` — pure, Revit-free, unit-testable functions, the same posture `cad2bim`'s `geom/compare.py` and `layers.py` already take for their own coordinate and classification math.
- `anongee_toolkit/markup/cloud_builder.py`: `create_revision_cloud(doc, sheet, model_points, revision_id, comment, author)` wrapping `Document.Create.NewRevisionCloud`.
- `Essential.panel/PDF Markup Import.pushbutton/`: `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (PDF picker + sheet-match grid + preview/create grid), `bundle.yaml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `icon.png` — the same per-button file set every sibling pushbutton already ships.
- Own `todo-list.md` inside the bundle naming v1 scope (axis-aligned, non-rotated single-page PDF exports only; one Revision per import batch) and the deferred items below.

**Future update:**
- Rotated/skewed-scan support via a 3-point manual calibration pick, for a markup PDF that came from a photographed or skewed scan rather than a direct export.
- Two-way sync: export the model's own open revision clouds back out to a markup PDF for a reviewer who doesn't have Revit, closing the loop in the other direction.

On the market, a saved/reusable filter library with one-click multi-view apply is sold only bundled inside paid production suites (BIM One's "Smart Filters", CTC BIM Tools, Rhythm's filter tools, IMAGINiT Utilities) as one line item of a much larger per-seat licence; nothing free turns a filter you already built for one job into the native graphic-override object Revit needs for the other.

**Description:**
`View Filter Generator.pushbutton`, a new sibling in `Advance.panel/FilterParameter.splitbutton`, reusing Multi Filter Parameter's own scope/category/condition-row UI almost unchanged:
1. **Scope + categories + conditions** — the exact same three controls Multi Filter Parameter already ships (`rb_whole`/`rb_view`/`rb_selection`, the category checklist, the parameter/operator/value row grid with its AND/ALL vs OR/ANY toggle), because a Revit `ParameterFilterElement` needs precisely the same three inputs: a category set, a rule set, and an AND/OR combination — scope only narrows which categories the picker even offers, since the filter itself always has to be category + rule, never scoped to "current selection" the way a one-off parameter edit can be.
2. **Live match preview** — reuses `_apply_filter`'s existing count-of-matches readout so a modeler sees how many elements qualify before anything is created, the same safety net the parameter-edit path already gives for free.
3. **Name + override** — a filter name field, then the native Visibility/Graphics override picker (line colour, line weight, line pattern, surface pattern/colour, halftone, transparency, surface transparency) via a thin WPF wrapper around the same `OverrideGraphicSettings` fields the V/G dialog edits, with a "filter visible" checkbox per target view.
4. **Pick target views** — a multi-select view checklist (same per-view multi-select list `Copy Rebar Visibility.pushbutton/script.py:125-134` already ships, reused rather than rebuilt), defaulting to the active view.
5. **Preview grid** — one row per target view: will-create filter / filter-of-this-name-already-exists-on-doc (offer reuse vs rename) / template-locked (view's `ViewTemplateId` controls its filter list — flagged, not silently skipped, the same posture `ToggleLinked.pushbutton` already takes for its own single-parameter template check).
6. **Apply** — one `Transaction`: `ParameterFilterElement.Create(doc, name, categoryIds, elementFilter)` once per new filter, then `View.AddFilter`/`SetFilterOverrides`/`SetFilterVisibility` per ticked target view, reporting created/reused/skipped counts the same way every other batch tool here reports its run.

**Implementation:**

- `Essential.panel`-style per-button files: `bundle.yaml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, own `todo-list.md` naming v1 scope (category + single-condition-grid filters only; no nested AND-of-ORs beyond the one flat `match_all` toggle the source tool itself already limits to) and the deferred items below.

**Future update:**
- Saved, named filter-rule templates exportable/importable as JSON across projects, so a firm's standard colour-coding (by Structural Material, by Phase, by Type Mark prefix) ships once and gets re-applied on a brand-new project instead of rebuilt by hand every time — the same "save the rule set, not just the one-off" step the already-logged Universal Renamer and Grid & Level Extent Sync ideas both end on.

For the much larger population of chajjas that were never drawn as a beam-bottom hatch at all — every hand-modelled building, every architect-added window after the structural drawing was issued, every project this toolkit's own owner has run through Revit without a cad2bim import — a modeler has no tool here (or, so far as the term "chajja" turns up in any Revit marketplace listing, on the market) and instead hand-sketches a flat `Floor` per opening, computing the soffit offset off the beam schedule by hand and redoing it by hand on every revision; this is a weather/drip-ledge convention specific to Indian and South Asian RCC construction, so the paid, English-market add-ins (Naviate, Ideate BIMLink, CTC's suite) that build out every other category this repo covers have never had a reason to build it either. The arithmetic to do this right already exists, measured and owner-approved on test14's 72 chajjas (36 following a dropped beam, 12 ties all resolved to the shallower 400 mm section) — it has simply never been pointed at a live model.

**Description:**
1. Modeler selects doors/windows directly, or picks a scope (a wall, a level, an elevation's worth of openings); each opening's head outline is built from its own bounding box and host wall face instead of a DXF hatch region.
2. For each opening, every `OST_StructuralFraming` beam whose geometry runs along that span is tested with the ported `_carrying_beam`/`_contact_run` shared-edge-length vote, generalized from "DXF ring vs `fold_plan`-built beam body" to "opening head ring vs a live beam's own location-line-derived body" — same rule, same SHALLOWER-soffit tie-break on a genuine two-beam span.
3. The identical offset formula applies, with `drop` now read as the difference between the beam's current and originally-modelled Z (or simply 0 for an untouched beam), so a beam a modeler has since moved by hand in Revit is picked up correctly with no legend or hatch involved anywhere.
4. A preview grid lists one row per opening — host beam id, shared contact length, soffit level, resulting ledge thickness/projection/offset, and a status drawn from the same vocabulary `chajja_slabs()`'s own notes already use ("touches no placed beam", "carries no thickness", "hangs off two beams... SHALLOWER soffit", "hangs off a dropped beam") — nothing ticked is silent, matching the house style every reinforcement tool in this repo already follows.
5. Apply places each ledge as a native `DB.Floor` through `builders/slabs.py`'s unmodified `_resolve_type`/`check_profile`/`_curve_loop` trio, but stamps the winning beam's `ElementId` and the computed offset onto two new parameters on the placed ledge, so a second run (or a future live hook) can find and re-level it instead of the DXF path's one-shot, never-revisited placement.

**Implementation:**
- New `anongee_toolkit/structural/chajja.py`: `carrying_beam(opening_ring, beams)` (ports `_carrying_beam`/`_contact_run`, `cad2bim/slab_stops.py:1151-1199`, off a live beam's tessellated location curve instead of a DXF `beam_segments` body); `ledge_offset_mm(thickness_mm, depth_mm, drop_mm)` (the same one-line formula, `:946`/`:956`, lifted verbatim rather than re-derived); `opening_head_ring(opening, projection_mm)` building the plan outline from the picked `FamilyInstance`'s bounding box and host `Wall` face in place of a DXF hatch region.
- Reuses `builders/slabs.py`'s `_resolve_type`/`check_profile`/`_curve_loop` placement trio exactly as it stands today — it already consumes any `{"ring","thickness_mm","offset_mm","part":"chajja"}` def regardless of where the def came from, so no new `Floor.Create` path is needed, only a new def source.
- `Essential.panel/StrucBIM.stack/Chajja Placer.pushbutton/` (beside `ConvertFloor.pushbutton`/`DrawFloor.pushbutton`, this toolkit's two other structural-floor builders): `script.py`, `ui.xaml` (opening picker, preview grid, apply), `bundle.yaml`, `icon.png`.
- Two new parameters (`BEAM_HOST_ID`, `LEDGE_OFFSET_MM`) provisioned the same one-off way every other shared parameter in this repo is bound today — the exact everyday gap the already-logged Parameter Pack Provisioner idea names — stamped onto each placed ledge so a later run can read them back.
- Tests: `tests/test_chajja.py` checks the ported `carrying_beam`/`ledge_offset_mm` against the exact numbers `slab_stops.py`'s own docstring already states for test14 (72 chajjas, 12 ties, every tie the same 200×400-dropped-75 vs 300×600-dropped-150 pair, soffits 475 vs 750, winner the 400), so the standalone port is checked against the same measured case the DXF original already proved itself against.

**Future update:**

## 2026-10-10 10:40 UTC

**Idea name:** Selection Set Composer — turns the multi-criteria element filter the toolkit already runs and throws away into a persisted, named, Boolean-composable `Autodesk.Revit.DB.SelectionSet` that survives after the window closes and feeds every other AnonGee batch tool.

**Potential:** `MultiFilterParameter.pushbutton/script.py` already builds a full rule engine — category/scope pickers (`_get_elements_by_categories`, script.py:256-280), AND/OR multi-row parameter conditions with text/numeric operators (`_evaluate_single_condition`, script.py:326-382), and a filter pass that narrows the live element pool to exactly the group a modeler wants (`_apply_filter`, script.py:488-528) — but the only thing done with that match list is a transient UI highlight: `_select_elements` (script.py:596-608) calls nothing but `uidoc.Selection.SetElementIds(ids)`, which Revit forgets the instant the selection changes or the tool is relaunched, and a repo-wide grep for `SelectionSet`/`NewSelectionSet` across `AnonGee.extension/lib` and `AnonGee.tab` returns zero hits — the toolkit has never once written a native, re-selectable Revit `SelectionSet` object; `OneFilterParameter.pushbutton` is the single-rule twin of the same gap. This differs from the already-logged **Filter → View Filter Generator**, which emits a `ParameterFilterElement` for live, Revit-re-evaluated per-view graphic overrides, not a static reusable `ElementId` bag usable for a schedule's "filter by selection," a tag-all, an isolate, or as the starting input for this toolkit's OWN other batch tools (Universal Renamer, Parameter Migrator, Cross-Element Parameter Copier each currently need either a hand pick or a one-shot throwaway `MultiFilterParameter` run every single time); it also differs from **Multi Filter Parameter — ElementId Write Support**, which teaches the same engine to write ElementId-typed parameter values rather than persist its match set, and from **Duplicate Instance Finder & Merger** / **Group Drift Auditor**, which are read-only report tools over ad hoc collector queries. Market check: the closest paid analog is Ideate Software's Ideate Explorer/BIMLink, which lets a user browse a parameter-filtered list and "Save as Selection Set" — but only as one flat list, with no Boolean composition across saved sets and no refresh-against-model-changes action; CTC BIM Logix's and Naviate's bulk-parameter tools likewise build one-shot work lists, not named, re-usable, algebra-capable sets. No free pyRevit extension offers rule-persisted selection sets with union/intersect/subtract composition, so this closes a real, uncovered day-to-day reselection tax for free, in-house.

**Description:**
1. Modeler opens Selection Set Composer and either starts from the current Revit pick or builds category + AND/OR parameter rows using the identical rule UI already shipped in `MultiFilterParameter.pushbutton`.
2. The tool previews the live match count and element list (reusing today's "Select" preview step) and adds a "Save as Selection Set" field where the modeler names the group (e.g. "L3 Shear Walls").
3. On save, the tool writes a real `Autodesk.Revit.DB.SelectionSet` inside a transaction, so the named group immediately appears in Revit's own Manage ▸ Selection dropdown — usable for Hide/Isolate, "filter by selection" in schedules, and tag-all, with zero re-picking.
4. Modeler picks two or more already-saved AnonGee sets (or a saved set plus a fresh rule run) and combines them with Union / Intersect / Subtract into a new named set, instead of manually re-selecting the overlap or remainder by hand.
5. A "Refresh" action re-runs a set's stored originating rule against the current model and unions any newly-matching elements (e.g. columns added on Level 3 since last save) back into the existing `SelectionSet`, keeping saved sets current as the Excel-driven Bridge pipeline keeps adding elements through the project's life.

**Implementation:**
- Factor `_evaluate_single_condition` (`MultiFilterParameter.pushbutton/script.py:326-382`) and `_apply_filter` (`:488-528`) out into `anongee_toolkit/revit/filtering.py` as shared `evaluate_rule`/`apply_rule_set` functions, so `MultiFilterParameter`, `OneFilterParameter`, and this new tool share one engine instead of a third copy-paste.
- New `anongee_toolkit/operations/selection_sets.py`: `save_selection_set(doc, name, element_ids)` wrapping `doc.Create.NewSelectionSet` + `SelectionSet.SetElementIds`, `list_selection_sets(doc)` via `FilteredElementCollector(doc).OfClass(SelectionSet)`, and `combine_sets(ids_a, ids_b, op)` for union/intersect/subtract.
- Persist each set's originating rule (categories, scope, rows, match_all) via `script.get_config()` keyed by the `SelectionSet` element's `UniqueId`, the same persistence pattern `JoinPriority.pushbutton`'s `cat_order` already uses, so "Refresh" can re-run it later without re-entering criteria.
- New `Advance.panel/FilterParameter.splitbutton/SelectionSetComposer.pushbutton/`: `script.py` reusing the existing modeless/`IExternalEventHandler`/`ExternalEvent` pattern verbatim from `MultiFilterParameter.pushbutton/script.py:174-213`, plus `ui.xaml`, `bundle.yaml`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `icon.png`.
- Tests: add `tests/test_selection_sets.py` with pure-Python unit tests for `combine_sets`' union/intersect/subtract logic (no live doc needed), and extend whatever fixture already exercises `filtering.py` to assert `apply_rule_set` returns the same ids `_evaluate_single_condition` produces today.

**Future update:**
- Pin saved sets to a quick-pick toolbar/dockable panel for one-click reselect without opening the composer at all.
- Teach Universal Renamer, Parameter Migrator, and Cross-Element Parameter Copier to accept "start from a saved AnonGee selection set" as an input source alongside "current selection," closing the loop the user's own batch-rename/parameter-mover workflows point at.

## 2026-10-12 00:43 UTC

**Idea name:** Duplicate Style Merger — finds fill patterns, line patterns and line-style subcategories that are visually/geometrically identical but differently named, remaps every element that uses the redundant copy onto the one kept, then deletes the redundant one cleanly

**Potential:** The three existing `Bulk Delete.pulldown` pushbuttons (`Delete FillPatterns`, `Delete LinePatterns`, `Delete LineStyles`) and their `Bulk Rename.pulldown` siblings only ever operate on an item's *name*; none of them look at an item's *definition*. `Delete FillPatterns.pushbutton/script.py:50-61` (`_collect_fillpatterns`) collects `(name, ElementId)` pairs only — it never reads `FillPatternElement.GetFillPattern()` (angle, spacing, grid lines), and the identical shape repeats for `_collect_linepatterns` (`:64-75`, never reads `LinePatternElement.GetLinePattern().GetSegments()`) and `_collect_linestyles` (`:78-90`, never reads the subcategory's `LineWeight`/`LineColor`/`GetLinePatternId()`). Because nothing ever compares definitions, a project that has been through repeated copy-paste between models, linked-model binds, or several rounds of CAD import (`cad2bim`'s own `builders/view_filters.py` and `classify/layers.py` create styles straight from CAD layer names, a well-known source of near-duplicates like "Hidden", "Hidden 2", "Hidden (IMPORT)" that render identically) accumulates dozens of redundant line styles, line patterns and fill patterns with no way to spot or consolidate them. The delete side makes the cost concrete: `_on_delete`'s loop (`script.py:268-277`) wraps every `doc.Delete(handle)` in a bare `try/except` and just counts it `skipped += 1 # system-locked / in-use` (`:277`, message at `:285-286`) — it never says *what* is using the item, so a modeler who wants to consolidate duplicates today has no way to find or clear that usage first; the delete just silently fails. This is a different mechanism from every adjacent logged idea: **Standards Diff & Selective Transfer** diffs these same three categories but *between two .rvt files*, never within one; **Bulk Purge** adds usage-*counts* for View Templates/Filters/Materials but explicitly keeps the three style categories' existing "list everything, try delete, skip failures" shape unchanged (its own write-up calls that shape "safe... for these categories" because a still-used pattern just fails to delete — it never proposes finding or merging duplicates); and **Duplicate Instance Finder & Merger** is scoped to coincident-location *model elements*, not type/style *definitions*. On the market, this is sold only inside paid whole-suite cleanup tools (Ideate Sidekick's "Model Health", CTC BIM Tools' Health Check) as a line item buried in a much larger per-seat bundle; no free pyRevit extension compares pattern/line-style *definitions* and remaps usage before deleting.

**Description:**
1. Modeler opens the existing `Delete FillPatterns` (or LinePatterns/LineStyles) pushbutton, now showing a "Find Duplicates" toggle alongside the current search box.
2. Toggling it groups the list by definition instead of name: patterns whose grid/segment/weight data match within tolerance are shown together, each group with one item pre-picked as "keep" (oldest `ElementId`, i.e. first created) and the rest pre-ticked as "merge into it."
3. For each ticked duplicate, the tool reports where it's used — materials' compound-structure layers and surface patterns for fill patterns, `GraphicsStyle.GetLinePatternId()`/`Subcategory.LinePatternId` and any `DetailCurve`/`ModelCurve`/dimension line-style assignment for line patterns and line styles — instead of the current blind try/delete.
4. Modeler reviews the usage list per group, adjusts which item is "keep" if needed, and clicks Merge.
5. One transaction remaps every found usage to the kept item's `ElementId`, then deletes the now-unused duplicates — succeeding cleanly instead of landing in the existing "skipped — locked/in-use" bucket — and reports "merged N duplicate(s) into M kept item(s), K usage(s) remapped."

**Implementation:** Extend the shared engine `anongee_toolkit/operations/bulk_delete.py` (and its three currently-inlined pushbutton copies, e.g. `Delete FillPatterns.pushbutton/script.py:50-90`) with a new `signature(doc, handle)` per provider in `_PROVIDERS` (`bulk_delete.py:64-83`) returning a comparable tuple of the pattern/line-style's own definition fields; a `group_duplicates(targets)` helper buckets items whose signatures match. Add `find_usages(doc, handle, kind)` to a new `anongee_toolkit/revit/graphic_styles.py` module, covering `Material.GetCompoundStructure().GetLayers()` + surface/cut pattern ids for fill patterns, and `GraphicsStyle`/`Subcategory.LinePatternId` plus a `DetailCurve`/`ModelCurve`/`Dimension` scan for line patterns/styles; a `remap_usage(doc, old_id, new_id, usages)` applies the swap inside the same `RevitTransaction` wrapper `bulk_delete.py` already imports (`revit/transactions.py`). Add tests under `AnonGee.extension/lib/py3/anongee_toolkit/tests/` (new `test_graphic_styles.py`) covering signature matching (identical vs. near-identical patterns) and the remap-then-delete path with a mocked/fake document.

**Future update:**
- Feed this engine's "keep one, remap the rest" primitive into **Bulk Purge**'s planned View Template/Filter/Material usage work, so a future "Full Model Purge" dashboard also surfaces duplicate *materials* with identical appearance assets, not just unused ones.
- Once **Standards Diff & Selective Transfer** ships its cross-document line-style/pattern diff, reuse this tool's new `signature()` functions as its per-item "identical vs. differs" comparator instead of a second implementation.
- Extend `find_usages()` to also catch Filled Region Types and View Filter overrides referencing a fill pattern, closing the one usage source (filter graphic overrides) v1 would otherwise miss.
